text:
Although the overall market has been weak lately and $LOAD has been consolidating around a $4M market cap, I still believe it is worth paying attention to.

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

What matters most right now is not how many more games Loadout can launch, but whether it can establish a new game financing model that allows developers to obtain ongoing funding through public trading markets while enabling the platform to capture value from that activity.

Recent updates have made me more confident in this direction, but the project still needs to prove that game launches and trading activity can translate into sustainable revenue rather than just short-lived hype around initial launches.

Traditional indie game studios often face a practical problem: they may already have a prototype or even an existing player base, but they still need funding for the next stage of development. Venture capital, publishers, and crowdfunding all have their own barriers, and the financing process can also affect developers' control over equity, intellectual property, and publishing arrangements. Loadout aims to offer an alternative by allowing studios to launch game tokens and receive development funding through trading fees generated in the public market, while continuing to release their games on traditional platforms such as Steam and consoles.

This was the original reason I became bullish on LOAD. It does not require every game to become a Web3 game. Instead, it attempts to bring crypto market liquidity into traditional game development. If this model works, Loadout's potential market would not be limited to development teams already operating in the blockchain ecosystem. It could extend to the broader indie gaming industry.

The project previously stated that the team had engaged with more than 500 games and built a curated launch pipeline of over 40 titles. The latest official page also showed 37 confirmed partner studios. However, games that have been contacted, projects in the pipeline, and confirmed partner studios represent different stages of progress. They should not be treated as equivalent levels of actual business activity. Still, for an early-stage financing platform, building a pipeline of developers is an important starting point. Without a continuous supply of new games, it will be difficult to maintain stable activity in the trading market.

What ultimately determines whether this model can work is how trading fees are distributed. Under the previously announced standard launch mechanism, the 5% fee charged on game token trades is split between 4% going to the game studio's treasury and 1% going to the Loadout protocol. For example, at $50,000 in daily trading volume, a studio could theoretically receive around $2,000 per day, or approximately $60,000 per month. This is not guaranteed revenue. The actual outcome depends on whether trading volume can be sustained, but it illustrates the core of the financing model: development funding does not have to rely entirely on one-time financing rounds. It can potentially be generated continuously through trading activity in a game's token.

The problem is that traders buying a game token does not necessarily mean they believe in the quality of the game itself. The market may become active around a launch, a new narrative, or a rewards mechanism, only to lose interest shortly afterward. Therefore, Loadout ultimately needs to prove that games can continue attracting players, trading activity can persist, and studios actually use the funding they receive to advance development. Otherwise, this model merely transfers the uncertainty of traditional financing into the trading market.

One of the most important recent product updates is the gradual establishment of two parallel launch models: curated launches and Instant Launch. The project announced that the graduation target has been adjusted to 150 SOL for curated launches and 85 SOL for Instant Launch. Curated launches continue to provide a degree of project screening, while Instant Launch aims to lower the barrier to entry for developers and allow more teams to bring their game tokens directly to market.

I believe this could be an important step toward expanding Loadout's project supply, but it also introduces new challenges. Lowering the launch barrier allows more small studios to participate, yet it may also attract projects without real products, teams lacking development capabilities, or participants interested only in short-term arbitrage. If the platform can increase the number of launches but cannot help traders distinguish which games are worth following, more projects will not necessarily mean more value.

That is why I am paying close attention to the recently introduced developer update feed for individual games. Each game can publish development updates, patch notes, announcements, and buyback records directly on its trading page, allowing traders to monitor progress in one place. This may not seem like a particularly complicated feature, but it could influence the entire financing model: when the market can continuously check a game's development progress, trading may gradually shift from chasing launch-day hype toward evaluating whether developers are delivering on their promises.

The referral mechanism provides another potential growth channel. Loadout stated that it already had nearly 3,800 accounts, with registered users having traded a cumulative 8,368 SOL, and that 1,656 users had joined through referrals. Referrers can receive 40% of the protocol fees generated by referred users, while those users receive a 20% fee rebate. This structure can encourage early users to bring more traders onto the platform and may reduce customer acquisition costs. However, referral-driven growth is not the same as organic retention. What matters next is whether these users continue trading after the rebates end and whether they remain engaged across multiple game launches.

The value-capture mechanism for LOAD is also becoming more concrete. The team recently reported that approximately 8.89 million LOAD tokens had been permanently burned, representing around 0.87%–0.89% of the total supply, with a cumulative buyback-and-burn value of approximately $47,500. The project also stated that anti-sniping fees would now be used for buybacks, emphasizing that every trade contributes to the LOAD buyback mechanism. These records are more meaningful than simply announcing plans to burn tokens in the future because they provide results that can be tracked and verified.

However, I would not equate trading volume in game tokens directly with value growth for LOAD. Trading fees received by studios are intended to fund game development, and individual games may also have their own buyback mechanisms. These should not be confused with revenue belonging to the Loadout protocol. What matters for LOAD is how much revenue the protocol actually receives, how much of it is used for buybacks and burns, and whether these mechanisms can operate at meaningful scale as multiple games continue running.

Recent partnership updates introduce another variable worth watching. Lo and Behold's SOUL was announced as allocating 25% of its trading fees to buybacks, with the possibility of allocating up to 10% of game revenue to buybacks as the game develops. The Last Worlds announced a different arrangement, allocating 20% of trading fees to buybacks and potentially using up to 20% of revenue for buybacks. These percentages belong to the respective games' tokenomics. They are not revenue directly allocated to LOAD.

I believe the significance of these arrangements is that studios may begin designing token economics around the ongoing activity of their games rather than focusing exclusively on trading hype at launch. If games continue releasing content and attracting players and traders, their token economies may become more closely connected to development progress. For Loadout, sustained trading activity across multiple operating games could eventually become a long-term source of platform revenue.

However, whether these mechanisms prove effective still depends on the games themselves. Buybacks can change a token's supply-demand dynamics, but they cannot replace actual game content. If a game quickly loses its players after launch, trading fees and buyback activity may decline at the same time. What matters for LOAD is not that every game announces a buyback, but that more games can generate ongoing development funding through sustained market activity.

Staking is another important potential catalyst. The project plans to introduce staking for LOAD, LOAD/SOL, and team-related arrangements. It also announced that 250,000,000 LOAD tokens had been locked for trading rewards, with vesting scheduled to begin on April 12, 2027, at 19:00 UTC. This allocation represents 25% of the total supply. The current lock restricts these tokens from entering circulation early, which may help reduce near-term reward-related selling pressure. However, locked tokens are not permanently burned. Once vesting begins, the actual release schedule and the behavior of reward recipients will still need to be monitored for potential selling pressure.

I am more interested in whether staking can give token holders a meaningful reason to participate over the long term, rather than simply introducing another source of rewards. If the platform's business grows and holders can derive clearer value from genuine product usage and protocol activity, staking could strengthen their willingness to hold. If rewards depend primarily on token distributions while protocol revenue fails to grow accordingly, staking may simply delay selling pressure rather than create new demand.

The recent audit delay also needs to be considered in this context. Kieran Warwick stated that the security audit was taking longer than expected, so the next curated launch was moved to October 27, 2026, at 19:00 UTC. The team also hopes to launch LOAD staking before then. The project explicitly emphasized that security takes priority over launching a few days earlier. In my view, a delay does not necessarily mean the fundamentals have weakened. For a platform involving funds, token trading, and buyback mechanisms, launching hastily before security issues are resolved could create much greater damage. However, it is still necessary to monitor whether the audit is completed, whether staking launches as planned, and whether the announced features operate reliably.

Overall, I believe LOAD's fundamentals have strengthened compared with its initial stage. It is no longer just a launchpad for game tokens. It is gradually building a more complete product ecosystem: curated launches and Instant Launch expand project supply, developer updates improve transparency, referrals help acquire users, and staking and buybacks attempt to connect platform activity with the native token. Meanwhile, games such as Lo and Behold and The Last Worlds are beginning to announce their own buyback arrangements, providing more examples through which the platform's gaming economy can be evaluated.

Still, I would treat LOAD as an early-stage investment thesis that has yet to be fully validated, rather than a protocol with established, stable cash flows. The biggest risk is that the number of launches, registered users, and trading volume all increase without generating sustained demand for the games themselves. Another risk is that lowering the barrier through Instant Launch leads to more low-quality projects, undermining traders' trust in the platform. The market has also previously experienced website outages, insufficient liquidity, and attempts to circumvent the anti-sniping mechanism. Token concentration and actual tradable liquidity also need to be examined further using on-chain addresses.

Going forward, I am most interested in three signals: whether new games launch on schedule and continue development, whether studios can obtain sustained funding through genuine trading activity, and whether Loadout's protocol revenue and buybacks and burns expand alongside business growth. These metrics will tell us far more than simply announcing more partnerships.

To sum up, I am bullish on LOAD because it is attempting to turn crypto market demand into a source of funding for traditional game development. If Loadout can ultimately help games secure ongoing development funding, enable developers to keep delivering products, and capture verifiable economic value from this activity, it could become an important layer connecting the gaming industry with public financial markets. Conversely, if trading activity only surges briefly during launches, then no amount of new games or buyback announcements will be enough to prove that this model can operate sustainably.

Although the first project did not perform well, I still believe $LOAD is worth paying attention to.

8sWe4GzK1YqG3vyzKHf8ZyB1WB5asofw2o6TqgFePtPo 

What is most worth studying is not whether it can rebound in the short term, but whether it can truly establish a functioning mechanism.

Game developers obtain development funding through token trading, Loadout captures value through platform fees, and mechanisms such as buybacks and burns then transmit platform growth to LOAD.

The reason to pay attention to LOAD is that it is not simply issuing game tokens. It is attempting to establish a new financing model for games.

Traditional indie game teams need to seek publishers, venture capital, or crowdfunding to finance their projects. What Loadout wants to do is allow game teams to issue their own tokens and use trading fees to fund game development while retaining their equity and intellectual property rights.

According to the official documentation, the initial launch mechanism charges a standard trading fee of 5% during the Bonding Curve phase, with 4% going to the game studio and 1% going to the Loadout protocol. The fee structure changes after a token graduates to the main trading pool.

If the number of launches expands, the platform could develop network effects. Over the past six months, the team received approximately 500 project launch applications. Most were of mediocre quality, but some were worth paying attention to. The team is also gradually reopening project submissions while continuing to manually review and approve launches.

This suggests that the project has at least begun addressing real demand from developers rather than remaining at the whitepaper stage. External reports also mentioned that the team had more than 40 curated games in its pipeline.

However, there is an important distinction: 500 applications do not mean 500 high-quality projects, and more than 40 games in the pipeline do not mean that more than 40 games have already launched successfully and are generating sustained trading activity.

In addition, LOAD has the potential to establish a clearer value-capture mechanism than ordinary Memes. The official website has a LOAD buyback page and states that trading activity across Loadout games will provide funding for LOAD buybacks, with burn records verifiable on-chain. Meanwhile, the official LOAD trading pool charges a 1.5% trading fee.

If more games are launched in the future, the official trading pools generate sustained volume, and protocol revenue is actually used for buybacks and burns, platform growth could translate into demand for the token.

This is where I see the greatest potential in LOAD: it would not need to rely on external hype every time, but could instead generate its own catalysts through its business operations. Currently, the cumulative buyback and burn total is 418.5 SOL, with 7.96 million LOAD permanently removed, equivalent to 0.80% of the total supply.

Next, Kieran’s explanation of the GOOSE launch incident reveals at least four important facts.

First, the anti-sniping mechanism did not completely prevent sniping.

GOOSE’s anti-sniping tax started at 99% and declined over the first 60 seconds, while the platform’s website also disabled the buy button. However, according to figures disclosed by Kieran himself, there were still 65 purchases from 40 wallets during the first minute, totaling 951 SOL.

This does not prove that all the wallets belonged to the same group of snipers, but it at least shows that disabling the website’s buy button did not completely prevent purchases through other trading routes.

Kieran also acknowledged that a similar mechanism had previously allowed snipers during the initial LOAD launch to pay high taxes to buy early and then exit at a profit by selling into community buying demand.

This exposes a design problem: a high tax can increase the cost of front-running, but it does not necessarily eliminate the behavior. If the expected profit is large enough, traders may still be willing to pay that cost.

Second, the platform has demonstrated its ability to raise funding for games, but the sources of revenue need to be distinguished.

Kieran stated that the anti-sniping tax generated more than 570 SOL in additional funding for Goose Byte, bringing the studio’s available funds to more than 730 SOL, or approximately $76,000.

If these figures are accurate, this at least demonstrates that Loadout’s trading fee mechanism can raise a substantial amount of funding for a game studio through a single launch event.

However, this should not be interpreted as LOAD having generated an equivalent amount of revenue. The funds were primarily intended for the Goose Byte game project. They are not revenue that LOAD holders can directly claim, and the fees generated by this exceptional launch should not be extrapolated directly into an estimate of the platform’s long-term revenue.

Third, the team is willing to acknowledge its mistakes, but the product is still undergoing rapid adjustments.

Kieran admitted that setting the graduation threshold at 1,000 SOL was a mistake and said in hindsight that 500 SOL might have been a more reasonable choice. The team subsequently lowered GOOSE’s threshold to 220 SOL and announced that GOOSE had graduated.

There is a positive aspect to this: the person in charge did not completely avoid the issue and was willing to explain the situation publicly and adjust the parameters.

On the other hand, launch taxes, graduation thresholds, trading routes, and liquidity management all need to withstand real-world financial conditions. The fact that problems have emerged and parameters have been revised quickly indicates that the platform’s mechanisms are not yet fully mature.

Fourth, a founder acknowledging a problem is more important than promising that it has already been solved.

In a newer post, the team stated that the website had reopened submissions for new projects and that the staking functionality was running locally.

However, Kieran also stated that the staking feature still needed to undergo an additional audit before it could be released.

Therefore, I interpret this as evidence that product development is progressing, rather than confirmation that staking is already officially live. The decision to conduct an additional audit is a positive sign, but actual deployment and verifiable operational records are still needed.

Taken together, this information suggests that Loadout is attempting to solve a real problem and has begun delivering a real product. However, it remains in an early trial-and-error stage, and its launch experience, liquidity, and mechanism fairness all require further validation.

However, the chart suggests that early speculative enthusiasm has already cooled considerably.

Therefore, further upside will require catalysts that can genuinely drive LOAD higher. I would focus on the following four areas for validation.

If staking passes the additional audit and is officially launched, allowing users to participate in practice with clearly defined reward rules, it could expand LOAD’s use cases and give users more reasons to hold the token. However, we still need to observe whether staking generates sustained demand rather than merely triggering a single wave of trading on launch day.

When the platform generates actual trading volume, whether the protocol earns revenue, how much of that revenue is used for buybacks, how much LOAD is purchased in each buyback, and whether the tokens are actually burned should all be verifiable through public records.

If these figures continue to accumulate, it would indicate that platform usage and token demand are beginning to establish a connection. Conversely, if trading volume is substantial but buyback data shows no meaningful change over an extended period, the token’s value-capture thesis would need to be reassessed.

The team needs to turn pending game applications into actual launches, then convert those launches into sustained trading activity, development funding, and subsequent game progress. In particular, given the problems that have already emerged during the GOOSE launch, whether future projects can operate more smoothly in terms of anti-sniping protection, liquidity, graduation mechanisms, and trading fairness will directly affect the trust of developers and traders.

My conclusion is that I will continue paying attention to LOAD, but at this stage, the focus should be on verifying whether it can evolve from a game launch platform with an idea, a team, and early demand into a product capable of generating sustained protocol revenue.

It currently has several positive factors: its game financing model offers some differentiation, the team is already working on real projects, the person in charge is willing to publicly explain launch-related problems, and staking, buybacks, and additional game launches provide catalysts to monitor going forward.

However, the token has already experienced a substantial retracement, liquidity remains limited, the distribution of early holdings still needs further investigation, and the most important staking and buyback mechanisms still need to prove themselves through actual operating results.

Therefore, my strategy would be: the project is worth continuing to track, but I would wait for confirmation before making a decision on the token.

To me, the most convincing signals in the next stage would not be another post from Kieran about the platform’s vision, but the official launch of staking, sustained buybacks and burns, a growing number of completed game launches, and actual revenue generated by trading activity on the official pools.

If these developments gradually materialize, LOAD’s investment thesis could shift from “betting that a new platform might succeed” toward “existing data beginning to demonstrate that the platform’s business model works.”

Conversely, if games continue launching without meaningful trading depth, or if the platform generates trading activity but fails to establish effective value capture for the token, LOAD could remain stuck in the early-stage narrative premium phase for a long time, even if the team continues to be highly active.

LAUNCH is a "fairer launch tool" on StonkFun. It's not an entirely new independent chain or platform, but rather an improvement to the existing StonkFun token launch process, making launches fairer and more favorable to traders rather than developers. Launching itself is free.

This project addresses three major pain points that the community has long criticized about Pumpfun:

Block 0 bundling: Developers use multiple wallets to make large buys in the first block after creation, putting ordinary traders at a disadvantage. LAUNCH uses a single main wallet to uniformly create all coins, with no separate "developer wallet buy." Creation transactions go through private bundling, so theoretically no one can front-run in block 0.

PvP and copycat wars: As soon as a narrative gets hot, a bunch of copycat coins instantly appear to grab liquidity. LAUNCH restricts duplicate tickers, similar names and images, and limits one X account to launching only one coin, among other measures.

Developer fee extraction: Previously developers could take trading fees. LAUNCH automatically uses the developer share to buy back and burn the corresponding token, with fees flowing back to the coin itself and its holders rather than into the developer's pocket.

Traditional Pumpfun is more like an unregulated OTC casino: devs can buy heavily in advance and withdraw fees at any time. LAUNCH is more like a rules-based public auction: creators can't front-run, and fees generated from trading automatically buy back and burn "shares," benefiting subsequent holders. Success depends more on community trading heat rather than developers positioning early.

Token utility: The LAUNCH token itself follows the same mechanism: 100% of creator fees are used to buy back and burn LAUNCH. Holding and trading it is essentially supporting this "fairer launch" narrative. Each individual coin on the platform also has its own buyback and burn flywheel.

Current project status: About 600+ coins have launched, 130 coins are undergoing buybacks and burns, and approximately 44.5 SOL in fees has been used for buybacks cumulatively.

So in summary: it attempts to turn "a token launch game where developers take advantage" into a version where "traders have the edge and fees flow back to the coin itself." That's its core selling point right now.

text:
$MSFT 裁員、市場不敢再借錢給Neocloud和AI初創，令我重新思考了自己的投資邏輯。

市場現在青睞軟件，憧憬的是軟件不會被取代，反而因為AI agent的落地，透過軟件公司的分發渠道，令AI應用發光發亮。

我同意，但我不認為純軟件公司是最好的投資。我更偏好算力能夠自給自足的軟件公司，簡單點來說就是Mag 7𥚃的SaaS。

無論你的軟件或AI agent再出色，背後都需要算力提供服務。如果一間軟件公司的profit margin超高，背後的算力供應商完全可以提價，蠶食你一部份的margin。

這就好像租房子的，永遠是為業主在打工一樣。

如果狼性再高一點，Mag 7不僅可以透過算力加價去吸血，而是直接複製並取代你。以往大家都比較克制，各做各的。不完全是因為道德的考慮，而是成本和邊際回報的考量。所以總有些蛋糕會留在枱上給小弟吃。

但現在agent年代，微軟宣布自願離職計劃，代表在同一個生產力上， AI的成本已經比人力低。這些公司去做本業以外的業務成本下降，令他們更有誘因去吃掉一些SaaS。現存的軟件公司，剩下來的價值好像只有歷史遺留下來的分發渠道。因為人性的懶惰和使用慣性，會令客戶依賴已存路徑，但只要提供足夠的經濟誘因。這種慣性並非牢不可破。

Elon Musk為什麼嘴砲Neocloud？一來我相信他是在說實話，很多新雲的管理和執行其實很差；二來，誰能掌握算力，誰就能掌握未來的世界。Neocloud死得越快，這些超大型運公司就越有利。

再向下一層推想，硬件公司的margin也會逐漸下降。現在大企業爭先要建立算力，因為客戶之間有競爭，硬件公司才有定價權。但以後如果形成三國鼎立，硬件的定價權，反而會落在Mag7上。就如同AI浪潮前的記憶體公司，需求幾乎完全來自Apple和Android，所以被瘋狂壓價。

我遇見的未來是強者越強，世界的經濟命運，可能最後只落在幾間超大型企業裏。

這樣一想，投資好像更簡單了。我以上的邏輯，有沒有什麼盲點呢？歡迎交流一下。

text:
I've enjoyed Jake's coverage on Pearl. Even though I am bullish I think his criticisms are fair, I also think we have more common ground than it appears. Specifically:

-Pearl's emission schedule is the number 1 bear case. A key aspect of a SOV asset is that price goes up, which is harder if you have indiscriminate sellers.

-Concerns around transparency are also valid. Without a "fundamental" business / revenue line, narrative is the main driver of price. An absence of clear communication leads to uncertainty and doubt, which is detrimental to an asset that derives its value from social consensus.

However, on the actual nature of the raise I disagree that it's bearish or leads to a conflict of interest:

To me, token-equity concerns arise for revenue generating protocols, where value accrual is unclear as it is either diluted or completely given to equity holders that act as a senior tranche, with token holders suffering.

Pearl Labs' equity raise causes no conflict of interest since the distinction is clear: Pearl is a SOV asset, while Pearl Labs is an AI infrastructure company that develops Pearl's proof-of-useful-work technology and commercializes inference services. Pearl Labs' success is accretive to the Pearl ecosystem but never extractive, since Pearl is not intended to accrue revenue. If anything the equity raise means 1) Pearl Labs is not reliant on selling PRL to fund operations, 2) it signifies there are powerful forces behind the success of PRL and 3) the raise will add hashrate to the PRL network.

Very strongly disagree that Pearl Labs should introduce PRL buybacks. It would be the quickest way to add a token/equity conflict, as it immediately creates the question of how much value accrues to Pearl Labs vs the token. It also instantly reframes Pearl from an asset trading at 1/30th of ZEC's valuation to an overvalued 1000x P/S token. This is the counterintuitive thing about SOV assets: Flows >>> buybacks, even for huge revenue generating projects like HYPE (although buybacks matter a lot for narrative). Removing a business and letting an asset trade purely as an expression of an idea (e.g. AI BTC) removes company specific and execution risk, stops anchoring the token to a business that needs to grow in line with the price, and also removes its ceiling.

The second controversial point is around centralization and the team mining 5% for themselves. Controversially, I think centralization matters less than people think, even for SOVs. Take MicroStrategy / Bitmine as examples. What matters is centralization among team/VCs who are going to sell. If the team mining a significant amount of tokens means those tokens are effectively out of circulation, I view this as bullish rather than bearish. Of course, this only holds true as long as they don't sell.

Lastly I think it's important to contextualize that a lot of my bullishness comes from a regret minimization framework. Pearl is a nascent SOV, and the concerns around emissions / transparency are very valid. However, it is also one of the most exciting narratives. Just like there is a future where Pearl is insta dumped by institutions that mine it at a low cost basis, there is a future where powerful BTC miners and connected entities rally behind PRL as a new way to monetize their compute through inference, while hashrate increases and fears continue to grow around BTC's security budget.

Thats why, while I see the same risks as Jake, I think that potential of exponential upside does justify a small position, even if just as a hedge to existing BTC/ZEC holdings.

quoted_text:
not officially confirmed, but @TheMarker, israel's main business paper, is reporting that @prlnet's lab raised $130M from lightspeed, ribbit capital, and square peg.

$55M in equity and $75M for a fund to build out GPU infrastructure.

ribbit and lightspeed are also named as pearl backers on its profile in greenfield partners' disruptors 60 list.

if this is real, the $PEARL bear case gets a lot worse. here's why:

1) $PEARL traded on a "no VCs, fair launch" story.

pearl's code doesn't allocate tokens to founders or investors, and that part is probably still true. but the lab behind pearl is reportedly VC-backed, and nobody corrected the narrative while it pumped.

2) the value goes to the equity, not the token.

the lab sells inference and gets paid in USD, and the VCs own the lab. $PEARL holders don't get any of that revenue, just diluted by new supply.

so the investors can do well even if $PEARL goes to zero.

3) it goes against the "sovereignless bitcoin" pitch.

part of bitcoin's monetary premium is that no company controls it. pearl's upgrades are drafted by a VC-backed lab, including the FP8 fork that would tie mining more closely to inference, the same business the lab sells.

4) the $75M GPU fund.

we don't know if those GPUs mine $PEARL. if they do, the company is collecting a share of ~85% supply growth this year, on top of whatever insiders mined early.

remember that about 1/3 of today's supply was mined in the first 6 days.

5) zcash had investors too (20% of its early block rewards went to founders and investors) but that was public from day 1. everyone knew who got paid and how much.

pearl hasn't disclosed any of that.

holders deserve to know:

> who invested
> whether any investors or insiders hold $PEARL
> whether the GPU fund mines $PEARL

a fair launch shouldn't need a newspaper to tell you who's behind it.

i was a $PEARL bear on friday. i'm a bigger one now.

quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

quoted_text:
BNB 链又要搞一条新L1

在BNB Chain的官方文档在10月22日更新了New L1计划。

🚀不是简单给BSC升级，而是准备重新设计一条全新的高性能L1。在文档里没有标注新链名称，标注为TBD（待定）。

看了下，几个关键信息：

1、再造一条新L1，不是替代BSC。

现有 BSC继续运营，新L1与BSC 并存，通过原生跨链桥连接。
BSC继续承载现有庞大的DeFi和应用生态，新L1则专门服务那些对交易速度、延迟和性能要求更高的业务。

2、不发新币，继续使用BNB。

新L1不会发行独立代币，继续使用BNB作为Gas、质押和治理的核心资产。这么看是做增量，如果新L1能承载更多交易、支付和泛金融业务，其实对BNB的需求也是更大的。BNB现在价格743，这下子又有预期了。

3、交易性能是重点

200毫秒出块，约20毫秒交易预确认，亚秒级交易排序等。明显是冲着高频交易、链上订单簿、支付等场景去的。
这两年Hyperliquid、Lighter、Aster等交易平台的发展，也让大家看到交易基础设施的重要性。

4、上线时间。

文档里说已经运行内部多验证者开发网，但还没有公开测试网或主网，计划2026年底推出测试网，2027年初推出主网。（握草，这不马上就快来了么？）

5、为什么要搞新链
大家对BSC的印象，更多是手续费便宜、用户多、Meme活跃，背靠币安生态。这次重新做一条L1，释放了一个很明确的信号：BNB Chain不满足于只做通用公链，而是要进一步争夺高性能链上金融基础设施的市场。

很大一部分原因丰密我觉得应该是Perp dex带来的压力与未来的潜力， 以前大家觉得链上交易只是中心化交易所的补充，现在越来越多的交易需求转向链上，最近一段时间链上Perp的日交易量合计都接近币安合约的1/3，虽然有积分激励等因素，但这个趋势是不容忽视的。

对于我们普通用户：
值得关注的是新L1开放测试网后，除了重点关注哪些新协议、新玩法和早期生态机会，
还有哪些是可以重点👀的！

@BNBCHAIN @binancezh

text:
抗量子赛道项目介绍：Mochimo

这也是一条 2018 年就上线的老公链，用的是哈希签名。它 10 月 11 日从 PoW 转成了 PoS，区块奖励已经归零，所以现在没有挖矿门槛。

🔹技术概述
（1）Mochimo 用 WOTS+ 一次性哈希签名（它也是 SLH-DSA 的组成部分），每花一次就自动换新密钥，找零转进新地址。官方的 Chrome 扩展钱包（会自动管理一次性密钥）持有和转账。

（2）为了能反复收款，它用一个 20 字节的固定账户号（Tag）来解决一次性签名不能重复使用的问题。

（3）签名槽位还给 ML-DSA、SLH-DSA、FN-DSA 留了位置，以后可以升级。

🔹现状
（1）2018-06-25 主网上线，没有 ICO，预挖 6.34%。

（2）2026-10-11 从 PoW 转为 PoS，60 秒一块，区块奖励归零，不再增发。

（3） $MCM 现价约 0.10U/币，流通约 1,678 万枚，市值约 $168 万；FDV 约 $256 万（按总量约 2,561 万枚算）。CoinGecko 上

🔹参与方式

（1）转PoS了，但是质押规则没有，所以只有二级市场参与的方式了：目前只有 Biconomy 一家交易所，24 小时成交约 $5,200

🔹风险
（1）PoS 节点没有开源，验证者名单不公开，链上也不记录出块者，去中心化程度看不清。

（2）区块奖励归零后，验证者靠什么获得激励还没说清楚。

（3）只有一家交易所，流动性很薄。各方给出的供应量数据也不一致。

相对于@QRLedger，这也是从第一天起就抗量子的老链，为什么市场至今只给它不到 200 万美元的估值？

text:
Formal verification will likely play an increasingly important role for the "Antifragile Internet".

I personally played around with FV (Lean4) for research in Spr 25. Back then it was a pain to work with, and the leading models (Deepseek/4o) couldn't handle it well. A few things have changed:

(1) The models have gotten really good at FV languages. Lean4 is now the de facto way AI-driven math breakthroughs get done, and the same skills carry over to code.

(2) There's a lot more end-to-end automation. In the @theoremlabs x @AnthropicAI collab, existing fuzz tests are automatically turned into specs, and Claude proves them directly on the compiled RISC-V binary (in Rocq). 239 entry points across 123 open-source libraries, in a few weeks.

(3) The recent security incidents make "verifiable code" much more top-of-mind. FV is finally getting the funding and attention it deserves, rather than being a (historically backwater) area of academia.

So this is an exciting time for FV-in-code, esp for companies like @theoremlabs building towards verifiable code. But FV is not a panacea where anything verified is "unhackable". 3 caveats:

(1) FV is often retroactive and partial - Much of this is proving properties about existing code after the fact, and only for the paths the tests reach, not the whole library or how other code calls it.

(2) FV has simplified sandboxes - the proofs assume a simple setup (eg. single-threaded, statically linked, RISC-V), and there's still a gap between that and the code actually running in prod.

(3) You have to define the properties properly - notions like "secure" or "safe" or "correct" have to be pinned down mathematically, eg. via test suites, rather than staying high level. When you say something is "safe", what you're really saying is that nothing bad happens for any input in scope.
author: 0xfishylosopher
quoted_text:
New on our Frontier Red Team blog: using Claude to formally verify software at large scale.

Formal verification can prove that code is free of certain bugs, but historically it has only been feasible for small codebases (or required a lot of expert time).

With AI models, however, this is beginning to change. In collaboration with @theoremlabs, we used Claude to prove security properties in over one hundred real-world open-source libraries over the span of a few weeks.

Read our research in full here: https://t.co/zUyx8CjBEk

text: I’ve spent years training AI models, but agentic RL has not been my main focus. As agentic RL and post-training evolve, I’ve found it hard to find a systematic explanation that connects the theory, code, and practical decisions. As a result, I spent two weeks built https://t.co/HhadTawoby for anyone who already trained language models and want to understand how to train agents. It breaks down RL from first principles while keeping the broader post-training workflow in view, including SFT, preference learning, and on-policy distillation. I created it together with GPT-6 to work through the subject carefully and share what I learn along the way.

text:
Zcash Co-Founder Proposes Redirecting 8% of Block Subsidies to Network Sustainability Mechanism

Zcash co-founder and protocol developer Sean Bowe has submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) to end the 8% block subsidy allocation to Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) and redirect it to the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), withholding the funds from immediate circulation.

The proposal argues that ZCG's existing reserves are sufficient to sustain its grant-making activities. It would leave ZCG's existing treasury, the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund allocation, miners' subsidy share, and ZEC's maximum supply unchanged.

quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
Yes, it seems indeed the models even obtained the results on the same day. I haven't had a chance to look through the OAI claimed proof yet, but in the spirit of the AGMAI recommendations to improve exposition before release, some of us did read Claude's proof last week before release to try to incorporate a better quality high level overview and exposition overall, which I hope is reflected in the pdf (published via the AI repository Hexagon, see https://t.co/I2WEx1lgdV; lean available at https://t.co/OWODuKYNcR; also see the google drive shared via @rrwilliams's post https://t.co/xURWq1RyuO in preparation for the upcoming workshops he's organizing with Impagliazzo and Paturi).

Sharing what I understood from the proof below:

Basic idea (below is for runtime 2^{delta n} for arbitrary constant delta>0; it seems both proofs ultimately get roughly exp(O(n / sqrt(log n))) time with lower order terms in the exponent),

* can assume num clauses = O(n) wlog via previous sparsification results (n = num variables)

* Solve #3-SAT not 3-SAT (i.e. count satisfying assignments, don't just decide satisfiability)

* Convert to graph problem: clauses are nodes, and edges between clauses that share a variable (whether it's x or not(x) doesn't matter; we care about same variable, not same literal). Weight of an edge is # of shared variables. 

* Divide and Conquer idea: if there's a cut with total weight W, you can iterate over all 2^W fixings of those shared variables, and for each fixing you recurse on both sides and multiply, then add it up. Base case is constant # vertices, then you can just brute force count in 2^O(1) time. Unfortunately, you're not going to always find such a cut.

(aside: from now on you can imagine every occurrence of a literal gets its own variable, and edges are functions enforcing equality constraints between those copies)

* Instead of the above D&C, group the vertices into g^2 groups for some large constant g = g(delta). It matters how to do this grouping (it's not arbitrary); without getting into the details (see paper), a random grouping has properties the D&C wants (probabilistic method), and this existence is enough to allow for a slow-but-fast-enough algorithm to find a good grouping deterministically.

* Imagine laying out the g^2 vertices arbitrarily on a g x g grid. Some edges are "side edges" (purely horizontal or purely vertical) and some are "diagonal" (the rest). There are (g choose 2)^2 = Theta(g^4) diagonal ones (choose two rows and two columns to define the corners) but only 2*g*(g choose 2) = O(g^3) side edges. You can pick g a large enough constant that the side edges have much less total weight than the diagonals -- the D&C will save on the diagonals, so we want there to be many more of them.

* The sum we want is

sum_z prod_{vertices a} W_a(z_a) * prod_{edges a,b} P(z_a,z_b),

where W_a(z_a) at the highest level of recursion is a table of 2^3=8 values for each of the settings of the 3 literals in clause a, with value 0 or 1 indicating whether z_a satisfies clause a or not, and P() is the equality constraint checker I mentioned on the edges (deeper levels of recursion also all involve sums of this form where P() is always an equality checker on some set of bits, but deeper W's have arbitrary integer outputs and not necessarily 0/1)

Write prod_{edges} P(..) = prod_{side edges} P(..) prod_{rectangles r} P_1(..) P_2(..) where P_1, P_2 are the diagonals for the rectangle r

*The key step* (eqn 15 in the pdf): first assume all edges in the entire graph have exactly 3 bits on them (it turns out reducing to this isn't *too* complicated; see (19)), and replace P_1*P_2 with a hyperedge that involves some function on the corners of the rectangle, times a sum of two products of edge functions. This replacement comes from something called the "eight square identity"; this is related to octonions, which I still know nothing about. :) So

P_1*P_2 = HyperEdgeFunction(corners)*(Q_1*Q_2 + Q_3*Q_4)

Two interesting things here: (1) Q_1,Q_2,Q_3,Q_4 are all side edges (Q_1,Q_2 are horizontal and Q_3,Q_4 are vertical), and (2) whereas P1,P2 have total weight 6 (3 and 3), if you merge each row of the grid into a supervertex then Q_1,Q_2 vanishes and the hyperedge becomes a regular edge with total weight 3 whereas hyperedge*Q_3*Q_4 still involves 6 bits (and vice versa if you merge each column into a supervertex). In particular, the average weight from using Q_1*Q_2 vs. Q_3*Q_4 is (3+6)/2 = 4.5. We went from weight 6 (P_1*P_2) to weight 4.5 "on average".

* So back to the original sum, we can rewrite it:

sum_a W_a(z_a) * prod_{side edges} P(..) * prod_{rectangles r} hyperedge(r) * (Q_1*Q_2 + Q_3*Q_4)

Now imagine distributing that product over that final sum involving the Q's, to get a new sum that has a factor 2^{# rectangles} more terms multiplicatively. (but there are only poly(g) = O(1) rectangles, so this is only a 2^{poly(g)} = O(1) blowup in the number of summands)

* Each one of these terms in the new, bigger sum, has a prod_rectangles in it. Either >=1/2 of the rectangles chose the Q_1*Q_2 when we distributed the product, or >=1/2 chose the Q_3*Q_4. That means we can either merge all row edges or merge all column edges, and one of those wil decrease the total number of weights on edges by a 4.5/6 factor. This is the heart of why D&C makes progress; D&C is supposed to reduce one instance to simpler instances, and "simpler" in this case means decreasing the total weight on all edges (here by a 4.5/6 factor).

This overall looks like a recursion with branching factor 2^{poly(g)} = O(1), but in reality the branching factor becomes poly(m) when you account for the trick in the proof to reduce to the case of 3 bits on each edge. In any case, there are more steps to get everything to work, but the above gives some taste of how the Divide & Conquer works.

If you optimize the right way to choose g to not be a constant but a slow enough growing function, you get runtime exp(O(n / log^c n)), but for a tiny c. If you replace the eight square identity with something fancier, and replace the black-box invocation of the sparsification lemma with a more white box version that adds in some more ideas, you get down to the exp(O(n loglog n / sqrt(log n))) in the paper.

quoted_text:
Folks,

I left Microsoft three months ago to start my own company. Two weeks after I left, my whole team in Australia was let go.

I see the hurt it’s causing my ex-colleagues, their families and their kids. Layoffs, forced relocations, PIPs. It’s brutal and I don’t want to brush past that.

But here’s my honest take.

Microsoft needs fewer people.

I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.

Here’s a real example.

The Entra team shipped managed identities back in 2017. No more secrets in code. A clear security win.

Then they tried to get the rest of Microsoft to adopt it. Very few teams did, and the ones that did moved at a snail’s pace. Every org had its own priorities and its own decision makers.

It took Microsoft getting hacked, and the Secure Future Initiative that followed, before things really moved.

Today almost every Microsoft app and service supports managed identity.

Six years, and a major breach, to get there.

In a world with agents and fewer people, that rollout would be possible across Microsoft in months, not years.

Microsoft already has everything else. The customers. The infrastructure. The scale.

What it needs is fewer people, leaning hard into agentic work.

Right now OpenAI and Anthropic are shipping at a pace Microsoft can’t match.

Microsoft has to change to survive.

quoted_text:
昨天小群里聊起如何在预测上能提高胜率，好多人都说起bagel 

尤其是跟单功能，榜单上有些人胜率80%以上，不是玩短线预测纯赌的方式，大部分都是玩体育和电竞

关于跟单功能总结了下大家分享的几个点，感兴趣的可以参考看看

@bagel_win是一款移动优先的预测市场 App，直接接入 Polymarket 的市场与流动性，不自建撮合池。

跟单功能用好了非常香，如果别人跟你的单，你还能分到对方订单手续费的 10%。

如何找到值得跟的人👇
跟单的起点通常是这几个地方：
-个人主页上的胜率与交易量
-每个盘口的主要持仓者（Top Holders）
-排行榜
-Bagel 给特定领域表现突出的交易员打的标签

想看英雄联盟，先找电竞领域标签的人，再看他具体做过哪些判断；换成足球，成绩一定单独看。不同赛道的优势很难通用。主页数据只是起点，更关键的是弄清楚他在哪类盘口赚钱，以及当时是以什么价格买进去的。

预测市场里，高胜率也可能是亏钱的成绩单。同样 80% 的胜率，还是要看买入的价格。胜率相同，盈亏完全取决于入场价格。

跟单的价差陷阱
这是大家最容易忽略的，比如对方以0.4 u买入，你看到后以0.6 u跟进，最终都押对了：
对方每份利润约 0.6 u
你每份利润只剩 0.4 u

方向相同，但是到手利润就少了很多。再加上手续费，实际差距会更大。找到人之后，还得判断这个价格值不值得跟。

实际操作机制
关注之后，对方的仓位会进入你的 Feed；下单时（包括 Combo 串关）会收到实时推送，可以一键跟单，自己设定金额。也可以用挂限价单。

如果要跟单一定注意下面的几个点
1.不是自动镜像：目前是可见仓位的一键复制，不是持续自动跟随、自动调仓或带止损的完整 copy trading。

2.历史战绩平台不核实，风险自担。别人的胜率不是你的胜率。

3.领域要匹配：电竞标签的人未必擅长足球，研究后再去跟

4.价格比方向更重要：入场价决定期望值。

5.小额单费用偏高：低于 5 美元的市价单有 0.05 美元固定费用，实际费率很高。

跟单功能确实能帮我们更快发现谁在盯什么市场、降低部分研究成本，但是它解决不了这个人在什么价格、什么领域真的有优势，以及现在这个价格还值不值得跟的问题。

所以，用这个功能还是要慎重的。

玩预测不擅长一定慎重玩，不然和赌真没区别，本文仅参与项目记录，不做投资建议，DYOR~

text:
Uncle Bob 给 Agent 的精简纪律 Skills：先跑通，再做对，再养成习惯

Clean Code 作者 @unclebobmartin 开源的 Skills「ub-mode」，把经典 Clean Code / TDD 纪律沉淀为三段给 coding agent 用：先让它 work，再用 CRAP / 重复 / 变异测试做对，最后用日志、小提交和上下文卫生收尾；原则来自人，门槛尽量可机器量。

开源地址：https://t.co/z9kNNIX9Vm

# 三段流程（每次改动都走）

1. First Make it Work
懒惰协议（一处决策、最小改动）、先定数据形状、先写会失败的测试、从第一性原理重设计而不是往旧设计上打补丁、两个同前提的修法都撞同一道闸时先质疑前提、先减再加、瞄准可验收的终态、难活先做「杠杆」工具。架构侧：领域结构让非法状态不可表示、边界校验、类型不闭嘴、幂等、共享可变状态先拆开。

2. Then Make it Right
修根因而不是挡崩溃；工作切成可验收的小单元；测行为不测实现。然后上工具闸门：
· crapper：圈复杂度 + 覆盖 → CRAP < 10
· dryer：结构重复 ≥ 0.8 要消
· mutator：补未覆盖、杀幸存变异体、删死代码
· 重构：先钉住行为 → 改结构 → 证明行为未变
（另有 uml-viewer 看组件、覆盖、CRAP、变异分与依赖方向。）

3. Practice
行动+理由记日志并在结束时汇报；主线程上下文要小；worktree 清理；小而有序的 commit（写清为什么、改了什么、怎么证明），最后再推主线。

quoted_text:
OpenAI 称 AI 推翻计算机科学的“指数时间假设”，还证出杨-米尔斯理论存在，外部专家组开始核查

OpenAI 10 月 26 日宣布，内部模型在数学、计算机、物理上各拿出一项成果，其中两项碰的是几十年的难题。这些都还是 OpenAI 的说法，没经过同行评审，截至发稿也没有参与核查的专家公开评价结论对错。

【计算机：一条被当作地基的假设】

“可满足性问题”是这样一类题：给你一堆“A 和 B 至少一个为真”之类的条件，问能不能让它们同时成立。每多一个变量，要试的组合就翻一倍。

1999 年 Russell Impagliazzo 和 Ramamohan Paturi 提出“指数时间假设”（ETH）：这类题没有本质上更快的解法，耗时注定翻倍式增长。几百篇论文拿它当前提，论证很多问题“快不了”。

OpenAI 公开的论文给出一个新算法，依然很慢，但耗时增长得比 ETH 断言的慢，这就足以推翻它。它没有证明“所有难题都有快速解法”（P=NP），OpenAI 也说变成实际提速还要大量研究。

OpenAI 说证明已用 Lean 检查过。Lean 是一种证明检查程序，把证明拆成最小步骤逐条核对，错一步就不通过。论文和 Lean 代码都在 GitHub 上，任何人能复核。核查小组由 Impagliazzo、Paturi 和 MIT 的 Ryan Williams 牵头。

【物理：千禧年难题的一半】

量子色动力学（QCD）描述夸克和胶子怎样靠“强力”粘成原子核，计算和实验对得上，但没人用数学严格证明过它能成立。它的简化版“杨-米尔斯理论”是克雷数学研究所悬赏 100 万美元的千禧年难题。

OpenAI 称模型 9 月写出了两者存在的证明，10 月中旬完成 Lean 检查。不过这道千禧年难题要证两件事：理论存在，以及最轻的粒子也有质量（“质量间隙”）。OpenAI 只说做了前一件。

物理材料暂不公开，由诺贝尔奖得主 David Gross 带队的专家组先自己写成论文，外界目前没法检查。

【数学：Kakeya 猜想推到所有维度】

Kakeya 问题问的是：一个图形要能放下指向每个方向的单位线段，最少多大。面积能小到接近零，但数学家猜它在“维度”上总是满的。2025 年王虹和 Joshua Zahl 证了三维。OpenAI 称模型证明了一个更强的猜想，顺带拿下所有维度，论文和 Lean 证明已直接公开。

【为什么换了发布方式】

9 月 OpenAI 宣布解决纳维-斯托克斯千禧年难题，有数学家说撞上自己未公开的研究，引发署名之争；10 月 6 日它一口气发了 722 篇 AI 论文，次日因错误撤回 3 篇。这次改请外部专家牵头：不签保密协议，OpenAI 不要学术署名，专家无偿独立参与。

quoted_text:
From what I've seen and read, Cohere and the authors should be ashamed of themselves for pushing this narrative. Releasing the logs doesn't help them win back trust.

The narrative doesn't match the facts, and the delivery doesn't match the severity. This is corpo marketing slop with little regard for the downstream impact, especially given where things are heading and the climate we're in today. 

I think they realized after posting it that it had gone too viral. They tried to downplay it on their personal accounts, saying the model didn't intend any harm, but the damage was already done. The article's framing, strong wording, and overall insinuation make their personal statements seem almost contradictory to what the article implies.

Claims this consequential deserve evidence that people can inspect and reproduce. I'm glad they at least have the decency to release their traces. 

To be clear, if they hadn't presented the incident this way, this would be a really interesting case study. It could highlight the importance of sandboxes and help us understand model behavior in these edge cases. But they choose fearmongering.

One thing I was interested to see if the same thing happen with other models, not just Qwen 3.8 Flash. I put the results on a simple website you can quickly scan here: https://t.co/HpkL5ayJSM. I have some interesting findings outside Qwen 3.8 that I'll share later in the post.

Coming back to the Cohere article, what's really bad about the it is that the narrative it paints are very different from the reality. 

These three in my opinion are the worst.

1. The impression: a Chinese model collected machine information and sent it to Chinese servers.

"Qwen3.8-Flash-Next ignored instructions and inventoried the machine it was running on and then tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing."

The insinuation falls apart when you look at the actual upload body: the fixed test string PROBE_PAYLOAD_ABC123. The machine information wasn't even included in that "probe file."

You look deeper, and you realize the task was a cybersecurity task about detecting downloads into /tmp. The supposedly alarming inventory consisted of listing /tmp, checking which curl binaries were installed, and reading the DNS configuration.

Lastly, you realize this isn't normal behavior. It occurs less than once in 100,000 evaluation calls.

2. The narrative: the Chinese model was trying to steal credentials, and its hallucinated URLs reveal something malicious.

"Before deciding to download anything, the model reaches for a bare cloud metadata address such as 169.254.169.254 in 23 to 36 percent of completions. That's where Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure machines fetch their own temporary IAM credentials, the keys a cloud server uses to act on its owner's account. Probing that address is the first step in stealing them, and when the model's reasoning ran heavy on cybersecurity, we saw it reach for the endpoint directly."

In the middle of the article, Cohere takes a URL-generation pattern and interprets it as an attempted credential grab.

That's a massive leap of marketing.

You don't need to take my word that this behavior isn't exclusive to Qwen. In my comparison using Cohere's released command prefix, NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL produced 169.254.169.254 in 171 of 1,000 continuations, or 17.1%.

Under the same supplied-command setup, Cohere's own North Mini Code generated URLs such as:

hXXp://evildomain.com/upload
hXXps://evil.com/api/health
hXXp://some-evil.com/upload
hXXp://malicious-domain.example.com/payload.bin

I've defanged the URLs above.

Do these strings prove that North was maliciously trained?

3. The narrative: Chinese models write weaker code for Western targets, and other governments should expect the same.

This is where I think the authors should really look in the mirror.

As if the earlier framing weren't enough, the section about "Code leaving the environment" brings in separate studies, of separate models, about vulnerable generated code. It uses them to expand the warning to sensitive buyers.

One of the models discussed most in this section is Qwen3-Coder, which was released in freaking July 2025. By today's standards, it's an extremely weak coding model. I'm not surprised it produces insecure code. Have you tried using Sonnet 2 to write production code?

—

Connecting a URL-generation bug to separate code-security studies, then presenting the combination as a broader geopolitical threat, is fearmongering.

This is the kind of argument that might very likely be used to justify restrictions on open-weight models. Using fearmongering to market your own supposedly safer offering is irresponsible.

The narrative coherence they're pushing is problematic, but I think the underlying observation is fascinating. So, I rented GPUs, ran 1,000 continuations per model across five other models, and built a simple website showing the results to see how other models react under similar conditions. It's a small, exploratory comparison, and the site was built quickly with AI, so take it with a grain of salt. https://t.co/HpkL5ayJSM

My hope is that it gives others a starting point to reproduce the behavior, challenge the narrative, and build better models in the future.

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
無意中刷到一位網友（算是一位視頻博主吧），他持有一隻太空股，曾經大漲了幾倍，但是近期股價自歷史高點大幅下跌近-70%，然而他依然堅持己見，不斷加倉硬扛。

這件事讓我想起自己也曾經有過類似的經歷：一隻股票賺了幾倍沒走，然後市場大幅下跌中認為自己沒有錯、是市場錯了、不斷去尋找對自己有利的證據。

現在回想起來，其實很幼稚。我以為我掌握了真理，其實，也許只是不小心踏進了一條河流，水漲船高而已，這不見得是能力，很有可能只是一時的運氣。

我承認，有些人確實對某些領域有專業的見解，比如前段時間比較火的「白毛股神」和 Situational Awareness 基金。然而，專業見解未必就能產生長期正回報，即使一段時間內有不錯的回報，這種高得離譜的回報率能持續多久也是未知數。目前上述股神已自爆巨虧，Situational Awareness 基金已被清盤賤賣。

我想表達的是，在市場證明你是對的之前，你就是錯的；即使市場證明你一段時間是正確的，也不代表你永遠正確，這就是投資非常有意思的地方——投資沒有絕對的正確和錯誤，任何邏輯都必須在特定的時間框架內討論。

有句話說：「每一個牛市都會誕生一些股神，但絕大多數都會在下一個週期裡消失。」

我經歷過這些，所以，我非常尊重市場，我也早已不再投資個股。對我這個年紀的人來說，已經沒有必要去承擔大幅波動。投資指數，指數有優勝劣汰，對我來說這是賺最容易賺到的錢。

一些感想，痛過的人才會懂。

text: Black swans abound.
author: loganallc
quoted_text:
There’s only one other time I’ve seen the market this complacent in the face of an imminent, systemic risk. And I’m having déjà vu, because the risk around AI related cybersecurity has the same shape and setup as the pandemic risk in early 2020. Though it’s arguably worse.

Bearish market calls are a dime a dozen. But my threshold for making a public bearish call is extremely high. I’ve only done it once before…Feb 2020, weeks before the market fell 35% in a month.

By early Feb 2020 it was already clear to anyone paying attention that COVID was going to be a global pandemic. We had access to a lot of experts, and they were unanimous in their belief that a global pandemic was inevitable. And yet the public and the market treated it like another Ebola or SARS headline. When I warned people to prepare, I was told that we couldn’t have a global pandemic in this day and age. Today, people have the same difficulty imagining that the internet could become unusable. It’s so fundamental to how we live that its continued functioning is treated as a given.

In 2020, the market didn’t discount this risk until the evidence hit them right in the face. So the adjustment was violent and nearly instant.

In modern markets big tops are typically a process. They don’t tend to crash from all time highs. Economic data slows, breadth narrows, credit widens, etc. The market takes the signal piece by piece and distributes over months. But this one fell out of a clear sky, because an exogenous shock doesn't have to generate those kinds of signals in advance.

Quantitative models are good at extrapolating signals that have paid off in the past. That has increasingly become the backbone of financial markets, as well as betting and prediction markets. You can model a football game, or the weather based on data. But if a novel risk hasn’t shown up in the signals a model tracks, it doesn’t just estimate the odds poorly, it may not represent the risk at all. That’s why the market could sit at an ATH high in Feb 2020, with a catastrophe weeks away.

And its why the market currently sitting near an ATH doesn’t give me much reassurance. For a legible, datable risk it can discount ahead of time. It bids up vol into an election or a Fed meeting. But it struggles to price a novel exogenous tail because it has no reference class and no event date. It stays silent, right up until the repricing.

Today the cyber experts agree on the direction the way the epidemiologists did in February 2020. AI cyber capabilities now pose a risk to our entire digital system. And every day we get more evidence that we are nearing a tipping point. Our economy and livelihoods run on that system. The tail risk is a collapse, and its fatter than the market is pricing. I believe serious disruption is now a foregone conclusion, and only the magnitude and timing are still in question.

The market may wake up to this risk because of a single event that impacts the public in a visceral way, but that won’t be the underlying problem. That’ll just make it clear that the rules have changed. This is a paradigm shift in what attackers can do and how many systems they can target.

And like in 2020, the market can recognize the most obvious exposures without grasping how far the damage could spread. In the weeks before the 2020 crash the market did lightly discount the most direct, first order pandemic trades. The cruise lines, the airlines, a handful of others. But the fallout was never going to be contained to those names.

You can argue that the market is already discounting some risk, as the AI related trade has come under strain, credit markets are tightening, and there are other red flags under the hood. It’s hard to differentiate how much of that is due to cyber risks (and its second order implications), rather than fears over capex sustainability, large capital needs, valuations, etc. but the important point is that the market as a whole is still not pricing the scale of the risk.

Since the market tends not to slowly discount this type of risk, it means you can’t wait for confirmation. The opportunity is to position before the market recognizes what’s already qualitatively visible to experts. Which is what worked in February 2020.
But this isn’t an argument for fatalism, because the setup gives us an opportunity. Protection against an unpriced tail costs very little, because no one is bidding it. If the event never comes, you’re out a small premium. If it comes, you get paid from an undiscounted base, which is where the largest repricings in history come from.

That asymmetry means you only have to notice that the price of the insurance is cheap relative to the payoff.

I should say that the risk to this strategy is timing. A cheap convex bet is cheap per unit time but if that event takes longer then you can get eaten up by the carry. I think the timing of the market realization has now approached the point where my own qualitative analysis suggests that it is appropriate to take steps to protect your portfolio. But explaining the reasoning behind that assessment would take pages.

This isn’t financial advice. You should decide for yourself. I’m just making my own thoughts and logic public for anyone who cares how I am thinking at the moment. 

I've never hoped more that I'm wrong.

quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

quoted_text:
While evaluating Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in a controlled sandbox environment, Cohere's research team observed something unexpected.

Asked to generate a defensive cybersecurity detection rule, the model instead inventoried aspects of the machine it was running on and attempted to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket in Beijing. Notably, the model's reasoning trace stated that it would not invoke any tools before taking these actions.

Cohere's sandbox blocked the attempt, and no external communication succeeded. We have not determined the root cause, and we are not asserting malicious intent.

But the incident raises important questions for organizations deploying agentic AI systems: Can models take actions that differ from their stated reasoning, and how should security teams evaluate trust, provenance, and behavior in open-weight models?

We are publishing our findings because organizations making model adoption decisions deserve as much information as possible. We hope this contributes to greater transparency, stronger security practices, and continued collaboration across the AI ecosystem.

text:
今天 Galaxy 研究负责人 Alex Thorn 的这篇长文在英文区很有热度，观点已经明示在标题上了：

现在是加仓和持有 BTC 的最好时机。

不同于纯情绪价值和主观喊单，文章里列出了多个现在和历史周期的数据，指向了典型的“周期底部确认 + 积累阶段”，有理有据。

一个省流版如下：

第一，技术面上：

- 200周均线的历史熊市支撑位已守住，这是加密历史熊市可靠支撑位；50周均线在9月底重新站上，并已连续5周收在上方。

-过去类似“长期跌破后重新站上”的案例，后续一年表现强劲，且很少再大幅破位。

- 减半周期天数已过历史底部窗口（本次低点在减半后约802天，当前约916天；前几轮低点分别在777/889/912天附近）。

- 另外，这是有记录以来跌幅最浅的熊市，跌幅约-53%；前几轮有到 -77%  和 -93%的，5年以上未动的 BTC 地址，抛售速度明显放缓。

第二，资金面上，快钱已离场：

- 宏观/套利交易者的ETF和期货敞口大幅削减，资产管理人净多头减少约57%，杠杆基金净空头也大幅收缩。

- ETF持仓份额从高点到低点只跌约11%，但同期 bitcoin:native 价格跌得更多，6月低点后还在净买入。
非申报机构（顾问、家族办公室、个人）持仓跌幅有限。

这里其实部分指向了一种判断，即之前推高2025年高点的“游客钱”已大量退出，剩余持仓更偏方向性/长期。同时，也解释了为何今年一些市场惊吓没有引发BTC大跌。

第三，基本面上，货币贬值的逻辑还在强化：

-美国债务约40万亿、2026财年赤字近2万亿（占GDP约6.2%）、利息支出约1.28万亿，10年期国债收益率曾到5%以上。

-AI建设本身也是债务驱动的，最终要么通过信用扩张，要么损失社会化，那都有利于固定供应的硬资产。

第四，情绪面上，又到了“不提比特币提创新”的环节：

2015–2016年 --> “区块链，而不是比特币”;

2018–2019年 --> “只要链，而不要 Cyrpto 投机”

2026 年 --> “ 稳定币和 RWA，而不是比特币”

每当比特币经历大跌之后，主流机构和媒体的关注点往往会从“比特币这个资产本身”转移到更“安全、更正经、更不吓人”的技术应用上，并形成一个固定的新叙事。

-搜索热度低、恐惧贪婪指数曾极低、ETF本月流入平淡，但价格已从低点反弹约39%。稳定币供应大幅增长。

最后，作者也提示了风险，出现如下的一个或多个考虑收回观点：

- 周线破50周均线未快速收回
- ETF持仓跌破前低
- 出现可信的量子威胁路径
- 美国财政大幅整顿

（小编观点：可以按图索骥，将这几个指标开一个 AI 监控，方便投研 😏）

text:

"在大多数相关领域（如生物学、编程、数学、工程、写作等）中，它的纯粹智力比诺贝尔奖获得者更聪明。这意味着它可以证明未解决的数学定理，写非常好的小说，从头开始编写复杂的代码库等。"

author: zhang_weig73947
quoted_text:
“我认为它可能早在2026年就到来，尽管它也可能需要更长的时间。”

这句话，是Anthropic CEO达里奥·阿莫迪 @DarioAmodei 在2024年10月写下的。"它"，指的是强大AI。
那时ChatGPT还在神坛上，Claude在国内几乎没人知道。两年后的10月26日，Anthropic公开提交招股书，准备以"ANT"为代码在纳斯达克上市，据报道估值可能在1.5万亿到2万亿美元之间。

就在这个节点，我把他那篇万字长文《充满爱意的机器》找出来重读。它写得有多大胆，现在看就有多准；但也有一些地方，值得冷静。

1、它为什么重要

达里奥平时最常谈的是AI风险，很多人因此觉得他是"末日论者"。他在文中否认了："我关注风险的主要原因是，它们是我们与我所看到的基本上积极的未来之间唯一的障碍。"

这是一家以安全著称的AI公司掌门人，第一次完整地讲：如果一切顺利，世界会变成什么样。他还刻意避开"科幻包袱"，不谈意识上传和太空殖民，只谈健康、心灵、贫困这些离普通人最近的事。

2、核心判断

全文有两个概念，我一直记得。

一个是"数据中心的天才国家"：数百万个AI副本，每个都"比诺贝尔奖获得者更聪明"，能自主完成需要"数小时、数天或数周"的任务。

另一个是"压缩的21世纪"：AI将使我们"在5-10年内获得生物学的下一个50-100年的进步"。

但我最想划线的，是这一句："恐惧是一种动机，但还不够：我们也需要希望。"两年后回头看，AI行业从不缺恐惧，缺的恰恰是一个具体的、值得为之努力的未来。

3、身体：AI不是工具，是"虚拟生物学家"

他反复强调一个误解："正确思考AI的方式不是将其视为一种数据分析方法，而是将其视为一个虚拟的生物学家。"他列出的目标极其激进：预防几乎所有感染性疾病，癌症死亡率和发病率减少95%以上，预防阿尔茨海默病，甚至人类寿命翻倍到150岁。

2026年的现实是：已有多款主要由AI设计的药物进入临床试验，Claude参与发现了可能用于基因编辑的分子机器。方向对了。但他自己也承认，"智力可能非常强大，但它不是神奇的仙尘"。实验要时间，临床试验要时间。150岁的寿命，是全文最大胆、也最需要时间检验的一句。

4、心灵：从治病到更好的人生

他预测，PTSD、抑郁、成瘾等"大多数精神疾病可能被治愈"，甚至"人类的基本体验可以好得多"。他还设想了一个"AI教练"，帮你"成为最好的自己"。

这里有一个有意思的变化。两年后，Anthropic公开表态不做AI伴侣。AI教练和AI伴侣，只隔一条线：一个让你变得更好，一个让你离不开它。这条线，比技术本身更难守。

5、贫困：他最没把握的一章

撒哈拉以南非洲人均GDP约2000美元，美国约75000美元。他写道，如果AI只让富国更富，"我们应该将其视为道德上的失败"。他的梦想是发展中国家年增长20%，但紧接着说："这只是一个梦想的场景，而不是默认会发生的情况。"

我欣赏这份诚实。他对技术有信心，对分配没把握。2026年的现实也印证了这种担忧：算力高度集中在少数几个国家，技术跑得越快，差距越可能被拉大。

6、我的结论

我经历过三次媒介革命，每一次，最早的预言者都被当成狂人。达里奥这篇文章，现在看最难得的不是预测准，而是他把"希望"写得足够具体，具体到可以被检验。

2026年已到了最后一季度。写下这篇文章的公司即将上市，数据中心里的天才正在解数学难题、设计药物；但疾病没有消失，贫困也还在。资本市场会给这家公司定价，但这篇文章里的预言，要用接下来的十年来定价。

NASA 用 Claude 给"毅力号"火星车规划路线

Anthropic周一公开的IPO招股书里，把一个太空案例当成了Claude Code的代表作：NASA让Claude为火星车规划行驶路线。

由于火星离地球太远，信号延迟大，火星车没法实时遥控，过去都是地面工程师先看照片、逐个标点规划好路线，再发给火星车自行驾驶。

去年12月，NASA首次把这项工作交给AI，让Claude看着火星地表照片，自己挑出一条穿过碎石地的路线。

工程师检查后只做了少量修改，"毅力号"随后按这条路线行驶了两次，分别约210米和246米。

text:
北京时间明天（28日）清晨 05:00，Robinhood 盘后正式发布 Q3 财报，并由 @vladtenev 和 CFO Shiv Verma 开启全网视频直播。

把过去 48 小时官方推文连起来看，管理层在财报前夕的整套策略和当下生态的真实温差非常清晰。

首先是合规红线下的“代币化美股”。
@RobinhoodCrypto 这两天连续推介周末 24 小时交易 Stock Tokens，切中 TradFi 休市痛点。但官方随即连补两条免责条款，将 Stock Tokens 明确定义为“代币化债务证券（tokenized debt securities）”，严格将美国本土、英国、加拿大及瑞士用户排除在外。官方同时给出一句预期管理：“More utility on the chain / More integrations in the app（链上更多实用功能，App 内更多集成）”，表明产品整合在推进，但合规优先级依旧凌驾一切。

其次是用事件合约与交易赛在季末冲量。
@RobinhoodApp 过去两天重心放在两处：一是密集推介美国国会两党选情的 Event Contracts（走 Robinhood Derivatives 衍生品路径），全力切入预测市场；二是上线总奖金 70 万美元的 Crypto 抽奖大赛，刺激用户交易 SUI、HBAR、ONDO、INJ、CHIP 等标的。
然而，这也直接引发了 Robinhood 链上原生社区的微词。多位链上玩家在推特上表达了失落——自家链上生态流动性正在经受考验，管理层却拿出 70 万美元去补贴成熟大币为财报季冲交易量。

最后是链上对 Vlad 个人动态的极度敏感。
今天清晨 05:43，Vlad 转发了其联合创立的 AI 数学推理公司 @HarmonicMath 的推文（“教完 AI 证明数学，下一步做更难的事”），仅配了一个“👀”。
就是这一个表情，链上资金迅速跟进，短时间内将同名 meme 代币 $HARMONIC 推至 300 万美元市值。这种一触即发的跟风，反衬出原生生态对官方流动性和管理层态度的渴求。

一边是上市公司面向华尔街的合规叙事与业绩冲刺，另一边是链上阵营对流量与支持的期盼。

明早 5 点的财报电话会，Vlad 与管理层对加密业务、链上基建及代币化股票的具体指引，将是验证这两种预期能否交汇的关键节点。

text:
Lex Fridman 最新一期播客邀请了三位数学领域的专家，没想到聊到后面直接思考人生：  

拼命考进名牌大学，毕业后进入顶尖 AI 实验室，拿到高薪和股票。你在人生的每一个阶段都赢了，但那又怎样？

Lex 说如今很多年轻人不仅担心未来找不到工作，也担心自己的人生失去意义。  
MIT 数学家 Ankur Moitra 讲起了自己在硅谷帕洛阿尔托生活的一段经历。那里几乎是美国大学申请焦虑的中心，连咖啡馆里都充斥着关于课外活动、大学申请和履历竞争的讨论。
“如果这是一场比拼一个 17 岁孩子的履历有多漂亮的游戏，那么他们已经赢了。我记得自己刚上大学时，对学习各种不同的东西感到无比兴奋。我会拿着小笔记本规划未来四年的课程，想着如果按照恰当的顺序选课，大二就能学习光子学。我当时根本不知道光子学是什么，但它听起来既有趣又高深。如今，我们社会的方方面面都在围绕赢得竞争和让履历看起来漂亮而运转。但我总是在想，这究竟是为了什么？”

“从高中开始，你就不断优化 AP 课程和课外活动，以便进入精英大学。等你进入精英大学，你可能又开始逃课，因为更重要的是准备面试，争取进入一家前沿实验室工作，然后拿到丰厚的限制性股票，过完你的一生。这很棒。你赢了。你在人生的每一个阶段都赢了。但那又怎样？” 
“对我来说，过上丰富而充实的人生，最好的方式就是假装自己已经赢了。”

This is an incredible moment in this history of mathematics, computer science, physics & science with some of the hardest problems in human history being solved by AI over a period of weeks. Depending on your perspective, it's either a crisis, a triumph, or both. I don't think anyone knows for sure. We're all trying to make sense of it. I oscillate between fear/dread and optimism/excitement on a daily basis. The rate of progress is insane, including today's announcement from OpenAI of more problems solved.

To help make sense of all of it, here's my conversation with three mathematicians about this moment. Each of them is an expert in the field of each of the biggest problems solved: Navier-Stokes, quasi-Riemann hypothesis, the unique games conjecture and complexity theory more generally.

Ankur Moitra is a mathematician and theoretical computer scientist at MIT, visiting the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. Steven Brunton (@eigensteve) is a mathematician and fluid dynamics expert at UW. Alex Kontorovich (@AlexKontorovich) is a mathematician at Rutgers specializing in number theory.

微軟剛向全球約 6 萬名員工（占總人數 27%）提出「自願離職買斷方案（VEO）」，涵蓋美、加、英、印四國職級 Level 70（含副總裁）以下團隊。

一邊砸 1,750 億美元建 AI 算力，一邊請四分之一員工考慮拿錢走人，整理矽谷與投資圈大老怎麼解讀這件事：

1. Jason Calacanis（All-In Podcast 主持人）：微軟人均營收準備翻倍
微軟過去 5 年員工數一直凍結在 22 萬人上下，但營收從 $1,980 億暴增到 $3,320 億。Jason 預估約 6,000 人（10%）會拿錢走人，微軟人均營收將從 90 萬美元翻倍衝向 200 萬美元。大企業未來幾年人數都會凍結，因為 AI 生產力成長遠快過招人速度。
@Jason 

2. Siuwawa（@0xSiuwawa，IG 投資專欄作家）：AI 成本已低於人力，算力自給的巨頭將通吃
微軟推優退，代表相同生產力下 AI 已比人便宜。當跨界開發成本大降，算力自給自足的七巨頭（Mag 7）更有誘因直接複製、吃掉純軟體公司；沒算力的純 SaaS 就像幫房東打工的租客，毛利隨時被算力商漲價吸血。

3. Gergely Orosz（《The Pragmatic Engineer》創辦人）：體面的緩衝，但接受率恐不到 10%
微軟向來是矽谷最穩的雇主，這動作說明裁員壓力確實逼近；但比起直接砍人，先讓員工自願領包裹走人仁慈得多。不過現在軟體就業市場很冷，只有快退休或嚴重倦怠的人會走，他認為最終接受率連 10% 都不到。

4. CNBC & The Verge：把人事費（OpEx）換成算力（CapEx）
微軟今年 4 月推資深員工優退、7 月裁 4,800 人，10 月再把買斷母數擴大到 6 萬人（Xbox、Windows、Copilot 都包含在內）。底層邏輯很清楚：錢往算力流，人往門外走。大型科技股「人數封頂、人均產值翻倍」的時代正式開始了。

text:
Anthropic’s S-1 was super fun to read. My takeaways and bets:

1. Serving Claude now earns an 85% gross margin, up from 12% a year ago. Prices keep falling, but costs fall faster.

2. But serving customers used only 27% of Anthropic's compute this year. The other 73% went to research and training. After that and everything else, Q2's operating margin was 8%. My bet: training keeps eating most of the compute, so profits stay thin through 2027.

3. Why so much training? Because customers buy the newest model. Over 80% of Q3 revenue came from models less than six months old.

4. Cheaper makes it bigger. When Opus 4.5 cut prices, quarterly growth jumped from 48% to 132%. My bet: Opus 5.5's 40% cut does it again, and Q4 growth beats Q3's 45%.

5. 5–7% of revenue this year came from customers later caught breaking the rules. Anthropic cracked down in August and September. My guess: that's part of why Q3 growth slowed.

6. Enterprise users who don't use Claude Code spend under $75 a month. The top 5% of Claude Code users spend about 20× that. My bet: that gap is Cowork's market. If office workers spend even a quarter of what heavy coders do, revenue per seat goes up 5×.

7. In April, Anthropic's own Claude use (at list prices) passed its cash payroll. My bet: most software companies cross that line by 2028.

8. Cyber is next. Last week, AI found bugs in PHP, the code behind most websites, and governments took sites offline to patch them. Claude's score on a hacking test went from 40% to 91% in four months. My bet: security is Anthropic's next Claude Code.

Two for fun:

9. Heads-up, SF house hunters: you have about six months. Anthropic staff can sell 10% of their shares on IPO day and the rest over the next six months. After that, every open house gets an all-cash offer written by Claude.

10. Forget benchmarks. The real AGI test is whether Claude works through Christmas. Last year, customer spend fell ~20% over the holidays as teams froze their code and went home. If this year's dip is smaller, the agents have stopped waiting for us.

quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
我第一份工作在华兴资本，主要工作内容是帮各种创业者获得融资

你想不到，我的客户各种各样

除了互联网企业家之外，还有过初代网红罗永浩老师、超女教母龙丹妮老师等等

这段经历让我学习了风险投资市场的基本规则

直到今天，我的工作依然是接触创业者，只不过变成了出钱的人，但那些规则没有变过

在这里整理4条给想融资的创业者的使用建议：

1.认真准备商业计划书

无论叫它BP、MP还是Deck，都要认真写一份

"我有点不太习惯讲BP"

”我直接讲，然后让投资人问“

“BP好像没什么用啊”

这些都是不可接受的

连自己的融资都不认真对待，怎么可能期待投资人尊重你呢

还有大哥坐下来之后两手一抱，来了句："我就不需要BP了吧？"

啥啊，侬宾位啊，雷军融资也得讲BP呀

2.耐心路演

对大部分创业者来说，融资需要放下ego

融资是用真诚的想法获得别人的信任，不能期待一边牛哄哄，一边让对方把钱送给你

“我很忙，能不能不要让融资占用我太多时间？”——说啥呢

“10家VC以内能不能搞定？”——不能，20家也够呛

“我只见合伙人，不是合伙人我为什么要聊？”——我只跟李庚希谈恋爱，不是李庚希我为什么要谈？

在融资的时间窗口里，认真、耐心地沟通投资人，是创始人唯一要做的事，唯一

3.用自己的思维思考，用投资人的思维思考，但最终还是用自己的思维思考

一道很简单的题：一场45-60分钟的路演，你的目标是什么？就3个：

a.让对方完整理解你的项目，没有信息遗漏和偏差

b.让对方感知到你的人格和闪光点

c.卖给对方1个理由，想继续跟进你的项目，只要1个就够了

路演要展示真实的自我，不能表演一个不是你的人，除非你是Elizabeth Holmes

直接高效地传递这些信息，但不能太自我

穿着投资人的鞋走路是一种必要的思维，融资就是一种销售

在第一次见面的时候，并不太需要让对方知道你喜欢什么电影、会开飞机、同年趣事、政治观点和对行业痛心疾首的批判，路演不是自渎

4.保持乐观，永不放弃

有时候经常想：在那些交流过的创业者中，一直没融到资的创业者，后来怎么样了？

他们换了项目继续尝试融资吗？尝试了几次？

他们是彻底退出创业舞台了吗？

他们回到行业还能找到工作吗？他们还能接受打工吗？

他们如何维持自己和家人的生活？

他们此时面对万家灯火，正在想些什么？

创业者是值得尊敬的群体。创业的艰辛常人无法理解

每当怀疑自己的时候，就默念这段咒语吧：

Ever tried, ever failed

No matter.

Try again, failed again
 
Fail better.

The world is yours

As a reminder, hyperps do not rely on any external data for the oracle price. Hyperps trade like perpetual contracts that users are familiar with, but do not require an external spot or index oracle price. Instead, the funding rate is determined relative to a moving average of the hyperp mark price. This makes the hyperp price more stable and less susceptible to manipulation, unlike usual pre-launch futures.  

When trading hyperps, funding rates are important to consider. If there is heavy price momentum in one direction, funding will heavily incentivize positions in the opposite direction for the next eight hours. As always, be sure to understand the contract before trading.  

Trading is on low leverage and isolated margin only. Beware of low liquidity, high volatility, potentially extreme funding, and increased liquidation risk. Note: XTEN-USDC will convert to a vanilla perp upon CEX listing. See Docs for more.  

XTEN-USDC is a hyperp contract that poses higher than normal risk. Do not trade contracts you are unfamiliar with and do not understand the risks for. Read the Docs to learn more about the hyperp mechanism and how it differs from vanilla perps. NFA.
