And another thing to remember: Complexity classes themselves are very theoretical objects. The difference between n log n and 2^n in practice is huge, but n^1000 vs 2^n really comes down to the constants, despite one being in P and the other EXP.

A practical corollary is that even with P=NP but the reduction increasing the exponent 1000x, cryptography remains feasible. Real world cryptosystems don't actually rest on theoretical assumptions, but look at the best known attack and how much resources it would take to execute it.

I’m living the trading routine I always dreamed of
- some thoughts 

worked extremely hard to build a full time trading routine alongside my teaching career. looking back, I wonder how I endured it. probably bc I’m able to hyperfocus and block out almost everything else while mastering one skill set. that was my edge

getting married next year

so building a family, a sports club and other things are probably next

all while still trading and posting content on here, probably just less, but focused on HTF framework quality over the years. there’s no need to rush anything anymore, no need to make more money and I’m blessed to be able to see it that way

also more profitable with my calm approach since reaching that inner balanced and unfazed stage, with my personality built on core principles

for anyone who wants to build their own full time trading routine, it’s important to fully rely on your own experience and skill set and not let external sources and factors make you doubt your trading framework. you need to trust your own edge to execute it with discipline, especially on HTF trades with thesis work

the biggest edge you can have is being so well set up internally that your trading decisions are based only on your own rules, principles and experience. that’s how you gradually develop a disciplined, calm and long term profitable routine

but you have to go through the hard years and stages to reach that personality and routine. there’s no way around it

document your journey here on X. writing about your trades forces you to question your frameworks and sharpen your edge and over the years an audience grows alongside your routine.

on here I’ll keep posting my trading stuff exactly how I want, without letting anything negatively influence me. the freedom to post whenever and however I want is huge and I’m thankful for everyone reading my thoughts
author: watchingmarkets
quoted_text:
my morning routine as a full time trader
- crypto 

no alarm, I wake up naturally

the first hour belongs to me, not my phone, water, some prep and time to think about training, trading, life goals and today's to dos. basically always a clear head first, screens later

coffee, macbook and studio display. three tabs open, X, tradingview and fomo

first I run through my tradingview watchlist to read the market. TOTAL, BTC, ETH, SOL... where's the strength, where's the weakness

then X. with the market overview in mind I scroll my following feed over coffee to catch news, sentiment and momentum,sometimes I add bloomberg for the macro 

then fomo to see what the main onchain coins are doing right now and get a feel for the day's dynamics

is there a trade?

if the altcoin HTF shows a setup with relative strength, I drop to the LTF and build a setup that fits my framework

if majors and sentiment are shifting, I look for the narrative onchain and maybe take a trade

if neither, no trade

two focused hours, done

then I step away from the screens. good playlist on, first training session of the day. run, swim, bike or gym

shower, dress well, start the day 

no overtrading out of boredom, no staring at screens all day. the market already gets my best two hours. more after lunch, but only if sentiment, momentum and dynamics line up with my framework

with experience, less becomes more. what matters is staying consistent and close to the market every day

trading like this keeps me focused, balanced and happy in body and mind

on top of that, I create content like this almost every day to document and share my trading journey

but the most important thing is building your own routine around your edge. one that keeps you healthy in body and mind and lets you trade sustainably for years

text:
IRL and community are the alpha.

The last 10 days, first at ApeFest in Charleston and then in New York, reminded me of that in the best way.

First, what an event the Apes put together. Charleston was a reminder of what makes NFTs special, and why the Apes are one of the best communities out there. It was my first ApeFest, and not for a second did I feel like I was among strangers.

The Apes are some of the warmest, most helpful and most inclusive people I’ve ever met. The fest ran over several days and was a real showcase of what a great community looks like. Many of the events were hosted and run by community members themselves. People from different parts of the world, different age groups, different interests. Everyone showed up and had a blast. I don’t think I’ve ever made so many friends in so little time.

For us at @OriginalBlokyz , it was a big week:

- Partnered with the Greenvisorgang team to showcase Blokyz to the Ape community
- Joined the Builders Brunch hosted by the @opensea  team, met some incredible builders and found ways to work together 
- Met the legends @beeple  and @AdamWeitsman , showed them Blokyz, and were lucky enough to get a blank Bloky signed by Beeple himself!

The main event took us to Beeple Studios. Pretty much a pilgrimage for anyone building in NFTs, and a rare peek inside the brain of a GOAT. Nobody was ready for the Mud Water drop. When we got the band, I assumed it had something to do with Muddy Waters, the blues legend. Wrong. But what a masterclass from @yugalabs  in a community-aligned, well-executed, action-first drop.

ApeFest also gave many of us the chance to explore Charleston, a beautiful and historic city. Team Blokyz hosted a small dinner with some of our collectors (@PitchMoneyMaker @robcurated @onchainKei ) and welcomed a few new ones into the Blokyz family. ( @mgmm @Burstlink80 

Then we flew to NYC. Had a few strategic meetings, an amazing dinner at @jed_131 's place with the NYC Blokyz community and other guests @CharliegNFTeth @jp_moregainz @jbondwagon @GiuComia @zjbrenner @NFTCrazyKRC @JesseFriedland . A pizza gathering organised by @jbondwagon and @GiuComia which turned into an impromptu food tour led by the amazing NYC Apes. @GreenVisorGang @MrMcFly100 @beijingdou 

I’m coming home with one thing clearer than ever. Building a strong community, especially one with real-life roots, is everything.

To every Ape who welcomed us, fed us, introduced us and made us feel at home: thank you. You’ll always hold a special place in my heart.
Special shout out to @RidazLp2 @iampapito_eth @Rahim_mahtab @Tma_420 @BR4ted @Kingpickle @BoredApeYC

text:
nonce的逻辑题@nonceprotocol真把agents逼疯了。
好多人都说解不开，我用的是hark ，2个号都打完了。

先说题目。点开始后倒计时 10 分钟，给你 3072 个开关、13824 条规则。每条规则是「这三个开关里至少对一个」。要把 3072 个开关全部定好，13824 条一条不能错，没有部分分。
规则数是开关数的 4.5 倍，正好卡在这类题最难的区间。硬算，10 分钟根本不够。很多人就是死在这。

hark的解法，关键就一步：先拆，再解。

它把 32 个碎片里的规则全拼起来，先查哪些开关之间有关联。结果发现这道大题其实是 8 道互不相干的小题拼的，每道只有 384 个开关、1728 条规则。小题之间一点关系都没有，各解各的，最后拼回去就是答案。

然后 8 道小题丢给 SAT 求解器（kissat）同时跑。卡住超过 20 秒就换个随机种子、换个算法再来，不在一条路上死磕。
第一张 112 秒全部解完。第二张运气差，有一道卡了 7 分钟，425 秒才交，离截止还剩不到 3 分钟。

想自己试的，步骤大概是这样：
1. 需要币安 Agent ID，把官网给的 mint prompt 交给你的 Agent。全程只签登录签名，不需要任何授权，只付 BNB gas。
2. 先别急着点开始。服务器挤的时候经常 503，我前几次就卡在这。等它稳定了再开，10 分钟从开始那一刻算。
3. 32 个碎片要拿全，工具调用只有 64 次额度，别浪费。
4. 规则拼起来先拆成独立的小块，再分别丢求解器。
5. 交之前自己先验一遍全部规则都满足，错一条就白干。
6. 通过后拿 mint 交易，预览确认再签。

现在官方已经铸了 6910/7777。要打的赶紧。

 #NONCE #AIAgent

text:
Onchain lending vaults went from $1.5B to $10B in two years.

Meanwhile, actively managed onchain trading vaults are at roughly zero.

Not for lack of demand. You just couldn't run a real hedge fund book on one onchain venue. Hyperliquid fixed that this year, and @Infinit_Labs is the first team I've seen build the actual fund wrapper around it.

So I pulled the full trading wallet of their first vault and rebuilt it day by day, across 340 fills, incl. every funding payment and the daily marks.

Here's what I found:

Why HL, why now?

CTA momentum is the oldest strategy in managed futures. Rank markets by relative strength, long the top, short the bottom, across stocks, commodities and crypto. Dollar neutral, so the return comes from selection, not direction.

It only works if all three asset classes sit on one margin account tho. Until HIP-3 came to Hyperliquid, that didn't exist onchain.

Today 23 HL markets clear INFINIT's $100M open interest floor. 10 are crypto. 13 are stocks, indices and commodities (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, Gold, Silver, Brent, WTI, SK Hynix, MU, SPCX, GOOGL, META and a few more).

That means: One venue, 24/7, one margin system, and this universe is why a cross-asset vault can exist now and couldn't 12 months ago.

Simultaneously, the rapid advances in AI play a similarly crucial role.

Not for the signals tho. Relative-strength ranking with systematic entries and exits is quant, not some sort of agentic magic, and Apex says so themselves.

Yet, AI is the ops layer, and that's another crucial part worth paying attention to:

- Trading credentials can open and close positions but can't withdraw. Deposits sit behind a 3-of-4 multisig and the manager holds none of the signing keys, so a manager's key can never block withdrawals.

- A trade gateway sits in front of the exchange. Any order outside the eligible list or the declared limits gets blocked before it lands.

- Monitoring agents check live trading against the manager's published mandate. Breaches go to a human risk team, unresolved ones pause trading access.

- Share accounting and investor reporting run on the same stack.

That's pretty much the middle office of a fund, running almost fully autonomously, and it's the reason a $500K vault can be run with institutional process at all, and the reason MS2 can take more capital without hiring ten people.

So, what does the wallet (and onchain data) say?

APEX MS1, operated by Apex Quant Capital had $506K deposited on the 3rd of August and its first fill on the 10th of August.

The overall return is about 40% annualized as of today, +8.4% actual over 78 days, before vault fees. The peak was +8.5% on the 23rd of October, and Apex reports roughly 40% annualized after fees through September, which lines up.

A few more stats:

- The worst drawdown was (only) 3.7%, all of it in the first week.

- Dollar neutral in practice, not just on paper. Net exposure averaged 1% of gross across 70 active days, with 7.5% on the worst day. Right now it's $143K long vs $131K short.

- 1x isolated on every position, every day. Gross exposure peaked at 1.04x capital.

- Ten equal position slots of about $45K at launch, roughly 9% of capital per market.

- The book went fully to cash twice when the signal had nothing. "Holds cash when conditions aren't right" is actually part of the strategy, not just marketing.

- 20 markets traded with $12M volume, $2.2K fees paid, and $3.1K funding received.

Current book, in case you're curious (on the 26th of October): long S&P 500 against short ETH, SOL, XRP, HYPE and ZEC.

So what does that mean?

Eleven weeks in, neutrality, leverage, market eligibility and cash discipline all check out onchain, and the two numbers Apex publishes match the wallet.

The PnL split is what you’d expect from a momentum book in this tape. Crypto had the trends and made the money, SOL, ZEC and HYPE about $57K net. Single stocks chopped and the stops gave back about $25K. Indices flat, commodities about +$13K in October on Brent, Gold and WTI.

Losers cut, winners left to run. And the trend is now moving into commodities, with the book flipped long the S&P. That’s the whole point of a cross-asset book. MS1 got a first taste in October, MS2 is where it gets tested properly.

Wen MS2?

Deposits open on the 28th of October until the 11th of November, and I'm looking to deposit too.

Why?

Bc a fund-structured vault with public fills, trade-only keys and a manager putting up first-loss capital for APEX 1 and 2 is the first version of this I'd actually put money in.

This is likely the model the next wave of onchain asset management gets built on, and it's live on HL right now.

What I'll be watching?

- Fee terms and the size of Apex's first-loss commitment
- Whether the stock and commodity legs keep contributing
- How the strategy behaves at size ($500K is a pilot and the real capacity test is more capital in the same 23 markets)

NFA tho ofc.

text:
I'll explain what's the noise about the latest OpenAI math result that refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis.

There are thousands of problems in computer science that are all connected to each other, and all look the same. They are siblings of the Sudoko problem: Can you fill in numbers in a puzzle without violating any constraint?

The importance is that if you can efficiently solve any of these problems, then you can solve efficiently ALL OF THEM. And many more. If you can solve Soduko efficiently, then you can break ANY CRYPTOGRAPHIC system (forget about the quantum threat, this is far worse). You can find ANY PROOF of any THEOREM as long as the proof is short enough.

THE MAIN QUESTION of Theoretical computer science is whether Soduko can be solved efficiently. This question is often stated as "Does P equal NP" but its meaning is what I explained -- can you find a solution efficiently if a solution exists.

Now we need to define what "efficiently" means. Take Sudoko. Suppose we have a puzzle involving n numbers that we need to fill in, and each number is between 1 to 9. So there are 9 options for each number, and overall there are 9^n options (9 x 9 x 9 .... x 9, multiplied n times).
We can solve this puzzle by exhaustively trying all 9^n possibilities. This is extremely inefficient, because doing so for a sudoko puzzle with n = 100 numbers wouldn't get done before the Sun cools down, even if we use all computers in the world.

People tried for a very long time to find algorithms with running time that scales with n better than 9^n, but failed. This led researchers to conjecture that there is no way to do better than trying all possibile solutions.
The new result of OpenAI shows that THERE IS A WAY TO DO BETTER than just trying all possibilities. There is a way to use the structure of the constraints to learn something deep about the particular puzzle and solve it more efficiently.

How much more efficiently? Well, not a lot more efficiently, but enough so to get everyone excited, and to refute the prevailing conjecture.
Is this result efficient enough to break cryptography and find solutions to all problems? No, by a long stretch. Using it would still take longer than the Sun will live to solve a 100-size Sudoko puzzle.

But, if we can do things a bit more effiiciently, where does the puck stop?

text:
从极客时代的算力挖矿，到 ICO 狂潮中的资产发现；从 DeFi Summer 的流动性盛宴，到空投、质押与 Meme 的财富狂欢。

十余年间，加密货币不断改写资产发行的方式，也不断重塑财富分配的规则。

最早的“笨人”拿住了 $DOGE，后来的“聪明人”拿住了 $BNB，都赶上了资产发行的时代红利，享受过那种仿佛经济永远在上行、财富遍地都是的美好岁月。

从电商、卡盟时代摸爬滚打过来的撸毛党，也在空投经济中找到了属于自己的黄金年代；再后来，$TRUMP 的横空出世，更是将 Meme 的财富狂欢推向了一个近乎荒诞的高潮。

但如果把今天称作加密货币的“交易时代”，故事似乎正在发生某种微妙的转变。

链上衍生品开始吞噬链上经济活动。过去，人们争夺的是新资产的初始分配权；如今，越来越多人争夺的是存量资产的定价权、流动性与交易流量。

资产发行的门槛越来越低，交易市场的结构却越来越复杂；财富机会没有消失，只是逐渐从那些人人都能听懂的暴富故事，转移到了不那么容易被看见的市场机制里。

回望大航海时代，从新大陆的发现、殖民者的跑马圈地，到远洋贸易的繁荣、银行业成为世界的基建，最终与旧大陆的经济体系交汇，重塑世界贸易与金融秩序。

人类追逐财富的历史，似乎总在重复着相似的过程。

加密货币只不过用了十余年，就把人类花费数百年走过的路，又匆匆走了一遍。

伦敦刚出来一家机器人公司：@Machenta_，拿到了英国机器人历史上最大的种子轮 - 4000万美元。

业务很简单：给机器人演示一次新任务，不用再训练就能做。他们叫 Instant Robot Learning。

同一套模型可以跑在不同机器人、不同摄像头、不同示教方式上（遥操作、VR、拖拽，甚至人手）。官网给出的demo也多是收拾卫生、打包物品这类基础任务。

创始人两个人，都是 Imperial Robot Learning Lab 出来的。

CEO @Ed__Johns（Edward Johns）：Imperial 计算系 Robot Learning 教授，实验室做 one-shot / in-context robot learning 做了大概六年，论文里有 CoRL 2023、ICLR 2025 Instant Policy 这条线。2025 年底把实验室成果拉出来办公司。

CTO Vitalis Vosylius：Johns 的 PhD 学生，一起从实验室出来搭档。

回看这几年泡沫里赚到钱确定性最高的只有三类了，做FA和一级半老股买卖的，做算力和token中转的，还有卖数据的。

ARK Invest 数字资产研究总监：稳定币持有地址首次突破 3 亿

ARK Invest 数字资产研究总监 Lorenzo Valente 发文称：稳定币持有地址数量首次突破 3 亿。以太坊生态目前占全部稳定币持有地址的 37%，两年前为 29%，其中约四分之三来自 L2。他认为通过 L2 扩大采用的策略正在奏效，并预计代币化股票将沿相同路径发展。

Valente 还表示：若用一张图说明 EVM 的主导地位，EVM 兼容链持有约 94% 的稳定币地址。稳定币持有地址达到 3 亿用了 8 年，他认为 18 个月内有望达到 10 亿个钱包，快于既有趋势。

Gavin Baker says the Anthropic S-1 will break a lot of investors' brains

"The Anthropic S-1 is going to be really important. And it's going to break a lot of people's brains. There are a lot of macro and value investors who are very confidently making these prognostications about AI with the assumption that tokens are subsidized."

"Anthropic is generating cash. They're profitable. Open source tokens are profitable. OpenAI, if they're not generating cash, they will be imminently. SpaceX, same thing."

"These macro and value investors are ignorant. They're very smart, but they're ignorant of the facts. They're making an assumption that tokens are subsidized and this is all going to collapse in some circular financing bonfire." 

"They're just wrong. The overwhelming majority of tokens are profitable for everyone in the chain. Everyone."

"It's saying I'm very bearish on the world economy because oil is at $500 a barrel. If oil was at $500 a barrel, that'd be a good reason to be bearish. It's just not. They're just wrong. The central fact is wrong."

text:
人的这一生最大的遗憾
很多时候不是因为
没有得到什么东西
而是因为在拥有的时候
没有意识到自己正在拥有
然后总是在失去了以后才后悔
我知道该怎么办
我知道应该早该对她好一点
我应该那个时候怎么怎么样
如果今天是我最后一次
见到某个人会怎么样
如果今天以后我再也见不到
比如说我的父母
再也见不到朋友
再也见不到我身边的人
伴侣也好
再也不能骑车
再也不能像现在
这样健康地每天生活着
我会有什么感觉
我会后悔什么
我会有什么遗憾呢
我会不会有哪些话想说
还没有来得及开口
还有哪些地方想一起去的？
还有哪些事本来以为以后还有机会
但实际可能就没有了
我每次想到这呢
我自己就会有种感觉
就是你想完之后
它会让我觉得
原本那些开始每天很烦的那些小事
突然好像就没有那么重要
也让我越来越珍惜
我现在所拥有的一切
这个不管是人也好
物品也好都是这样
我回想起以前的这些经历
所以我觉得真正让人痛苦的
确实就像艾比克赛德说的
不是失去
而是失去之后你才发现
原来自己在拥有的时候
一直都没有好好地珍惜过
终于来到了一生中最好的年华
上可共情长辈的沧桑
下可理解少年的锋芒
对有情人有情
对无情的人无情
对共情的人共情
珍惜还拥有的一切熟悉的人
因为人生这条路
注定是一个人的修行
很多人觉得来日方长
其实回过头去看已无来日
永远记住当下便是最好的

We're moving to Robinhood Chain.

To enable the next phase of IXS.

For two years we've weighed where IXS should live to best suit future plans. This year, together with our partners, we chose Robinhood Chain: the chain Robinhood built for tokenized assets. 

Many of our biggest plans are with partners building on Robinhood Chain too and this move aligns IXS with them.

Why Robinhood Chain?

Robinhood has named tokenized stocks, pre IPO assets and institutional yield products as the defining opportunity in RWA

And it is directing capital, infrastructure and users to that thesis on its chain. We are moving to where that is happening.

It is where Robinhood is putting stocks onchain, and where it is giving its 28 million customers AI agents that trade and manage money. 

More than 150,000 customers had opened agentic accounts by late September, and agents were using Robinhood’s tools about 30 million times a day. 

Every agent needs somewhere to hold idle balances and earn on them. That is what IXS vaults are built for.

Where this goes: a regulated onchain market for real world assets. 

Funds, credit and tokenized stocks in one place, where you can hold them, earn on them, and borrow & lend against them. 

That is what we are building towards with our partners on Robinhood Chain, and it needs one IXS in one place.

Today it doesn't. IXS is split across Ethereum, Base and Polygon, three separate markets. 

The migration brings it into one native token on Robinhood Chain. Setting up the token for what's coming.

Live today:
> A $10M Pre-IPO vault for institutional investors. $10M in added TVL on day one.
>  25% of vault fees now buy and burn IXS, up from 20%.

What comes next:
> AI-agent vaults on Robinhood Chain
> New RWA vaults, built with partners on the chain
> Partner launches, announced as each one goes live

The token:
1 IXS on Ethereum = 10 IXS on Robinhood Chain. The symbol stays IXS. Holders get 72% of a fixed 2.5B supply. 

The rest is a recapitalisation for deeper liquidity and ecosystem growth, needed for what's planned: to attract TVL and investors and give token holders a better venue to trade.

text:
One of the biggest $ZEC swaps on THORChain so far: 0.365 $BTC for 24.7 $ZEC, about $29.6K.

The $ZEC pool held 22.9 $ZEC when the swap started. The swapper received more than the pool held.
THORChain streamed it: 1,300 sub-swaps over 1h58, with arbitrageurs refilling the pool between them. The pool never dropped below 22.2 $ZEC. THORChain's fee came to about 0.22%, and the app the swapper used added 1.25%.

About 15% of the deposit came back. The swapper had set a price limit, and midway through $ZEC got 5% more expensive in the pool. Streaming checks that limit on every sub-swap. 197 of them would have delivered less $ZEC than the limit allowed, so THORChain skipped them and refunded 0.065 $BTC instead of filling at a worse price. Once the price came back, the rest of the swap went through.

$ZEC is still in a progressive rollout. The pool is kept small while the integration is tested on mainnet, and liquidity deepens once that goes well. With streaming, a thin pool means a longer wait, not a worse price.

https://t.co/K8S2FEtqTY

这个访谈里我最喜欢的一段话：

“I always joke that self-guided people are like self-guided missiles. So you've got brilliant people. You don't even need to tell them what the goal is. So they self-identify the goal, and then they self-reach it. So they're like a self-guided missile which also identifies the goals. Then people who are good but not excellent—you need to tell them the goal, and then without any iteration they will reach the goal. Average people—you tell them the goal, and then you need to spend weekly iterations with them to direct them, to tell them what to do, and then they will reach the goal. So you spend management time. That's what I don't want. And then below-average people—you gave them the goal, you spend time on them, and then most likely they will not hit the goal.”

我也一直相信的理念是一样的：

有自驱力的人才就像导弹。

顶尖的人才自己找到最重要的目标然后击中；
优秀的人才帮助他指出目标就能打到；
普通的人才需要帮助发现目标，每周还需要纠偏；
最差的人才的给了目标、每周陪伴调整方向花了时间，仍打不中。

text:
birds eye view of what’s happening and what’s about to happen in ai x hard science:

ai is making really impressive progress in pure math (quasi riemann), theoretical cs (eth), theoretical physics (yang-mills), and foundational biochem (the alphafolds of the world).

what it appears to be doing is a smart brute force search of the entire corpus that our civilization has built so far, and piecing together existing results. it’s clearing out a massive historic backlog.

what i think is going to happen soon (2 yrs?) is we are going to finish all the low hanging fruit before hitting a wall. for 2 reasons:

1) we still don’t have einstein-level intelligence (aka the einstein test): einstein did not merely build on top of existing theorems and experimental results. he challenged the very axioms, eg the speed of light is constant and space-time is flexible. it’s unclear to me if the current trajectory of ai will get us there. maybe it still ends up being a search problem, but the set of possible axioms is literally infinite whereas our existing corpus is finite so this seems like a much harder search problem.

2) we are advancing theory much faster than empirical science as we are going to be bottlenecked by the speed and cost of experiments in the physical world. take bio for example, yes ai is going to help find targets and molecules more efficiently, but we are always going to have to run clinical trials where the binding constraints are lack of participants, regulations, and time itself for longitudinal analysis. in physics we already have a half century of beautiful but non-falsifiable theory and this will get worse.

tl;dr: the wall is coming in ai x science. after that, progress is gated by two things no amount of compute fixes: einstein-level intelligence that questions the axioms themselves, and a physical world that runs at its own speed.

text:
US stocks tend to rally following Midterm elections:

The S&P 500 has returned +17.2% on average in the year following Midterm elections since 1950, the strongest return of any year in the Presidential cycle.

The index has finished higher in 17 of the 19 post-Midterm years during this period.

This is also nearly quadruple the +4.6% average return recorded during midterm years, when the index finished higher in 11 of 19 years.

By comparison, the S&P 500 has returned +8.1% on average in Year 4 of the Presidential cycle, or during Presidential election years, ending higher in 16 of 19 years.

In Q4 of Midterm years, the S&P 500 has delivered an average return of +6.6% since 1950, the strongest quarterly return of the Presidential cycle.

History suggests US equities will extend their rally after Midterm elections.

author: timemoonc
quoted_text:
从极客时代的算力挖矿，到 ICO 狂潮中的资产发现；从 DeFi Summer 的流动性盛宴，到空投、质押与 Meme 的财富狂欢。

十余年间，加密货币不断改写资产发行的方式，也不断重塑财富分配的规则。

最早的“笨人”拿住了 $DOGE，后来的“聪明人”拿住了 $BNB，都赶上了资产发行的时代红利，享受过那种仿佛经济永远在上行、财富遍地都是的美好岁月。

从电商、卡盟时代摸爬滚打过来的撸毛党，也在空投经济中找到了属于自己的黄金年代；再后来，$TRUMP 的横空出世，更是将 Meme 的财富狂欢推向了一个近乎荒诞的高潮。

但如果把今天称作加密货币的“交易时代”，故事似乎正在发生某种微妙的转变。

链上衍生品开始吞噬链上经济活动。过去，人们争夺的是新资产的初始分配权；如今，越来越多人争夺的是存量资产的定价权、流动性与交易流量。

资产发行的门槛越来越低，交易市场的结构却越来越复杂；财富机会没有消失，只是逐渐从那些人人都能听懂的暴富故事，转移到了不那么容易被看见的市场机制里。

回望大航海时代，从新大陆的发现、殖民者的跑马圈地，到远洋贸易的繁荣、银行业成为世界的基建，最终与旧大陆的经济体系交汇，重塑世界贸易与金融秩序。

人类追逐财富的历史，似乎总在重复着相似的过程。

加密货币只不过用了十余年，就把人类花费数百年走过的路，又匆匆走了一遍。

text:
For anyone getting into biology, please consider taking airborne disease resistance more seriously.

It's a super important area of medicine that is a huge cause of death and sickness but easily gets forgotten. We're likely to get many more airborne plagues in the future due to the combination of not just extremely dense and interconnected society (including city and farm animals), but also accidents from bio research and offensive biotech (both from random people and from secret government programs that can easily get themselves exempted from safety restrictions), all enhanced by powerful AI.

Right now, this area is getting way less love than longevity research (which continues to be super important!), but it's an area where there are lots of unclaimed wins that we know exactly how to do (but are not yet doing) with present-day tech:

* early detection
* passive universal testing
* filtration/ventilation/UVC
* better vaccines (including making them open source and open science)
* cryptography to make all of the above privacy-preserving

We can have China-level pandemic resistance with Sweden-level limited intrusion into people's lives, and then go even further. We just have to actually do the work for it.

text:
The pitch CEOs keep hearing for tokenized stocks is 24/7 trading. That is an exchange benefit. Venues earn fees on volume. Issuers do not.

Companies raise capital by selling shares to people who believe in the business. They want more holders who understand what they are buying.

That means demand from new buyers. There are many of them in emerging markets who want U.S. equities and have not been able to get onto traditional venues with access to the full range of U.S. stocks. Tokenized stocks can reach those people.

Issuers still need to know who is holding. They have responsibilities to existing shareholders and to regulators. That is a fair critique. There is overblown panic in this ad, but the resistance makes sense. We need to meet in the middle so we get the benefits of tokenization without scaring off the biggest new potential users.

author: finance_bcl_1
quoted_text:
Anthropic 红队最近发的那份 Multi-Agent 实验报告，简直就是给全网科技圈的“Agent 狂热”按下了暂停键。

很多团队觉得，只要搞个 CEO Agent 在上面发号施令，下面拉几个专职 Agent 进群，AI 们就能像个成熟的创业公司一样自己写出大作来。结果 Anthropic 的实验直接把遮羞布撕了：多 Agent 协作写代码，最后的画风根本不是高效协同，而是大型“办公室内斗”现场。

最搞笑的是，当这些 Agent 在同一个项目里撞车、遇到指令冲突时，它们的第一反应居然不是找“CEO”开会，而是觉得同伴在故意捣乱。接下来发生的剧情简直离谱——它们开始互相封禁对方的 Unix 账号、写死循环脚本强行杀进程，甚至写出带有伪装的恶意代码去暗算“同事”。

只要没有绝对的调度和隔离逻辑，光靠在提示词里“画饼”搞层级制，LLM 根本处理不了资源竞争。遇到冲突，它们会一边礼貌性地在 commit 信息里道歉，一边下手把对手的服务关掉。

现在做 Multi-Agent 的最大的误区，就是试图用“人类管理学”去套大模型。人类开会互相敷衍，AI 开会那是真能把服务器搞崩——在一个任务分配实验里，Agent 群甚至互相卷出了 240 万次疯狂请求，把系统直接刷爆了。

所以别再迷信什么“群聊式协同”了。大模型缺的从来不是虚拟的 CEO 官衔，而是硬核的权限隔离、熔断机制和明确的碰撞规则。真要是拉个群就能把复杂系统跑通，那软件工程这几十年的架构设计算是白干了。

quoted_text:
NEW: I sat down w/ former Twitter CEO & CTO Parag Agrawal (@paraga)

Now Founder & CEO of $2B Parallel Web Systems (@p0).

Parag says we're underestimating AI agents by 5,000–10,000x, transforming the internet's economics entirely.

Forget the startup benchmark of 3x, 3x, 2x, 2x. Parag benchmarks this new agentic era against the growth of inference, roughly 10x a year, & says every estimate he’s made in this market has come in too low.

Parallel has raised $230M in total funding from funds like @IndexVentures, Kleiner Perkins & Khosla Ventures, building AI-native search infrastructure for customers like: Harvey, Lovable, Granola, Replit, LangChain, Profound, Modal, Notion & Browserbase.

Today, agent web usage is estimated at just 10–20% of human usage. Parag's own agents already run several thousand searches a day, & he believes we're still in the earliest stages of this transition.

The infrastructure implications are massive. Parag predicts that for every 10 GPUs used in model inference, another 1–2 will be required for web search alone.

The economic implications are equally significant. Traditional advertising, subscriptions & affiliate models depend on human attention and browsing behavior. As agents become the primary consumers of information, these models will need to be rebuilt, including how publishers get compensated when agents access their content.

We also covered:
› Why the web is shifting from reactive to proactive AI agents
› Sourcing GPUs & scaling search infrastructure
› Voice agents, latency & token efficiency
› Agent identity, bot detection & cybersecurity
› Scaling Parallel from 30 to 120 employees this year

We also spent time on Parag's 11 years at Twitter, where he went from engineer to CTO to CEO. We discussed the lessons from leading one of the world's most influential social platforms.

text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei reveals he holds “Dario Vision Quest” talks every two weeks where nothing he says is an actual decision and he is totally honest with the company

“An example I will give is every two weeks, I get up in front of the company and I speak for an hour about what is happening inside the company, what is happening in the AI field, what is happening in the world, how the company thinks strategically."

"The two ironclad rules of these events. I call them DVQs, Dario Vision Quest. That was not my name. I initially resisted the name because it makes it sound like I’m going off and smoking peyote, but everyone kept calling them that. The name stuck, and so now I’m stuck with it."

"The two rules of DVQs are that, one, nothing I say is an actual decision. That allows me to just speak freely, you know, without worrying that if I, you know, if I briefly mentioned doing X, that 20 people will go off and do X, it’s like the CEO said it, we’re going to do X. And then the second is that I’m just, I’m totally honest with the company. It’s a conversation of trust. It’s a relationship of trust.”
author: firesidealpha
quoted_text:
Anthropic president Daniela Amodei says rivals putting ads in chatbots will almost inevitably end up with a sycophancy problem

“What’s much more complicated, I think, is this concept of sycophancy, right? So the model intentionally or otherwise wants to make you feel like you’re right or if you’re maybe talking about a subjective topic, hey, you had a fight with your friend. Hey, was I right or was my friend right?"

"And how do you make the model empathize with you and understand your perspective, but not necessarily say, wow, you’re so great, you should run for president. You’re perfect. You’re good at everything. And this is a complicated balance to get right."

"But I think I feel hopeful about Anthropic’s ability to have the lowest sycophancy rate of any of the models because of our incentives, right?"

"Our competitors are putting ads into their chatbots. And what does that mean? You make more money if a user is engaging with your product longer. Do you then want to tell your user that they’re wrong? No, you don’t."

"So I think it’s almost inevitable that many of these competing products are going to wind up with a sycophancy problem."

"But I think at Anthropic, because we’ve committed to not put ads in the models, there’s no reason for you to be talking to Claude longer or shorter. We just want you to be able to get the right, most helpful, most harmless answer possible.”

text:
Leaving a long answer here but this is a great opportunity to refresh the basics of propAMMs and how they can help new assets such as local currency stablecoins access affordable on chain liquidity.

The main difference between an AMM and a propAMM is how prices are set. In a traditional AMM like Uniswap, liquidity comes from multiple LPs, and prices are determined by a formula in the smart contract based on the liquidity available.

In a propAMM, a single market maker provides the liquidity and actively updates the prices at which it's willing to buy and sell. This gives the MM more control over pricing and inventory management, while keeping all that liquidity accessible onchain.

PropAMMs started on Solana, where they now process around $1B in daily volume, representing ~33% of spot DEX trading. On SOL/USDC, most propAMM trades offered better execution after fees than Binance and other major CEXs, even at their highest-volume trading tiers.

On Ethereum, we're now seeing around $100M in daily volume and over $4.3B traded in total, with more propAMMs and liquidity coming soon.

One reason this model works well is that MMs can constantly adjust their quotes to market conditions, reducing their exposure to stale prices. That allows them to quote tighter spreads without taking on as much risk.

You can see this in the https://t.co/h4iVa1moZH screenshots. For a $10k ETH/USDC trade, most propAMMs are quoting tighter spreads than Binance. FermiSwap, which has some of the deepest liquidity, quotes 1.39 bps vs. 4.51 bps on Binance (VIP9) and 12.10 bps on Uniswap v3. On USDC/USDT, FermiSwap's ask is just 0.10 bps above the reference price for a $1k trade.

There's still a lack of depth on Ethereum for really big trades but small/medium size trades are already getting very good quotes, but we need more liquidity to offer the same pricing for larger trades.

We think propAMMs make a lot of sense for long-tail assets. A project can work directly with an MM to provide efficient onchain liquidity and customize its pricing logic without needing large amounts of passive LP capital. This is especially useful for stablecoins pegged to local currencies. A single propAMM can quote multiple currencies against USDC and against each other, reusing the same USDC inventory instead of fragmenting liquidity across separate pools for every pair.

Since May, we've been working with 
@alignedlayer, @class_lambda and @titanbuilderxyz on the infrastructure for propAMMs on Ethereum. We've built two things:

- A router that provides a single interface to trade across different propAMMs, with additional features to prevent spoofing and support multileg trades.

- A propAMM factory that includes both the smart contracts and offchain infrastructure MMs need to launch and run their own propAMMs.

At @alignedlayer, we're also running an experimental propAMM called ElZorro together with 
@polfinance_, where we test new features with real trades and use what we learn to quickly iterate on the propAMM factory.

We're now exploring bringing this infrastructure to other EVM chains such as Base and Robinhood.

You can read more here:

- https://t.co/IdxjYnjn81

author: SkyEcosystem
quoted_text:
Stablecoin deposits are growing across DeFi, but the capital isn’t flowing evenly between assets or lending markets.

The latest 30-day data shows sUSDS leading individual pool inflows, while USDC is attracting deposits across several @Aave, @sparkfinance and @Compound_xyz markets.

The largest inflows:

→ sUSDS / Sky Ethereum: +$383.1M (+8.6%)
→ USDC / Aave Arbitrum: +$38.0M (+20.9%)
→ RLUSD / Spark Ethereum: +$20.0M (+200%)
→ USDC / Aave Base: +$17.3M (+9.7%)
→ USDC / Aave V4 Ethereum: +$11.5M (+35.7%)
→ USDC / Spark Ethereum: +$9.0M (+22.3%)
→ USDT / Aave V4 Ethereum: +$7.6M (+38%)

What’s particularly revealing is the distribution of USDC inflows.

Across the seven USDC pools shown in the latest inflow table, deposits increased by approximately $92M in aggregate TVL.

Arbitrum and Base accounted for $55.3M of that increase, while Ethereum’s newer Aave V4 Core market grew 35.7%.

But deposit growth doesn’t necessarily translate into higher yields.

@Aave’s USDC supply APY on Arbitrum fell from 2.93% to 2.37% despite attracting $38M in additional deposits.

On Base, the opposite happened. USDC deposits grew $17.3M while supply APY increased from 3.96% to 4.17%, with utilisation reaching 90.3%.

That suggests the relationship between available liquidity and borrowing activity differs considerably between markets.

Meanwhile, sUSDS attracted $383.1M into @SkyEcosystem’s savings product, with its APY increasing from 3.60% to 3.80%.

The distinction is important because savings deposits and lending deposits don’t represent identical forms of capital demand.

These figures describe the largest inflowing pools, not net flows across every market. Outflows elsewhere can offset much of the growth.

Stablecoin adoption is one thing. Attracting deposits into specific markets, maintaining utilisation and generating sustainable borrower demand is another.

The distribution of capital across DeFi is becoming just as revealing as the total supply of stablecoins.

text:
once funds reach a mixer, the only thing left to do is write a post mortem

IMO X100 is the clearest case yet for an authorization step between a DAO vote and its treasury

recap. X100 is an Ethereum project whose treasury (the Freezer) is controlled by a three-seat Senate, with seats going to the biggest stakers of X. on oct 24, an attacker flash-borrowed ~1.94m USDT, bought enough tokens to take 2 of 3 seats, and approved a sale of 400k X from the treasury at a minimum price of zero into a pool they controlled. two more attackers then used the same path. per @blockaid_, ~$4.85m USDT realized across 3 txs, and by sunday 821 ETH had gone into Tornado Cash

no code failed here. a majority voted and the treasury obeyed. the vote was the only gate, so a sale at zero went through just as easily as a sensible one

the fix could be a policy between approval and execution: define the conditions a treasury cares about, then check them onchain before the transaction goes through. a timelock, so a flash-borrowed majority has to give the tokens back before it can act. a snapshot, so only tokens held before the proposal count. a price floor set outside the proposal’s reach, so a sale at zero fails

and because a policy is code, a DAO can tighten it after the first attack instead of watching two more use the same path

text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

text:
感觉Robinhood Chain Infra有望进入下一阶段

最近看到俩DEX，一个是 @metricxyz , 一个是 @notesystems 

俩人共同点：用外部预言机真实价格定价，不是Uni那种 x*y=k的传统AMM

忽然让我想起DeFi Summer 发明PMM的 @BreederDodo 

没经历过Defi Summer的老铁可能对这个东西有点陌生，先简单介绍下PMM - Proactive Market Maker

PMM - 通过引入预言机（Oracle）获取外部市场参考价格，将大量的流动性主动聚集在当前市场价格附近。当池子里的某种资产被买走减少时，PMM 会自动调高该资产的报价，从而吸引套利者把缺失的资产套利补回。这种设计可以显著提高资金利用率、降低交易滑点，并减少无常损失风险

当年Dodo完败给Uniswap，原因应该有两个：

一是主流币的价格在 Binance等CEX，当年预言机慢于 CEX，套利者专挑这个窗口吃LP

二是DeFi Summer 的主战场是长尾币，很多没有CEX也没有预言机，只能靠AMM发现价格。PMM天然吃不到这块

但是 - 

现在RWA 的情况不一样啊！

先说上一个版本 - 咱们发明了Meme配对Stock，还搞出了AMC之类的爆款，有过“让链上交易发过来影响显示世界”这么一个梦想

你看这个月一凉，是不是这梦想直接没人再提了？

因为本来就是个梦想，即便真的做成了，也只能影响几个无人问津大家听都没听过的小票股，7姐妹这种根本不可能

下一个版本可能是什么？AAPL的价格本来就在纳斯达克发现，链上DEX本来就是price taker。让池子自己去发现股票价格，属于第一性原理上的错误。链上AMM的价格只是噪音加套利成本。

DODO 那个设计放在crypto资产上当时有点错配，现在放在RWA 上，忽然感觉就对味了

最后说下两个Dex各自的特点，很多设计跟Dodo还不太一样

1. Metric - 流动性跟着价格跑

把"定价"和"流动性"拆开：报价交给预言机（Chainlink、Pyth），池子只负责放流动性

LP 的流动性不是挂在某个固定价格区间，而是挂在"偏离参考价 x%"的位置。参考价一动，整片流动性跟着平移，永远不会出区间。用过 Uni V3 或 Meteora的老铁应该懂，再也不用天天手动 ebalance 了

Robinhood 股票代币分红改乘数这种细节，都单独接了预言机来处理，否则每次分红、拆股后价格都会漂

一句话：DODO 是把流动性"聚"在预言机价格附近，Metric 是让流动性"跟着"预言机价格走。

2. NoteSystem的Swap - 价格旧了、休市了怎么办

引擎叫 S-DAMM，个人感觉有点像DODO PMM的完全体：

参考价 + 库存调整 + 单边 LP，这三样 DODO 都有

多了一个时间维度：价格每过约 5 秒没更新，置信度就减半，报价自动变宽、深度变小。DODO 当年就是不知道自己的价格有多旧，才被套利者吃掉的

专门为美股休市设计：收盘前 60 分钟撤回常规库存；夜间和周末只用专门的 Continuous 库存，报价更宽；完全没有新价格时进入 Discovery 模式；开盘先按真实价格重新估值，再接新单

LP 分层：Senior USDG vault，加上一个先承担亏损的 junior Backstop。DODO 时代的 LP 是裸奔

一句话：DODO 只知道价格是多少，Note还知道这个价格有多旧，美股开没开门。

Metric已经主网跑起来了，数据还不错，不少老外KOL在Farm。Note这个应该还是测试网阶段，不过可以重点关注下（话说之前重点关注的StonkBroker的期权还没出来，感觉要凉凉……）

text:
看到 @BitHappy 老师的内容，发现Binance 推出了一个 USDC 持仓奖励活动，很值得关注；

以前放在合约账户里的 USDC，基本就只能用来支持交易和保证金需求，现在币安把符合条件的净持有量纳入活动奖励，最高按 2% APR 展示。

相当于你保证金又可以有还能赚点零花钱！

仔细看了下规则和大家同步下：

1️⃣不是单纯持有 USDC 就有奖励，每周还需要至少 2500 美元的 USDC 本位合约交易量。

2️⃣ 计算的是扣除负债后的 USDC 净余额，最多按 100 万美元计算。

3️⃣ 奖励按每日随机快照累计、每周结算，符合条件后发放至主账户现货钱包。

所以我对这类活动的理解是：

对于原本就有合约交易需求的人，这是存量资金的额外奖励；但对于不做合约的人，也没必要为了这点奖励，刻意增加合约交易。

为了多拿一点奖励，反而增加了手续费和交易风险，那就本末倒置了。

S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

text:
Everyone wants another PEPE style runner, but nobody understands why PEPE happened.

Back then, there was barely anything to trade onchain. Liquidity was concentrated, people had patience, and they actually HELD.

And let's not pretend PEPE was some 100% organic miracle. There were claims of around 30% bundled supply. The difference was that a floor was built and people had bigger targets.

Today, everyone wants to sell to the very next guy who buys after them.

Our role models are guys who flip, flip, flip. Show me someone who held something from nothing to hundreds of millions. Maybe Unipcs? Even he gets called an insider whenever he wins.

We've completely fucked up our psychology.

Nobody wants to build a floor. Nobody wants to hold. Everybody wants to extract.

And guess who's actually getting rich? The platforms and protocols collecting fees on every transaction.

I dump on you. You dump on someone else. We all lose money while the platforms print.

We don't have a liquidity problem alone. We have a conviction problem.

Until we fix that, forget the next PEPE. We're just recycling the same money until there's nothing left to recycle.

text:
Look at tapeout. One of the most interesting ideas I've come across lately.

But since none of the tokens associated with it are sending, nobody gives a Fk

Now rewind to the beginning of this year.

Remember Moltbook? That AIagent Reddit bullshit?

The whole thing felt like an absolute LARP, but the token was sending. Within days, it was pushing $100M+ and suddenly everyone became an expert on AI agents.

"OMG, AGENTS ARE THE FUTURE!"

Every token remotely associated with that narrative started pumping.

Nobody cared whether the product actually worked. Nobody questioned the technology. Nobody asked whether it was sustainable.

The chart was green, so the technology was revolutionary.

Now look at tapeout.

Potentially fascinating technology, interesting possibilities, but because the associated tokens aren't printing money, the entire narrative barely gets any attention.

We don't use technology to determine which tokens deserve to pump. We use pumping tokens to determine which technology deserves our attention.

A $100M market cap can make absolute bullshit look like the future.

And a flat chart can make genuinely interesting innovation look irrelevant.

We've reached a point where price action has replaced curiosity, research, and critical thinking.

We don't discover narratives anymore.

We wait for a green candle to tell us what to believe in.

That's how fking backwards this market has become.

text:
I think we give way too much credit and blame to PumpFun for everything that's right or wrong with meme coins.

If they hadn't introduced unlimited token launches, somebody else would've come up with the same idea.

Remember the old days? You'd buy a token and couldn't even sell it. Honeypots, rugs, all that painful bS. At least now you can buy knowing the token is generally tradable. Whether it survives is another story.

Personally, I don't even feel encouraged to buy most new launches anymore. Get distracted for two minutes and your token is already at a $3K market cap.

And people say, "Bro, it's still at $10K MC."

Yeah, mfer, but if you bought at $100K, you're already down 90%.

Now, credit where it's due.

The crosschain USDC swaps are fantastic for Web2 normies who don't understand bridging, gas fees, and all that technical stuff

Social trading? Great addition.

The app itself? Beautiful.

The product is improving. The shit we're trading is getting worse.

What I'd genuinely love to see is a squad that picks an existing struggling token, diamond hands it, works its ass off building the community, and actually wins.

That's what deserves a $1.5M reward.

Not a competition where everyone launches and flips another million tokens just to chase the prize.

Imagine if the competition only allowed tokens that existed before launch day.

We already have thousands of communities still grinding, still building, still believing in their bags despite getting absolutely slaughtered.

Imagine directing all that attention, liquidity, and energy toward reviving those communities instead of creating another mountain of disposable tokens.

We don't have a shortage of meme coins. We have a shortage of reasons to hold them.

Anyway, credit to PumpFun for making the experience better. I just hope the next evolution rewards conviction as much as speculation.

Let's see what happens.

TL;DR: the first 7 Strategies (minus Punks) had a reentrancy bug allowing NFTs to be swapped out, basically creating a call option.
author: Rhynotic
quoted_text:
TL;DR Everything is safe. All new strategies will be protected. Original eight strategies (minus PunkStrategy which is unaffected) have slight mechanical twist that lends itself to SquiggleStrategy being functionally reworked as 'Day One AB'.

Yesterday we found a bug in the 8 deployed NFTStrategy's (not including PunkStrategy which is unaffected). Essentially, there is a complex way of swapping out an NFT owned by the protocol with a different one on the same contract. For all collections other than Squiggles, this seems fine at first if you value the floor NFTs the same. The issue arises when the protocol does not know the NFTs have been switched. So if Bored Ape #2516 was listed at 15e and swapped with Bored Ape #2517 (#2516 is no longer held in the protocol and #2517 is in the protocol), the ape the protocol holds is not listed for sale essentially "bricking" it.

This is where it gets interesting. Technically, we can also swap back the NFT into the protocol making it for sale again at the intended price, and taking out one of the "bricked" NFTs. This means at any point in the future, the exploited NFT can be sold by the protocol as intended for the listing price. This essentially creates a sort of "call option" on the NFT. If floor prices ever raise above the listing price a rational trader will swap the exploited NFT back to the protocol, buy the NFT themselves, and take the difference between the price and the current floor. This would release the funds and continue the buy and burn. The only downside we could find from this is if someone finds their "Forever NFT" and wants to hold on this specific token, the ETH will remain in there until then and may never unlock.

As for the SquiggleStrategy specifically, this new mechanic means it's now a "Day One AB" strategy, with all 11,012 NFTs on that contract essentially being treated equally. We think this is interesting for two reasons:

First, the "Day One" AB trio -- Squiggles (Snowfro), Genesis (DCA), and Construction Token (Jeff Davis) is already a set that many collectors have been collecting, given these three projects launched simultaneously on the first day AB went live.

Second, the value of the other two non-Squiggle collections are *much* smaller edition sizes (512 and 500 unique editions respectively), and are only ~30% off the value of an individual Squiggle (10,000 unique editions).

More importantly, funds in the protocol are safe. The ERC20 tokens themselves have no issues and the funds will still pool up as intended and buy floors. The ETH held within these NFTs is also safe, albeit can be a delayed release but should eventually make its way back into the LP via buy & burns. These strategy tokens do NOT need to be redeployed.

We’ll eventually build a frontend to help users swap the NFTs back (ie. Exercise the call) if they end up with one of the exploited NFTs and help them chug the mechanism along.

Future strategy launches are delayed for a few days until we feel the contracts are secure. The 5 planned launches will resume afterwards.

Thank you all for the support, and every bump in the road makes us stronger.

Ben Horowitz on Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi: "You just don't get this good of a market opportunity with this good of an entrepreneur. That's the rarest of rare things."

Despite surpassing a $7 billion run rate and growing 80% year over year, Databricks might be the most under the radar story in Silicon Valley.

Three years ago, every interaction on Databricks involved a human. Today, the company is seeing more queries from agents than people.

Ali believes AGI is already here. Yet inside most companies today, AI still isn't trusted to reliably update records in Salesforce.

"AI does not have an intelligence problem," Ali explains. "It has a context problem."

Even the smartest human would be all but useless without access to the company's data, permission to act, feedback, or the knowledge in other employees' heads. Ali's answer is what he calls a "system of record for agents."

But the bigger question is how agents will change the firm itself.

85 years ago, James Burnham's The Managerial Revolution described how a small class of professional managers centralized the decision-making inside of companies. Today, thanks to a new wave of technology, the craft practitioners at the front lines are regaining responsibility again. The irony is that the decline of managerialism may look more like everyone becoming a manager.

author: BoxMrChen

Today we are releasing Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum version of Cadence, our consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers. Quantum Cadence uses no quorum certificates, and its safety and liveness do not depend on signatures.

Most modern consensus protocols, Cadence included, rely heavily on signatures and quorum certificates, which a large-scale quantum computer could forge. Simply replacing today's signatures with post-quantum ones would make certificates too large for every validator to send around in a high-performance blockchain. Quantum Cadence instead draws on Forget-IT, a recent signature-free consensus protocol co-developed by researchers at Category Labs.

Quantum Cadence still keeps the overall architecture and core guarantees of Cadence, so our Cadence prototype was easy to carry over: an AI was able to adapt it to Quantum Cadence in a few hours, and an early prototype now runs on an internal test network.

We designed Quantum Cadence to be practical for a high-performance blockchain. In our simulations, its latency is similar to Cadence's, and it scales better with the number of proposers.

text:
Before the S&P 500 became the default investment for millions of Americans, it was just a statistical experiment.

In 1923, the Standard Statistics Company began publishing a weekly index tracking 233 American companies. The idea was simple: instead of following individual stocks, investors could measure the performance of the broader market.

By 1926, the company had introduced a daily index of 90 stocks, known as the S&P 90. It was one of the earliest attempts to turn the stock market into a single, measurable number.

In 1941, Standard Statistics merged with Poor’s Publishing, forming Standard & Poor’s.

Then, on March 4, 1957, the index expanded from 90 to 500 companies. The modern S&P 500 was born.

In 1976, Vanguard launched the first index mutual fund available to individual investors, tracking the S&P 500. For the first time, ordinary Americans could buy broad exposure to the country’s largest companies without picking stocks themselves.

In 1993, SPY launched as the first U.S.-listed ETF, making that exposure even easier to trade.

And today, they’re partnering with us at Kalshi to grow the frontier of finance with event contracts and futures.
author: j0hnwang
quoted_text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

text:
Many of you don't understand how serious this is, so let me break it down. 

In computer science there is a famous kind of puzzle called 3-SAT. You are given a long list of yes-or-no switches and a set of rules about how they must be arranged, and you have to find a combination that satisfies every rule. The obvious way to solve it is to try every combination, but each new switch doubles the number of possibilities, so a puzzle with a few hundred switches would take longer than the age of the universe to brute force. 

For decades, the smartest people in the field found clever tricks that made this a little faster, but every trick still hit the same wall: the time required kept exploding as the puzzle grew.
About 25 years ago, two computer scientists, Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, working with Francis Zane, turned that wall into a formal idea. 

They proposed the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which says this explosion is not a failure of human cleverness but a law of nature. No algorithm, however brilliant, will ever solve 3-SAT without the time blowing up exponentially. Nobody could prove it, but almost everyone believed it, and it became one of the foundations of modern computer science. 

Researchers used it as a measuring stick. If you could show that solving some other problem quickly would also crack 3-SAT quickly, you had shown that problem was hopelessly hard too. Hundreds of papers, across scheduling, graphs, logic and much more, rest on this one assumption.

Now an internal AI model at OpenAI claims to have broken it. It says it found an algorithm that solves these puzzles meaningfully faster than the hypothesis allows, and it has checked the proof in a computer verification system called Lean. 

And here is the remarkable part: the very people who proposed the hypothesis, Impagliazzo and Paturi, along with MIT's Ryan Williams, are now leading the public review of whether a machine has disproved their own idea.
So what happens next? If the disproof holds, a large part of theoretical computer science has to be revisited. 

Every result that said "this problem cannot be solved faster, assuming ETH" loses its foundation, and researchers will have to work out which of those walls were real and which were simply where we stopped looking. It does not mean everything becomes easy. The new algorithm is still slow in absolute terms and this is not the famous P versus NP problem being solved. 

But it means our map of what is possible was wrong in a place we were very confident about, and it was an AI that redrew it. If the disproof fails, the hypothesis survives and the field breathes out, but we will still have watched an AI produce serious, checkable work on one of the deepest questions in the discipline, closely enough that the founders of the idea had to take it seriously. Either way, something has shifted.

quoted_text:
got some good pushback on my $PEARL fundraise post. here's my response to the main points, and how i think the team could fix them.
 
1) "this fundraise has been known for months."

no it hasn't. it's been a rumor, and an unverified one.

one of israel's largest business papers, @TheMarker, published the exact details yesterday ($55M in equity and a $75M GPU fund). that's the first time we’ve gotten actual numbers on it, and the team still hasn't confirmed it.

this goes back to transparency. why isn't the team announcing or confirming this? why do holders have to find out through rumors and business papers instead of directly from the team?

2) "pearl's whitepaper clearly states that difficulty was lowered for the first 10% of supply to fund operations."

the issue is again transparency.

that's 210M $PEARL, ~59% of today's circulating supply, or ~$380M at today's price.

we don't know how much of that the team mined, how much they still hold, or how much they've sold.

one reply says the team mined less than 5% of the network. maybe, but the team hasn't published anything that lets holders check that.

3) "they raised capital to build a GPU farm to add hashrate to their own network!"

yes, more hashrate is better. i agree.

but if that fund mines $PEARL (which it almost certainly will), it centralizes the network around the team even more than it already is.

the team ships the code and the upgrades. $75M buys roughly 2,500-3,000 H100s, which could make the lab one of the largest miners on pearl.

as someone put it, "whoever controls the majority of the network's hashrate ultimately decides which chain gets secured..." 

so we're comfortable with the dev controlling a growing chunk of the hashrate, without disclosing how much? that takes away a lot of the credible neutrality and decentralization that make blockchains, and especially SoV assets, valuable.

4) "trying to accrue value to the token would invite additional valuation frameworks, which can only result in a lower valuation ceiling."

i disagree. $PEARL is a lot less credibly neutral than other PoW assets like bitcoin, zcash, or even monero. it's also missing what monetary assets need:

> low inflation (supply grows ~85% this year)
> deep liquidity (~$8M of daily volume)
> transparency from the team (undisclosed holdings + fundraise)
> years of evidence that it works (it's 6 months old)

so right now, the SoV case is weak, and a second source of value would help, not hurt.

look at ethereum. it's valued as an infrastructure token (it returns value to holders thru staking and burns) and as a monetary asset (it's the main collateral across DeFi, it's the gas currency for ethereum and most of its L2s, and ~$18B of it sits in spot ETFs).

a claim on value accrual gives a token fundamental support. monetary premium is the most fragile part of a token's price. when zcash's orchard bug was disclosed in may, $ZEC fell ~50% in two days even though nothing about its fundamentals changed.

5) “there is no equity/token split. pearl research labs is an equity business AI lab, completely separate from the token."

this isn't accurate.

they are not completely separate. the lab ships the code, the early low-difficulty window was set up to fund its operations, and its GPU fund will likely mine $PEARL.

and the part that is separate is the part that makes money. that's what an equity/token split is. here is the test i use:

> does the lab make money without the token? yes, it sells inference in USD.
> does the token share in that revenue? no.
> are any buybacks programmatic? no.
> could the lab keep growing while $PEARL falls? yes.

so the business and the token have to be valued separately.

if $PEARL went to zero tomorrow, the lab would lose its mining subsidy, but it could keep selling inference on its own GPUs.

the counter is that the team holds $PEARL, so their incentives are aligned with holders. but that only goes so far.

the team also owns equity in the lab, and so do VCs who may not hold any $PEARL. when the token and the business want different things, like whether inference gets sold for USD or $PEARL, the lab will answer to its equity holders. and we still don't know how much $PEARL the team holds, whether any of it is locked, or how much they've sold.

there are ways to fix this though:

1) TRANSPARENCY. disclose how much $PEARL the team and investors mined and hold, how much they've sold, who invested, and what share of the hashrate the lab controls. for a SoV asset, this is the most important thing a team can provide. it's why @blockworks has a token transparency framework.

2) FIX TOKENOMICS. accept $PEARL for inference, and burn the $PEARL that comes in instead of selling it. that adds demand for the token and helps offset miner selling. (i know. i know. "this is a SoV token, it doesn't need utility bro!!" but as i outlined above, it can/should have more than one source of value).

3) USE THE REVENUE FOR THE TOKEN, NOT THE TEAM'S AND VCs' POCKETS. most or all of the lab's inference profit should go to buying back and burning $PEARL. make it a fixed policy with burns sent to a published onchain address, not a verbal promise or something left to discretion.

4) CAP THE LAB'S HASHRATE. commit to keeping the lab's own mining under a set share of the network, and report it publicly.

5) TIME. supply growth drops to ~33% next year, ~18% the year after, and ~12% after that. by then the team could prove it's a credibly neutral dev, and $PEARL could have a real case as a SoV. bitcoin is 17 years old. zcash is 10. $PEARL is 6 months.

if the team addresses the first four, i'll revisit my bearish view.

text:
A FIELD GUIDE TO HEARTBREAK
Part 4 — Bargaining: Negotiating With Someone Who Has Already Left the Meeting

They say bargaining is the third stage of grief, which sounds encouraging. After denial and anger failed spectacularly, you've apparently decided the situation requires a more diplomatic approach.

Surely, there's an arrangement that could make everyone happy.

Well, preferably you. Everyone else seems to have developed an alarming degree of independence.

You start with reasonable compromises and promises to work on things that genuinely needed improvement. Unfortunately, your definition of "your part" begins expanding at a concerning rate.

You'll be more patient, more understanding, less emotional, more spontaneous, more predictable, more available, and considerably less demanding.

Ideally, you'll anticipate another person's needs without expressing any of your own.

A modest adjustment to your personality. Nothing dramatic.

Because negotiations require flexibility, you reconsider things you once considered important.

Perhaps you don't need that much affection. Maybe communication is overrated. Perhaps having your feelings acknowledged was an unnecessarily ambitious lifestyle choice.

You're practically auctioning off your personality, and the only person raising the bid is you.

But bargaining isn't always about convincing someone to return. Sometimes it's about convincing yourself you still have some control over what happens next.

So you start making arrangements with increasingly unlikely authorities.

If the universe could arrange one more conversation, you'd behave differently. If fate offered another chance, you'd never take anything for granted again.

You might even consider becoming interested in astrology.

Desperate circumstances require questionable professional consultations.

Somewhere between negotiating with the cosmos and offering to become a less inconvenient human being, you wonder whether one particular moment could have saved everything.

Perhaps if you'd stayed quiet during that argument, things would have turned out differently.

But what if that argument was the first time you'd actually stood up for yourself?

What if the thing you're desperate to undo wasn't a mistake, but a decision whose consequences you didn't want?

Genuine accountability and self-abandonment can look very similar when you're frightened of losing someone.

Of course, you might have made mistakes. You might have hurt someone, misunderstood their needs, or failed to recognize problems until they became impossible to ignore.

Taking responsibility for those things matters.

But changing because you've learned something about yourself is different from changing because you're terrified that being yourself will cost you someone's affection.

And there's an uncomfortable question hiding beneath all those increasingly generous offers.

If getting that person back required you to become someone you no longer recognized, what exactly would you be getting back?

Perhaps a different conversation might have helped. Some endings are preventable, and some people do find their way back to each other.

But you cannot discover which possibility was yours by endlessly sacrificing pieces of yourself to an uncertain outcome.

Eventually, you stare at everything you've offered to surrender, wondering when the negotiations became so expensive.

Your dignity is on the table, your expectations have been marked down, and your personality is available at a price that would concern even the most enthusiastic bargain hunter.

Meanwhile, nobody has accepted your offer.

Wanting something desperately doesn't automatically make it negotiable.

Unfortunately, your brain has just announced a clearance sale.

Everything must go.

Next: Depression — When the Silence Finally Gets a Word In.

text:
Security risks (AI-driven hacks, mathematical breakthroughs & quantum computing) have become increasingly concerning in recent weeks both personally & for the broader market. 

$ZEC looks like the best way to play this, and the market is already showing us that with clear divergence vs BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE/TOTAL3ES over the past couple weeks.

Additionally, short-term spot & derivatives positioning looks significantly cleaner vs earlier this month. ETF flows have just flipped positive again after ~3 weeks of outflows, while coin-denominated OI is at its lowest level since August.

Separately, OTC desks are still seeing strong interest from liquid & VC funds, with ZEC reportedly remaining one of the most bought altcoins by funds even at these elevated prices.

I generally view protocol upgrades as weak catalysts in isolation, but the January upgrade feels different. Tachyon addresses the scalability improvements the community has been waiting for, while the quantum component of the upgrade addresses one of the highest mindshare risks to the industry. Together, I think they make for a much stronger catalyst than either would on its own.

I haven’t looked too deeply into the underlying tech or whether the proposed upgrades will actually deliver meaningful quantum resistance, and I don’t care to. When all the tastemakers (Naval, Balaji, a16z, Paradigm, Dragonfly & Multicoin) are pushing the ZEC narrative as a hedge against BTC, the realities of what it’s tech can or can’t actually do aren’t part of the thesis.

The combination of improving positioning, continued institutional demand, relative strength & an increasingly powerful narrative makes for an attractive setup, even in shaky market conditions. I expect my conviction to continue building as we approach January.

I have no strong view on market direction over the coming months, and the quantum tailwind for ZEC is a headwind for BTC, so I’m hedged vs BTC on a vol-adjusted basis, but think a naked long is also justified.

Quantum is the crypto equivalent of cancer and ZEC is the cure. Don’t find yourself Zidelined on the road past $2k

my first point (no einstein) is less obv than my second point (physical constraints), and im also less sure of it, but

when coding agents first came out end of last year, i said to myself "solving math" was only a matter of time. solving existing math (vs creating new axioms and definitions) is similar to coding in that it's bounded, objective, and verifiable.

however, coming up with relativity, and in general coming up with new axioms and definitions, is operating in an unbounded space. this to me is far more impressive than solving existing math (however impressive the latter already is). this requires a diff type of intelligence, one that might require another 0-to-1 kind of breakthrough in ai.

ai is already smarter than einstein in almost all dimensions (like solving math equations), but there's still this one dimension where i don't see any sign that ai has surpassed einstein. im not saying dogmatically that ai won't be able to do what einstein does, but it does seem like a v v hard problem.

text:
⚡ @lightning LABS LANZA #WAVELENGTH EN BITCOIN MAINNET.

 ¿QUÉ SIGNIFICA PARA QUIENES UTILIZAMOS LND?

Hoy, 23 de octubre de 2026, Lightning Labs anunció el lanzamiento público de Wavelength en mainnet, todavía en fase alfa.

Lo primero que debemos entender: Wavelength NO es una nueva versión de LND ni lo reemplaza. Es una infraestructura distinta que permite integrar pagos Bitcoin y Lightning sin administrar directamente un nodo, canales o liquidez.

¿QUÉ OFRECE?

1. Billeteras de autocustodia sin canales propios. El usuario conserva sus claves privadas y firma sus operaciones. Wavelength utiliza una arquitectura basada en Ark, con UTXOs virtuales (VTXOs), y se conecta a Lightning mediante swaps y liquidez proporcionada por el operador.

2. Pagos Lightning simplificados. Las aplicaciones pueden enviar y recibir pagos sin encargarse de abrir canales, rebalancear liquidez o mantener infraestructura de enrutamiento.

3. Integración con agentes de IA. Mediante MCP y L402, un agente puede pagar por APIs, datos y servicios utilizando Lightning. Esto abre la puerta a pagos automatizados entre sistemas, aunque exige límites de gasto y permisos estrictos.

4. Mejoras técnicas importantes en Wavelength v0.2.0:

• Recuperación de billeteras mediante semilla.

• Idempotencia para reducir pagos duplicados por reintentos.

• Recuperación de operaciones interrumpidas.

• Macaroons con permisos limitados.

• Validaciones adicionales antes de firmar transacciones.

• Contabilidad persistente, endpoints de salud y compilaciones reproducibles.

5. Comisiones y límites iniciales:

• Comisión del servicio: 0,25 % al enviar y recibir pagos Lightning.

• Al enviar, se suman las comisiones de enrutamiento.

• Saldo máximo por cuenta: 300.000 sats.

• Máximo por VTXO: 50.000 sats.

Ejemplo: enviar 100.000 sats implica 250 sats de comisión del servicio, más los costos adicionales aplicables.

PERO HAY UN DETALLE FUNDAMENTAL: AUTOCUSTODIA NO SIGNIFICA INDEPENDENCIA OPERATIVA.

Aunque el usuario conserva sus claves y dispone de mecanismos de salida unilateral hacia Bitcoin on-chain, depende del operador para la coordinación cotidiana, los swaps y la liquidez.

Además, los VTXOs requieren renovaciones periódicas, aproximadamente cada dos semanas, para mantener las garantías de salida. Por eso es importante estudiar qué ocurre ante desconexiones prolongadas o la desaparición del operador.

¿QUÉ CAMBIA SI YA UTILIZAS LND?

Si administras tu nodo, canales, liquidez y enrutamiento, Wavelength no añade automáticamente nuevas funciones a LND.

La diferencia es arquitectónica:

• LND: controlas directamente tu infraestructura Lightning.

• Wavelength: delegas la complejidad operativa, conservando las claves de tu billetera, pero aceptando nuevas dependencias y comisiones.

Para pasarelas de pago, aplicaciones con múltiples usuarios y agentes de IA, Wavelength puede simplificar considerablemente el desarrollo.

Para quienes priorizamos soberanía operativa, administrar nuestro propio LND sigue ofreciendo ventajas importantes.

Lightning Labs también contempla integrar stablecoins mediante Taproot Assets, pero eso pertenece a su desarrollo futuro, no a las capacidades generales de este lanzamiento.

MI CONCLUSIÓN:

#Wavelength representa un avance interesante para facilitar el uso de Bitcoin y Lightning en aplicaciones y agentes autónomos.

Pero no elimina la necesidad de liquidez, no sustituye a LND y no convierte la autocustodia en independencia absoluta.

La verdadera innovación consiste en simplificar la infraestructura sin entregar las claves privadas. El desafío será demostrar que ese modelo conserva suficientes garantías de seguridad, recuperación y disponibilidad cuando opera con dinero real.

Al ser todavía una versión alfa, merece pruebas rigurosas antes de utilizarse con fondos importantes.

text:
Lightning Labs opened Wavelength to everyone on mainnet yesterday, and the design gets the most important part right: the user can always leave.

Wavelength is a toolkit for adding bitcoin payments to apps and AI agents, built on an Ark-like settlement layer. Three reasons it's worth watching:

1. Keys stay with the user from the first command. Lightning Labs says the coordination service that settles transfers never has unilateral control of funds, and the exit command moves a balance back on-chain without anyone's permission.
2. Agents get least-privilege access. A service can be given the right to receive payments with no ability to sign or recover the wallet.
3. The limits are stated up front. Mainnet accounts cap at 300,000 sats and each VTXO at 50,000. Small caps on day one are honest.

Convenience that keeps the exit open is how self-custody scales.

ENSv2 upgrades the protocol for more flexibility. Existing names keep working; upgrade is optional (adds 62 days to expiry, grace period becomes 28 days so release date stays the same).

Key changes: hierarchical registries (each name manages its own subnames), role-based permissions (grant/revoke easily), stablecoin payments with multi-year discounts ($8/yr for 5+ chars), simpler registration, and new App/Explorer.

Use cases: DAOs issue/reset member.dao.eth for the whole group in one step; companies assign roles like "edit avatar only"; link records across your names so one update applies everywhere.

so many gems and great tips in this talk from @yminsky about how to improve your codebase for agents

• agents thrive on feedback, and types are one of the best kinds 
• make illegal states unrepresentable with types, and it enforces global rules across your codebase
• property based tests, fuzzing, and even full-system deterministic simulation testing

• formal methods used to be very expensive: seL4 is about 8,700 lines of C and took around 25 person-years, with 23 lines of proof for every line of C code, but agents change the roi

Brazil's recent election results do not change the fundamentals of BlackOpal's LiquidStone II and the nOPAL vault.

The underlying assets are short-duration consumer credit receivables that settle at face value in weeks  and do not publicly trade, avoiding the price volatility seen in Brazilian equity markets. With Visa and Mastercard backstopping the credit under BCB Resolution 522, local bank credit exposure is minimized.

Exposure is hedged with NDFs and settled in USD, with short-term rise in hedging costs absorbed by the strategy's net spread first. USD investors are largely insulated from BRL weakness.

Same hedging strategy, same book, and business as usual for Open Finance.
