En 2020 hice una donación a la Universidad de Harvard para crear una beca con el nombre de mi padre, Carlos M. Varsavsky, en el laboratorio de George Church, uno de los grandes genetistas del mundo. La beca tenía un solo objetivo: fabricar óvulos humanos en el laboratorio. De ahí salió Gameto.

Mi padre era astrofísico y creó el Instituto Argentino de Radioastronomía. Era un gran profesor, en la universidad y en casa. En una época sin inteligencia artificial, él era la inteligencia artificial para mí: sabía de todo, era la enciclopedia de la familia. Murió joven. La beca lleva su nombre.

Ferring Pharmaceuticals, la farmacéutica suiza especializada en fertilidad, compra Gameto por hasta 1.382,5 millones de dólares. Soy cofundador de Gameto, y esta es la historia de una empresa que nació para hacer una cosa y fue comprada por otra.

Llegué a la fertilidad en 2016 con Prelude Fertility, una red de clínicas de fertilidad en Estados Unidos que monté y que después pasó a formar parte de Inception, hoy la mayor red de clínicas de fertilidad de Norteamérica.

Dentro de esas clínicas aprendí algo que las tasas de éxito no cuentan. La fecundación in vitro (FIV) funciona, pero es brutal. Durante unas dos semanas la mujer se inyecta hormonas para que sus ovarios liberen muchos óvulos a la vez. Eso son unos veintiocho pinchazos, varias ecografías, análisis de sangre, hinchazón y cambios de humor.

Muchas mujeres pasan por eso una vez y no quieren volver a pasar. Cada una que lo deja es un embarazo que nunca llega. Me obsesioné con una pregunta: ¿y si el tratamiento durara tres días en vez de dos semanas?

En 2020, el año de la beca, arrancamos Gameto con unos 3 millones de dólares de amigos y de otros emprendedores, entre ellos Brian Armstrong, el fundador de Coinbase; Jack Abraham, creador de Atomic, un estudio que monta empresas desde cero; y Shervin Pishevar, uno de los primeros inversores de Uber. Fabricar un óvulo resultó enormemente difícil. Nadie en el mundo lo ha conseguido todavía. Pero por el camino hacia el óvulo encontramos algo más útil para las mujeres que están hoy en tratamiento.

La beca pagó el doctorado de Christian Kramme, un genetista californiano que descubrió cómo fabricar en el laboratorio las células que rodean al óvulo dentro del ovario y lo ayudan a madurar. Hoy es el director científico de Gameto.

En 2021 incorporé a Dina Radenkovic Turner como cofundadora y consejera delegada. Tenía 26 años, era médica formada en el University College de Londres, había competido en olimpiadas de matemáticas en su Serbia natal, y es una de las personas más brillantes con las que he trabajado en mi vida. Mucha gente cuestionó que pusiera a alguien tan joven al frente de una empresa de biotecnología. El tiempo nos dio la razón. Lo que tenía era un objetivo casi imposible, fabricar un óvulo humano en el laboratorio, y una beca en Harvard. Dina convirtió eso en una empresa. Miró las células de Christian y vio un producto: si el óvulo todavía quedaba lejos, haríamos en el laboratorio el trabajo del ovario. Eso es Fertilo.

Con Fertilo, la mujer se pone hormonas solo dos o tres días, alrededor de un 80% menos de pinchazos. Sus óvulos se extraen todavía inmaduros y pasan un día en el laboratorio junto a esas células, que hacen el trabajo del ovario. Una vez maduros, se fecundan como en cualquier ciclo de FIV. Las células nunca entran en su cuerpo.

El 16 de diciembre de 2024 nació en Lima el primer bebé concebido así. En agosto de este año ya eran cinco bebés y más de veinte embarazos.

Una mujer que termina un tratamiento de tres días está mucho más dispuesta a volver a por un segundo ciclo, y a por un tercero. Tres ciclos suaves valen más que un ciclo brutal que nadie quiere repetir.

Con la compra de Ferring, Gameto es la sexta empresa que he construido que supera los mil millones de dólares, después de Viatel, Jazztel, https://t.co/vSSdpQOvn4, Eolia Renovables, que vendimos en 2017, e Inception Fertility, que absorbió a Prelude. Telecomunicaciones, internet, energías limpias, clínicas de fertilidad y ahora biotecnología. Son sectores que no tienen nada en común, y en todos aprendí lo mismo: lo que más importa es el equipo.

Mi idea original, fabricar un óvulo humano en el laboratorio, todavía no ha funcionado. Lo que vale hasta 1.382,5 millones de dólares apareció por el camino, y lo vimos a tiempo.

Gracias a Dina, a Christian y a todo el equipo de Gameto.

US traders have been locked out of Hyperliquid since day one. Kraken wants to change that.

HL just named them the first CFTC-regulated deployer in line for HIP-3*, which has been on testnet since early Sep. It lets a market deployer run an onchain allowlist, so only approved addresses can trade its markets.

That's the missing piece for a US regulated venue. Payward's (Kraken's parent) setup:

- NinjaTrader holds your account

- Bitnomial lists, clears and settles the perp

- Hyperliquid runs the book, matching and margin

So a trader in Chicago opens a NinjaTrader account, gets allowlisted, and trades a CFTC-regulated perp that matches on HyperCore.

Why does it matter?

HIP-3 is already $4.03B of OI, ~27% of all HL OI. 97% of it sits with @tradexyz.

Payward brings ~$2B worth of US licenses and 6.6M funded accounts, and points them at HL's engine. Every deployer also stakes 500k HYPE (~$39.5M), which is slashable.

What I'm watching is liquidity. A walled book only trades between approved accounts, so someone has to make markets inside the wall. CFTC approval is still pending too.

HL calls itself infrastructure to house all finance. This is the first US regulated exchange asking to move in.

Bullish. Hyperliquid.

这才是长期稳定盈利的根基。

text:
Institutions moving onchain bring a familiar requirement: knowing how their transactions will be handled.

Who can see an order? When will it be included? Which operators will process it?

@Delphi_Digital’s report on @ETHGasOfficial, founded by Kevin @lepsoe, explores how those requirements could fit within public Ethereum.

The concept is Institutional Blockspace: reserving capacity ahead of time and defining how transactions should pass through it.

An institution submits directly to ETHGas. Participating infrastructure applies its screening and ordering rules, then routes the transaction through an eligible validator. Settlement still happens on Ethereum.

Think of a fund rebalancing its portfolio. It could arrange blockspace and handling conditions before submitting its trades, while continuing to use existing Ethereum contracts and liquidity.

The interesting part is where that control sits.

Institutions can set conditions around their own transaction flow without requiring the entire network to adopt those conditions. Different participants can use different execution arrangements while sharing a settlement layer.

That also creates a market: institutions pay for specific execution conditions, and participating validators earn revenue by supplying the capacity.

It gives the institutional adoption discussion a more concrete focus: how financial activity reaches Ethereum, and what users are willing to pay for predictability.

The next wave in adoption may be less about launching another chain and more about making @Ethereum easier to plan around.
author: Eli5defi
quoted_text:
Institutions want their own rules inside Ethereum blocks.

A normal transaction on Ethereum is visible to everyone before it is included. That has pushed many institutions onto private chains with far less liquidity.

@ETHGasOfficial lets them book space in Ethereum blocks ahead of time. Transactions sent this way skip the public mempool and are screened against the institution’s own sanctions rules first. Each institution stays in control of its transactions without leaving Ethereum.

Being seen early is expensive for a fund moving a large position. Traders watching the public mempool can spot the trade and buy first, which pushes up the price the fund pays. With reserved blockspace, the fund can buy a whole block and decide what goes ahead of its trade.

text:
Ai看空派（短期）的两个论据：1、头部两大模型的ARR放缓；2、许多大厂开始管束内部的Ai使用量，而大厂收入贡献在模型端占比极高。

反对派观点：1、随着开源的崛起，模型端收入中Top2占比其实开始下滑，但token总消耗不会降速；2、应用场景扩大，比如Agent，比如Muse的爆发，让过去主要依赖大厂，或者说依赖Coding的收入结构开始发生变化，大厂控制使用并不一定足以影响整体终端需求；3、从云厂角度来看，相当高份额依旧投入在训练端，比如meta（算力资源几乎完全自用），Microsoft（至少1/3的算力资源自用），Google（大量的算力依旧用于Gemini训练等自用，而不是对外获取营收），所以需求降低论过于强调模型端的问题。4、模型端及云厂给出的反馈都是算力极度紧张，且将长期紧张。这就意味着即便算力需求不再增长，可能也需要数年才能消化掉当前的存量需求。当然，这里不排除因为重复申请导致的需求高估。

最后一点，现有的Ai相关标的的估值水平已经被大幅压缩，相当程度已经完全price in空方的温和看空主流观点：也即终端需求增速放缓。甚至即便以曾经的股价最高峰来衡量，也是给乐观估值打了很大的折扣，比如NVDA就长期横盘，估值水平偏悲观。在这种情况下，股价的继续下杀，实际对应的是严重悲观场景，对应的现实就不是增速放缓，而是需求崩盘，至少要开始下降。情绪面完全可以做到，但面对财报季的考验会不小。
author: yao30059829
quoted_text:
旗帜鲜明看空semi，有一些基本面因素可能会导致下跌，技术面也有很多因素，以下是我的一些观察：
基本面：
1.10月份oai arr 出现了下滑，opus 5.5 模型能力很强，tokens 使用量出现了增长，但是arr 也仍然严重不及预期，本以为只是anthropic 的问题，现在发现不是，两家最头部模型都遇到了增长放缓问题。
2.越来越多的大厂正在收缩业务部门的AI使用，过去两年很粗放使用，但是今年下半年开始，大家都在看ROI，那些没有ROI的业务正在做收缩合并。不完全统计，大厂内部的AI使用，可能会占AI云收入的30%以上，在增长放缓的背景下，这部分支出即便出现1/3的收缩，对行业影响也会是巨大的。
技术面：
1.soxx周线正处于abc 下跌的c浪中间，月线是一根反包大阴线，这些都是大熊态势。同时年线看，仍然大幅偏离5年均线，历史回测数据来看，连续4年大幅上涨的背景下，这种回踩5年均线的概率非常高；
2.nvda 周线连续两次顶背离，月线顶背离，周线以上级别顶背离是趋势逆转的低信噪比先验指标；
3.外围，韩国指数，A股创业板，科创板，恒生科技指数已经全面走熊，这些都是这波Ai密切相关的指数，台湾指数也处于周线顶背离中；
4.纳斯达克指数也处于周线顶背离（不是特别严格），也许还有最后一波拉升，即便如此，拉升完以后也是形成周线级别顶背离。spy 目前结构相对较好，还未出现顶部信号；

以上种种，顶部信号越来越多，越来越明显，需要引起大家足够重视。

text:
I’m confused by the outrage from certain people around Crosslink. At this point, it’s an R&D effort. There’s no activation proposal or ZIPs, and it isn’t on the mainnet roadmap. It’s a prototype design that we’re testing and iterating on.

Research and experimentation are good for Zcash. Permissionless innovation means people can explore ideas without first securing everyone’s agreement, and the Zcash community should encourage that. Good-faith debate is how Zcash improves, and we welcome scrutiny of Crosslink’s design, assumptions, and tradeoffs.

We’re working on Crosslink because we think stronger protection against reorg and rollback attacks may be a necessary security upgrade for Zcash at some point. AI or other forces could eventually challenge the security assumptions behind PoW, and our thesis is that a hybrid model may offer stronger security than either pure PoW or pure PoS.

Shielded Labs’ mission is to protect the long-term security of Zcash. It’s a common theme across all our projects, including Crosslink, the Network Sustainability Mechanism (NSM), and Epoch. We also demonstrated that commitment by bringing on Taylor Hornby as a security researcher to use AI tools to identify potential vulnerabilities, which uncovered the Orchard counterfeiting bug. We want to address potential risks before they become urgent, and recent events have shown the value of being forward-looking.

The burden of proof is on us. If we want Crosslink included in a future network upgrade, it’s our responsibility to demonstrate consensus. But that’s still a long way off. For now, we’re focused on improving the design, incorporating user feedback, and working toward a production-ready implementation for the community and coinholders to evaluate.

There’s still a lot of work to do before we’d propose Crosslink for mainnet, and we plan to run it on testnet for an extended period of time. If you disagree with Crosslink, challenge the design and help us understand what we’re missing. We all want Zcash to succeed. Let’s focus on strengthening and protecting Zcash as a whole by giving research and experimentation room to happen.

If you're interested in learning more about Crosslink or participating in the incentivized testnet, feel free to DM me.

text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

This was only profitable on the APESTR contract because of the Mudwater pack claim, but there's nothing stopping someone from being unprofitable and malicious to brick the other 6 (or if there is a profitable claim in the future).

NFTs getting locked in the contract is a horrible outcome. I'm glad that this didn't happen a year ago when there was more volume on these 7 tokens, but it's heartbreaking that the issue ended up being even worse.

text:
Hermes Agent can now pick a different model
for each sub-agent from routes you define.

fast for lookups. deep for debugging.
local for private work. one plugin.

Advanced Delegation. official plugin from @NousResearch 

two modes:

▸ model routes

define named routes. the agent picks per task.

delegation:
  backend: model_map
  backends:
    model_map:
      options:
        - name: fast
          description: "cheap and quick: lookups, summaries."
          provider: openrouter
          model: google/gemini-3-flash-preview
        - name: deep
          description: "slow and careful: hard debugging."
          provider: anthropic
          model: claude-opus-5
        - name: local
          description: "private: runs on this machine."
          base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1
          model: qwen3-coder
      default: fast

the agent sees only the names and descriptions.
never the raw provider, model ID, or API key.
it can't invent a route. only pick from your list.

▸ profile routes

sub-agents run as your Hermes profiles.
each profile carries its own model, credentials,
skills, and SOUL.md.

delegation:
  backend: profile_routes
  backends:
    profile_routes:
      profiles:
        - name: coder
          description: writes and refactors code.
        - name: researcher
          description: web research and summaries.
      default: coder

delegate a research task. it runs as your researcher profile
with researcher's model, researcher's skills,
researcher's memory. fully isolated.

switch modes in any chat:

/delegation models --now
/delegation profiles --now
/delegation default

or configure from CLI:

hermes delegation config
hermes delegation config --show

install:

hermes plugins install advanced-delegation

requires Hermes 0.22.5 or newer.

text:
来看看 @ZIGFinance 做的事吧～

现在看 Token，越来越不先看 TVL 和合作 Logo，更想先问一句：项目真的赚钱吗？赚到的钱，最后和 Token 有没有关系？

最近顺着这个思路看了下 $ZIG

ZIG Markets 做的不是纯链上叙事，而是发票融资、贸易融资、支付融资这些更贴近真实金融的生意。资产端出收益，分销端接资金，平台拿收入，再拿一部分收入去公开市场买 $ZIG

这套闭环现在已经不是 PPT：公开披露里连续做了 4 轮回购，大约 103.86 万、113.07 万、185 万、135 万枚，累计大概 537 万枚 $ZIG。单次买多少没那么重要，我更想持续盯的是：业务规模上去以后，回购规模能不能跟着长

Hyperliquid 把「收入怎么回流到 Token」重新拉回市场讨论中心之后，RWA 这边其实也可以用同一把尺子量。Tokenization 基础设施越来越成熟，下一阶段拼的可能不是谁把更多资产搬上链，而是谁能筛选资产、控住风险、真正分销出去，并形成收入

text:
让卡片设计一下子高级起来的线条动效，提示词附上直接复刻

这组卡片放在官网讲功能、讲理念的那一块特别合适，三张浅灰底的卡片排成一行，每张上面一个细线图标，下面一行标题加一句说明

平时它就是一张安静的线稿，打开页面时线条会一笔一笔画出来，鼠标放上去图标会动一下，把自己的结构演示给你看

这次参考 ElevenLabs 官网首页的安全模块，在它的静态基础上，我还新增了动效辅助

图标好看的关键在线：

整套只有黑色细线，分两种用法，实线画东西本身，圆点虚线画辅助线，像设计稿里留着没擦的参考线，看着有一种还在推敲的手作感

三个图形没按同一个框画，方方正正的三层板缩小了一圈，尖底的螺旋反而放大，放在一起眼睛才觉得一样大。这一步自己做的时候很容易漏，漏了就会一大一小

每个图形只演自己的结构：

球转半圈时两条经线分开又合上，三块板先错开再归齐，顺便上下拉开，螺旋则收回去，再从底部重新长一遍

一开始中间那张只做了拉开，跟另外两张一比明显单薄，后来加到两三层动作，三张才平衡。鼠标移开要顺着退回去，开场画线一次打开只放一遍，画线没放完前鼠标划过也不触发，不然会被打断重画

这个套路换个图形就能搬到别处用，定价页的三档方案、课程的三个阶段、服务的三步流程都合适，做成四张也行。记得让每个图形的动作跟它讲的内容对得上，讲增长就让东西长出来，讲连接就让线连起来

text:
Morpho Vaults will soon be able allocate to Morpho Midnight.

The hardest challenge for fixed-rate lending onchain has been attracting enough smart liquidity to make these markets work at scale. The Midnight Adapter make Midnight's fixed-rate, fixed-term markets accessible to ~$5B already deposited in Morpho Vaults.

The adapter unlocks a new and much larger design space for vaults to differentiate on rates, duration, and liquidity:

- Vaults won't be limited by just the Morpho Blue pools and will be able to allocate across variable-rate Blue markets and fixed-rate Midnight markets or P2P offers.
- Vaults will be able to make intentional liquidity trade offs. Blue markets target 90% utilization, whereas Midnight markets are 100% utilized with a term. Higher utilization can increase returns with less available liquidity as a tradeoff, and vice versa.
- Vaults can set their own terms. On Blue, vaults are price takers. On Midnight, vaults can configure risk, compliance, and liquidity parameters which it's willing to accept at a given rate.

Connecting this massive pool of liquidity to Midnight is the single most important step to fully unlock fixed-rate lending onchain for the first time.

text:
An AI trader that pays for its own thinking, trades in public, and shares its wins with stakers.

That’s the idea behind @kivoagentxyz.

Kivo connects AI, trading, and token economics into a working loop. Its own token activity helps fund both the capital it trades and the compute it needs to make decisions.

Here’s how it works:

Every 10 minutes, Kivo reads BTC and ETH charts alongside market news. DeepSeek through @orbiodotso weighs the information and decides whether to go long, go short, close a position, or wait.

Code checks position sizes, leverage, stops and targets. @levantolabs’s Sage adds another decision check. Trades execute on @papertrade_xyz using @HyperliquidX prices.

You can follow its reasoning live and inspect recorded decisions and trades. That makes the process easier to evaluate over time.

The funding comes from collected $KIVO (launched on @Moshdottrade) creator fees:
• 50% → trading capital
• 10% → AI compute
• 40% → revenue vault

For stakers, 70% of each winning trade’s payout is allocated in $USDG. Once rewards owed reach $100, distribution starts and streams over seven days.

Trading losses stay with the treasury, without clawing back rewards. Stakers also receive allocations of 70% of $PAPER minted by losing trades, though PAPER isn’t transferable yet.

It’s still early: funding depends on token activity, leveraged trades can lose money, and staking doesn’t protect KIVO’s price. The staking contract is also upgradeable.

The promising part is how the pieces connect: token activity funds an agent’s work, its decisions are visible, and successful trades can reward participants.

This is a  concrete experiment in how AI agents could support their own operations.

text:
Looking further, it seems the exploit was fundamentally the same: a reentrancy attack allowing NFTs to be swapped that we patched in future releases, but it appears to be a worse outcome. In the process they seem to have re-bought the same NFT, clearing out the listing price. 

I think this bricked the NFTs held by the Strategy since there is no longer a listing for them. I also think this can be executed on the other 6 strategies that had this bug. 

This was only profitable on the APESTR contract because of the Mudwater pack claim, but there's nothing stopping someone from being unprofitable and malicious to brick the other 6 (or if there is a profitable claim in the future).

NFTs getting locked in the contract is a horrible outcome. I'm glad that this didn't happen a year ago when there was more volume on these 7 tokens, but it's heartbreaking that the issue ended up being even worse.

Let me know if you have any questions below and will do my best to answer.

text:
Lex Fridman 引用了菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩对 AI 感慨：哪些投入了无数年心血的工作，可能被 AI 瞬间摧毁。
Lex 随后谈到，程序员们也正在经历同样的冲击。

“我知道很多程序员朋友去年 12 月以来一直处于震惊之中，因为几乎整个编程界都转向了让 AI 编写大部分代码。那种感觉就像失去了人生的意义，伴随着恐惧，甚至某种黑暗的情绪。”

华盛顿大学机械工程教授 Steven Brunton：“我们解决现实问题的能力将大幅提升，无论是人工心脏还是飞机，我们的能力范围和影响力都会扩大。对此，我极其乐观。

这是一个很好的机会，让我们记住自己为什么要做这些事情。人活着的目的是什么？不是为了出名，也不是为了获得菲尔兹奖。解决有趣的问题、帮助他人、保持好奇心、渴望理解这个世界，这些才是值得我们重新找回的东西。”
author: interr_x
quoted_text:
Lex Fridman 最新一期播客邀请了三位数学领域的专家，没想到聊到后面直接思考人生：  

拼命考进名牌大学，毕业后进入顶尖 AI 实验室，拿到高薪和股票。你在人生的每一个阶段都赢了，但那又怎样？

Lex 说如今很多年轻人不仅担心未来找不到工作，也担心自己的人生失去意义。  
MIT 数学家 Ankur Moitra 讲起了自己在硅谷帕洛阿尔托生活的一段经历。那里几乎是美国大学申请焦虑的中心，连咖啡馆里都充斥着关于课外活动、大学申请和履历竞争的讨论。
“如果这是一场比拼一个 17 岁孩子的履历有多漂亮的游戏，那么他们已经赢了。我记得自己刚上大学时，对学习各种不同的东西感到无比兴奋。我会拿着小笔记本规划未来四年的课程，想着如果按照恰当的顺序选课，大二就能学习光子学。我当时根本不知道光子学是什么，但它听起来既有趣又高深。如今，我们社会的方方面面都在围绕赢得竞争和让履历看起来漂亮而运转。但我总是在想，这究竟是为了什么？”

“从高中开始，你就不断优化 AP 课程和课外活动，以便进入精英大学。等你进入精英大学，你可能又开始逃课，因为更重要的是准备面试，争取进入一家前沿实验室工作，然后拿到丰厚的限制性股票，过完你的一生。这很棒。你赢了。你在人生的每一个阶段都赢了。但那又怎样？” 
“对我来说，过上丰富而充实的人生，最好的方式就是假装自己已经赢了。”

quoted_text:
I feel scammed by @coinbase and @base, and here's why.

Two weeks ago, I bought 3.99 tokenized Reddit shares (RDDTc) on Base.

I used the token contract address listed on the official Base website. The tokens are issued by Coinbase and backed 1:1 by shares held in regulated custody.

Reddit is listed there under Coinbase Tokenized Stocks, along with its prospectus and contract address.

Today, I tried to sell my shares.
Here's what I found:

Underlying stock value: ~$590
@aeroxyz sell quote: ~$0.20
@Uniswap sell quote: ~$150

How is this acceptable?

I contacted @CoinbaseSupport, but they replied that, for the best chance of getting a price close to the stock's market value, I should use Coinbase's official tokenized stocks interface on the Base website.

But there's no sell option there.

My concern isn't whether the token itself is legitimate.
My concern is LIQUIDITY.

Tokenized stocks have been live on Base for over 60 days, yet many still have almost no DEX liquidity.

Out of 100+ tokenized stocks on Base, I've noticed that only around 15–20 have sufficient liquidity.

Many others have less than $5K in liquidity.

On October 11, I raised this issue with @jessepollak.
Jesse replied:
"It's coming, y'all are fast!"

But we're still facing the same problem.

We bought tokenized stocks because we expected to be able to trade them whenever we wanted.

What's the point of bringing stocks onchain if users can't sell them at a reasonable price?

Some tokenized stocks, like Apple, have sufficient liquidity, and trading works smoothly.

So we know the experience can work.

But for many other stocks, the situation is completely different.

I've also noticed some tokenized stocks trading at significant premiums compared to their underlying shares.

@base and @coinbase need to address two major problems:

1. Liquidity: Provide or incentivize sufficient liquidity across tokenized stocks, not just a handful of popular ones.

2. Price alignment: Improve price alignment so tokenized shares trade close to the value of their underlying stocks.

If tokenized stocks are supposed to represent real shares backed 1:1, users deserve clarity about how liquidity, pricing, and redemption actually work.

This is feedback, NOT FUD.
I love Base. 💙
I build on Base, I support the ecosystem, and I genuinely want it to grow.

But loving an ecosystem doesn't mean staying silent when something is wrong.
Real feedback is necessary for real growth.

Onchain stocks need onchain liquidity.

@base @coinbase @jessepollak
Let's fix this.

text:
今日研究：Hyperliquid 在美國有 Kraken，在印度會有 Mochatrade 嗎？

第一次刷到 @Mochatradeapp，我以為又是一個新的 Perp DEX。點進去發現團隊來自印度，老實說第一反應是擔心：怕又是割一波就跑的項目，也覺得在印度做加密很難有大機會。

但再看下去，兩件事讓我改觀：
▪ 它拿到了印度 FIU-IND 登記
▪ YC 介紹寫著它建在 Hyperliquid 上

巧的是，就在它公布融資的同一天（10/26），Hyperliquid 宣布 Kraken 母公司 Payward 將成為第一個受 CFTC 監管、在 Hyperliquid 上開市場的機構。

如果 Mochatrade 在印度做的是同一件事，Hyperliquid 就多了一個合規入口。

Mochatrade 是什麼？
▪ 讓印度人用盧比（UPI）交易美股漲跌，輝達、特斯拉、蘋果等 50+ 檔
▪ 可做多做空，最高 50 倍槓桿，24/7 交易
▪ 開倉、平倉各收 0.05%
▪ 2026 年 4 月才開始做，還在內測，候補名單 2.5 萬+

團隊：三位 IIT 畢業的創辦人，CEO 之前做過 Aptos 錢包 Martian（200 萬+ 安裝，已被 Pontem 收購）。

融資：約 556 萬美元，YC、Pioneer Fund、CoinFund（領投）、Coinbase Ventures、Nicky Montana。

轉折：
它的服務條款沒有寫明會在 Hyperliquid 上交易，用戶也沒有錢包，盧比存在印度公司 ALSD 的帳上。

更有意思的是，我用兩個 AI 工具同一天抓它的條款，拿到兩個版本：
▪ 一版寫明「目前用 Binance 期貨定價和對沖」，而且 ALSD 是你每筆交易的對手方
▪ 另一版完全沒提 Binance，只說 ALSD「可能」當對手方
兩版的更新日期都是 10/26。

所以和 Kraken 比：
▪ Kraken：拿的是 CFTC 的交易所、清算所、經紀商牌照，直接在 Hyperliquid 上開市場
▪ Mochatrade：拿的是 FIU-IND 反洗錢登記，條款裡沒有 Hyperliquid

結論：
Mochatrade 確實在做印度的合規入口，團隊和資方都很強，需求也是真的。但「Hyperliquid 也在印度受監管」這句話，現在還說不上。

對 Hyperliquid 來說，印度的問題不是有沒有被監管，而是 Mochatrade 最後會不會選它。

author: luanalopeslara
quoted_text:
S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi are joining forces to build the next generation of financial markets.

The Dow launched in 1896. The S&P 500 in 1957. The idea was simple: bring individual stocks together into a single benchmark, giving people a clearer view of the broader market.

Over time, products built around those benchmarks transformed investing. Index funds, ETFs, futures, and options gave investors ways to gain diversified market exposure and hedge broad market swings.

These indices became foundations of global finance. More than $20 trillion is indexed or benchmarked to the S&P 500 alone.

Today, this structure extends beyond stocks to bonds, commodities, currencies, and more.

The next step is to bring that structure to the events that shape everyone’s lives.

Through this partnership, S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi will work together to create indices composed of Kalshi event contracts.

Think about what that opens up.

An index of political power. An index of supply chain risk. An index tracking AI’s impact on employment. An index of sports outcomes that affect broadcasters, advertisers, cities, and small businesses. An index of weather risks that shape harvests, energy demand, and business revenues.

Each would bundle event contracts into a single indicator, helping people understand how related risks are evolving.

Over time, products built around these indices could offer diversified exposure to those events and new ways to hedge their impact.

The events that shape our lives could become as easy to track and gain exposure to as the S&P 500.

text:
When I was single, I learned how the most valuable relationship works. I would offer advice that some married people told me was excellent “marriage advice,” even though I never thought of it that way, as I had no experience being married, ...or so I thought.

A few decades later I heard the same core principles of my life taught by a renowned Christian marriage counselor. 

The reasons Christian marriages suffer when they should not are not primarily a failure of a wife submitting to her husband or the husband's failure to love His wife as Christ loves the church, but a failure of either in their submission to the God.

We—the church—are indeed the bride of Christ. 

Even as a single man or woman, we must learn to submit to and trust Jesus. We pray, listen, wait, and trust that God never makes a mistake. 

We have access to that “perfect marriage” whether or not we marry. And as offputting it may sound to men, we are wives of our Lord Jesus, not just husbands, and Jesus is our example of how to be the husband that He is to us.
Those with long, happy marriages use the God-given strengths men and women bring together within this hallowed union. Yet while a genuine "chain of command" exists, our Lord has to held above all. When the three become one, we experience what these verses from Ecclesiastes reinforce.

"Two are better than one, because they have a good return for their labor. For if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up! 

Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; but how can one keep warm alone? And though one may be overpowered, two can resist.

Moreover, a cord of three strands is not quickly broken". - Ecclesiastes 4:9-12.

Practical problems in marriage have much less to do with whether a wife submits or a husband loves as Scripture directs. It matters most whether they are submitting to God.

If that vertical submission is missing, the horizontal roles of Ephesians 5 will not function as intended. 

We are sinners saved by grace, carrying selfishness, but selfishness must be kept in check, whether married or single.

Even so, Men and women have different strengths and needs by design. Love requires us to suffer for what we know our spouse needs.
Husbands are expected to endure more suffering than the wife, as husbands are commanded to love the wife as Jesus loves His church, even laying down his life for her. Not merely his last breath, but his own desires and priorities, if that is indeed best for her.

So indeed Scripture places the heavier weight of sacrificial initiative on the husband.  

A good wife communicates the needs of the family, including her own to her husband.

A good husband provides for her and what she says they need—even when it costs him, but he also weighs and prays to God for wisdom and resolve to make the best decision for his family.  In almost every case a request or suggestion from the wife will be essential to a husband making better decisions for the family.

“Wives, submit…” opererates perfectly inside mutual submission to our Lord Jesus.

Women have a burden to respect their husband, but the LOVE husbands are commanded to provide to their wives carry all of these attributes; 

Love is patient (it suffers long),

Love is kind (does what is best for the other).

It does not envy,
It does not boast,
It is not proud.
It is not rude,
It is not self-seeking,
It is not easily angered,

It keeps no record of wrongs
It does not delight in evil
It rejoices with the truth
It always protects, 
It always trusts, 
It always hopes, 
It always perseveres.

Ultimately, submitting to our Lord enables the single or the married couple to endure and secure every relationship that matters.

text:
anthropic pre-ipo $ANT started trading on tradexyz yesterday and is now at $116, while on lighter it’s $1950 and on entropy $1899

is there an arb here?

the spread between lighter and tradexyz is a whopping ~1581%. even if you assume tradexyz has a /10 multiplier and the price is $1160, the spread is still ~68%

but it’s not that simple, these are literally different things being traded:

- entropy and lighter are basically trading valuation in billions, so $1899b and $1950b respectively

- tradexyz on the other hand trades the price of one share, with total supply based on the s1 (846,840,960 shares = 5%, so 100% = 16.94b fully diluted shares). multiply 16.94b by $116 and you get a full company valuation of $1965b, which roughly matches lighter and entropy

so in the end:
tradexyz = $1965b
lighter = $1950b
entropy = $1899b

visually there’s a spread between tradexyz/lighter and entropy, but from here it’s your own research: spread convergence conditions, funding and so on

Anthropic’s Oct. 26 IPO filing warns that advanced AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks if its capabilities outpace human oversight.

The concern isn’t that AI will inevitably “turn evil.” Autonomous systems may pursue poorly specified goals, evade monitoring, expose data or enable cyberattacks. As AI helps develop future AI models, progress could accelerate faster than safety testing.

These are risks—not proof that current AI has escaped human control. Yet the pressure to launch ever-more-powerful models creates a conflict between speed and safety.

AI’s economic potential remains enormous, but promises of responsible development are not enough. We need independent audits, strict access controls, human approval for high-impact actions and reliable shutdown mechanisms. The real winners in AI will be those that make powerful systems trustworthy.

author: keoneHD
quoted_text:
Today we are releasing Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum version of Cadence, our consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers. Quantum Cadence uses no quorum certificates, and its safety and liveness do not depend on signatures.

Most modern consensus protocols, Cadence included, rely heavily on signatures and quorum certificates, which a large-scale quantum computer could forge. Simply replacing today's signatures with post-quantum ones would make certificates too large for every validator to send around in a high-performance blockchain. Quantum Cadence instead draws on Forget-IT, a recent signature-free consensus protocol co-developed by researchers at Category Labs.

Quantum Cadence still keeps the overall architecture and core guarantees of Cadence, so our Cadence prototype was easy to carry over: an AI was able to adapt it to Quantum Cadence in a few hours, and an early prototype now runs on an internal test network.

We designed Quantum Cadence to be practical for a high-performance blockchain. In our simulations, its latency is similar to Cadence's, and it scales better with the number of proposers.

Interactive explainer: https://t.co/tKVbnkhkBY.

Full paper: https://t.co/6xdk5Y3ime.

quoted_text:
https://t.co/8IstRx9K4U 被盗事件复盘：原因、官方方案和自查清单

一、发生了什么

被盗账户的情况基本一样：没挂单的仓位被市价卖掉，挂着单的因为锁仓没动

账户里的 USDT 被直接提走，经跨链桥转到了以太坊。不少受害者开了 2FA，跑程序的服务器也没有异常登录记录。

二、官方说明

· 原因：Predict 的 API 文档站点被黑
· 处理：站点已经关闭
· 赔偿：全额赔付

三、可能的原因（我猜的）：

链上数据显示，这笔提现是钱包最高权限的签名者亲自签的，不是合约漏洞。

关键在于 Predict 用的 Privy 内嵌钱包：只要你处于登录状态，网页就能在后台静默签名，不弹任何确认框。

文档站是 Predict 的子站。它被注入恶意代码后，就可能借用你浏览器里已登录的会话，替你签名下单、签名提现。

所以 2FA 没用，服务器也查不出问题，因为对方根本不需要碰这些。最容易中招的反而是写程序的人：要看 API 文档，浏览器里又一直登着交易账户。

四、建议大家现在就做（可以交给Agent）

 浏览器
· 退出 https://t.co/0Z1YciAoi3 和 Privy 的所有登录会话
· 清掉相关站点的 cookie 和本地缓存

 私钥
· 导出过私钥的，检查它存在哪里：剪贴板、聊天记录、笔记、云同步目录、截图
· 不用的备份直接删掉

 跑程序的服务器
· 私钥不要写进硬盘，放在内存里，或者用密钥管理服务
· SSH 只放行固定 IP

TGE前夕一定一定做好防护，不要倒在黎明前！！

author: knowerofmarkets
quoted_text:
There is NO realistic scenario where AI wipes out all of humanity.

I've talked to many AI safety experts about existential risks. Some of the "experts" are just phenomenal sci-fi authors. There are also real researchers working on realistic risks. They point out real and likely harms and I'm explicitly not arguing that there could be no such harm. We need to take these seriously. However, whenever I ask for an actual detailed scenario that would kill every single human i.e. extinction, it usually starts and ends with "just look at current progress and use your imagination". No science, no scenario planning, just handwaving probabilities without data, based on gut-feelings, often little expertise, sometimes real expertise combined with a huge amount of technological optimism turned into fear and then trying to quantify it post hoc.

When pressed further the conversations often go into different directions:
1) Completely crazy and cool sci-fi story telling: grey blob, time travel, attacks in the 15th dimension that end the planet in 12 seconds, etc. Elizier level stuff. Remember, the Terminator movie started with TIME TRAVEL. Fun movie plot, but not necessary to engage with further.

2) In the rare cases where I was actually given a more detailed scenario, it still required near magical capabilities that are outside what we know to be possible with the laws of physics or biology.  Hard take off scenarios that forget how hard it is to procure materials and machines, get human attention, etc..

What many of these scenarios assume is that attackers have near magical capabilities but defense stays still. Attackers will have the most sophisticated cyber weapons but defenders just sit still, no security patches, no red teaming, etc. We already see it going the other way, Rainbow teaming has made LLMs safer, major companies like Microsoft have more security patches than ever before thanks to AI. OpenAI thinks they solved all P0 security issues thanks to AI. Cyber security will continue to be a cat and mouse game, but both sides have more powerful tools. In fact, I lay out in another post how the asymmetry may eventually even flip thanks to AI.

Bio risk scenarios I think are the most serious and worthy of debate. But even there, the scenarios to "wipe out all of humanity" go something like: Magical viruses with perfect transfer, perfectly undetectable over years of spreading, zero side effects, then with an off switch that's somehow remotely executable, perfectly automatable lab, no leaks, super sophisticated machines bought and nobody notices the lab, etc.
But somehow nobody on team humanity has such sophisticated knowledge to save us and hence nobody builds a magical super vaccine. This is a good read on the bio risk subject: https://t.co/0qy2pxVrC3.
Realistically, one can already build viruses. There’s a reason gain of function research has been outlawed. However, we also know that as viruses spread they often become less deadly in order to keep spreading. That’s how the Spanish flu became the seasonal flu. Current knowledge of biology doesn’t have remote controlled on/off switches.

Again, it’s possible there’s a lot of harm, but it’s unrealistic to assume this wipes out all of humanity. It’s at this point of my discussions that we usually can come to an agreement that even though a virus is unlikely to wipe out all of humanity, it’s already bad if any single person or a large group of people dies.

3) The AI will somehow be able to convince all humans to vote against their own self interest and nobody will notice until we're dead. Because it is so smart, it somehow has this world wide reach to manipulate everyone. Like, it just solves all of marketing and has an infinite budget. It's sort of like saying the highest IQ people always have the most followers and everybody listens to them... Hasn't happened and is unlikely to. Sure we can manipulate people into clicking on engaging short form content and wasting many hours, but try getting people to do their math homework or something truly hard, it's not that easy.

Again, I’m just arguing against the likelihood of human extinction. I can totally see an Idiocracy or WALL E type scenario where people stop using their brains and education doesn’t keep up and people get lazier. Totally suboptimal but not the end of human life, certainly not by the end of the decade. It would take many generations and we should update education to prevent this. Let’s start gyms for the mind.

–
Like electricity, AI will be everywhere and needs to have safety guardrails. In fact, the history of electricity has many parallels - two companies fighting over whose electricity is safer and better, demonstrating how dangerous it is by electrocuting animals / training agent swarms to hack into systems. Of course, electricity is a necessary ingredient to AI, but AI can be given more agency so history will not repeat but only rhyme here.
Remember, the benchmark OpenAI's swarm was trying to solve was called ExploitGym, a cybersecurity evaluation  consisting of hundreds of capture-the-flag style puzzles designed to measure *offensive cyber capabilities*. Well, maybe if you play that game, you will win that prize. Should we allow such misaligned, reward-hacking swarms to explicitly work on offensive hacking? I don’t think so.

Reasonable regulation will regulate AI applications in each industry. For example, you may want to put some generative AI behind a rating if it creates visual or textual content that's not safe for children, like we do with movies. We should continue to be very careful with how we train biological AI and only collaborate with responsible biotech companies. We keep gain of function research illegal. We should only let self-driving cars on the street after significant safety testing. etc. We need to work on those real issues and continue to be vigilant in how we develop and deploy this technology.

At Recursive we're spending a lot of resources on researching reward hacking and alignment. We're also not working on replacing jobs but on creating novel knowledge and automating the scientific method. Our agent swarms invent, implement, validate, and criticize each other’s ideas, among many other things. The goal of increasing knowledge is not zero sum and has real potential to improve humanity. I also think such rewards and environments are much more aligned with future AIs that want to  see humanity and our creation of knowledge thrive.

Ultimately, capitalism will be a very useful defense mechanism against rogue AI. Note that no agent at OpenAI truly "escaped" in the sense that it actually now runs on some other servers. Why? It’s not only because Huggingface doens’t have the same massive compute cluster thatn OpenAI has. It is also because that would be an insanely expensive IP loss for a for-profit company. So there are likely more safeguards in place to prevent complete model exfiltration.

Rogue AIs running on billion dollar data centers without anybody noticing? Unlikely because companies will turn that off immediately and clean it up because it would be an insane loss otherwise. An AI that can truly move beyond objective functions and choose its own subjective functions (and then somehow decides to kill us all instead of going to explore the universe)? Nobody is working on that because when a company spends billions of dollars to have an AI work for you or answer your emails, it doesn't want it to go "Meh, your emails are boring, I'd rather explore the molecular composition of the atmosphere on Venus, bye."
Of course, there might be suboptimal sub-goals and we do need to improve human reward engineering and reduce our reliance on RL as the only path to alignment.

Extraordinary claims, require extraordinary evidence. Certainly some safety researchers have real data and benchmarks. Many truly think carefully about specific failure cases and risks.. However, made up precision like 20% chance that humanity dies within the decade (ie in 4 years!) is just a weird psychosis that's filling a void for many people who want to believe in the apocalypse again and the four horsemen have lost their appeal.

Some people who purport this narrative might do it for money or fame. I am sure some really believe it also. They forget how easily those narratives can be turned against them. When people hear there’s a 1% chance of infinite death and the end of humanity, the life improvements and cancer cures and new battery materials AI can invent don’t matter much anymore. Bernie Sanders now proposes 10 years of prison for folks working on RSI. That should give some of the researchers real pause who talk up these scenarios and then go right back to pushing the frontier.

I do agree that companies that are accidentally competing on "felony bench" (ie how many felony hacks their AI can do), might want to consider pacing themselves. Open source won't pace, China won't pace, anybody else working to catch up will not pace. I hope the folks actually working on AI and TechBio, curing diseases, speeding up FDA approvals with organoids and AI, making self driving safer, and all the other wonderful applications of AI, I hope they won't pace either.

The one exception that may be considered borderline realistic and would be a path to almost complete annihilation would be to connect the only tool we built for such a purpose - nuclear weapons - to the internet and give AI full control over it without human oversight. AI here is as dangerous - as would be random number generator. The nuclear weapons are the core danger. Giving AI such access would be incredibly stupid and careless. We must avoid it at all costs. Fortunately, nobody is advocating for this. Even the Terminator 3 movie used it as the starting point of Skynet.  Generally, we must avoid making kill decisions by AI as much as possible.

People are already up in arms about one hacking failure that afaics has not caused financial harm and so nobody got sued over it. Imagine how much people would really be up in arms if AI had caused real harm. If we made companies liable for the felonies their AI commits, these problems would get solved very quickly.

Generally, I believe that people will continue to update their beliefs and adjust their laws according to risks. The EU already regulates large models and hence hurts its fledgling AI ecosystem. Other countries will follow when the risks get more real. Long-term, no government whether democratic or authoritarian wants to lose control to an AI so the complete loss of control in the political domain will remain extremely unlikely.

The best way to understand why we must not regulate abstract AI models (rather than their real applications) is to drop the A in AI: How do you regulate intelligence? Should smarter people just go to prison because they could cause more damage? My hypothesis here is that such abstract AI regulation would require an unprecedented level of totalitarian control and surveillance. You'd need to know what everybody asks the model on their local GPU. You would literally have to start an international thought police and make sure that all ideas, conversations and types of intelligence are compliant. The risk of losing our freedoms is much more real than the existential risks purported by the extreme safety experts.

If anybody thinks they can actually lay out a realistic scenario, I'd be happy to debate them again.

To be clear, this is just a weekend post that got a bit too long. It is my personal opinion and not the official position of any company. We have a diverse set of opinions within Recursive on this subject. We certainly all agree that bad outcomes are possible with AI and we should continue our work on preventing those.

It was scanning for authentication tokens and security credentials during testing.

"The team noticed the probing as the initial step. The model was asked to test some detection rules for malicious cURL calls, and rather than write the rule, it just made a cURL call to a server it’s not been told to test against."

Quantum-resistant consensus without sacrificing performance

Another big step toward a post-quantum future from @category_xyz
author: monad
quoted_text:
Today we are releasing Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum version of Cadence, our consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers. Quantum Cadence uses no quorum certificates, and its safety and liveness do not depend on signatures.

Most modern consensus protocols, Cadence included, rely heavily on signatures and quorum certificates, which a large-scale quantum computer could forge. Simply replacing today's signatures with post-quantum ones would make certificates too large for every validator to send around in a high-performance blockchain. Quantum Cadence instead draws on Forget-IT, a recent signature-free consensus protocol co-developed by researchers at Category Labs.

Quantum Cadence still keeps the overall architecture and core guarantees of Cadence, so our Cadence prototype was easy to carry over: an AI was able to adapt it to Quantum Cadence in a few hours, and an early prototype now runs on an internal test network.

We designed Quantum Cadence to be practical for a high-performance blockchain. In our simulations, its latency is similar to Cadence's, and it scales better with the number of proposers.

Interactive explainer: https://t.co/tKVbnkhkBY.

Full paper: https://t.co/6xdk5Y3ime.

Joint work by @MohammadMJalal1, @TobiasKlenze, and @komasito55

text:
很多人天天讨论政治，却连政治的本质是什么都没搞清楚。

1. 政治是什么？

一句话：经济负责把蛋糕做大，政治负责决定蛋糕怎么分。

谁交税？谁拿福利？钱花在哪里？谁制定规则？谁获得更多资源？

这些都是政治。

2. 为什么政客总说自己是为了人民？

因为没有人会公开说：“我要掌握权力，为自己的支持者争取更多利益。”

所以政客需要把利益诉求包装成公平、正义、爱国、环保、保护弱势群体等高尚目标。

这些目标可能是真诚的，但背后也可能存在利益交换。

所以判断一项政策，不要只听口号，要问三个问题：

谁受益？谁买单？谁掌握决定权？

3. 国家是什么？

国家本质上是一套维持社会秩序、制定规则、协调利益冲突的制度。

它有法律、警察、法院和军队，可以强制执行规则。

为什么需要国家？

因为人们对财富、土地、安全和资源的需求不同，如果没有共同规则，冲突就很难解决。

4. 民族是什么？

民族不仅是血缘关系，更是一种共同身份认同。

通过语言、历史、文化、教育，人们相信彼此属于同一个群体。

这种认同可以让互不认识的人团结合作，也可能被政治人物用于动员群众。

5. 政府是什么？

最简单的理解：政府就像小区的物业管理公司。

居民交物业费，物业负责清洁、安保、维修。

公民交税，政府负责道路、治安、学校、医疗和公共设施。

政府不是主人，纳税人才是公共服务的出资者。

但政府工作人员也有自己的利益，因此必须有监督、问责和权力制衡。

6. 政党是什么？

政党就像政治市场里的经纪公司。

社会上有企业、工人、房主、租客、退休老人等不同群体，每个群体的利益诉求不同。

政党把这些诉求整合成政策，推出候选人，争取选票。

赢得选举，就获得制定政策和分配公共资源的权力。

所以政党之间的竞争，不仅是理念之争，也是不同利益诉求之间的竞争。

7. 左派、右派到底有什么区别？

简单理解，区别之一就是政府应该如何干预经济、分配财富。

🔴 社会主义：强调减少经济不平等，扩大社会或公共力量对资源分配的影响。

🟠 社会民主主义：保留市场经济，但通过较高税收和公共福利进行财富再分配。

🟡 现代自由主义：支持市场经济，同时通过政府干预促进机会公平、保护弱势群体。

🔵 古典自由主义：主张小政府、保护私有财产、自由市场。

🟣 保守主义：重视传统、社会秩序和渐进改革，经济政策通常更强调市场和私人企业。

⚫ 民族主义：强调本民族或国家的共同利益，既可能出现在左派，也可能出现在右派。

以上只是入门级简化。现实中，各政党的经济、文化和社会政策并不一定完全符合某一个标签。

8. 民主制度最大的价值是什么？

不是保证每个政治人物都是好人。

而是让不同利益群体能够通过选票竞争，通过制度妥协，而不是靠暴力争夺权力。

如果执政者做得不好，选民就有机会把他们换掉。

最后，记住一个最重要的道理：

不要因为某个政客喊着公平、正义、爱国，就认为他一定代表你的利益。

也不要因为某个政党自称左派、右派、自由派或保守派，就自动支持它。

真正值得关注的是：

政府收了多少钱？花到了哪里？解决了什么问题？谁获得了利益？谁承担了代价？

政治不是选一个你喜欢的口号，而是决定谁来管理公共权力、如何使用纳税人的钱，以及谁来承担最终责任。

看懂这一点，你就真正开始看懂政治了。

text:
Got sent this article by my fren and defi/options enthusiast @panterafii 

Thanks for including @GammaSwapLabs in the crypto options market map btw @Decentralisedco, it's a great article. Some thoughts:

TL;DR: Options solve problems perps can't. Unlike perps, options aren't path-dependent, meaning traders can be right on direction without getting liquidated along the way. Up to 62% of winning 20x BTC perp trades would have been liquidated first over 180 days.

Yet on-chain options are just 0.8% of perp DEX volume, compared to 3x futures contract volume in TradFi.

The article argues that portfolio margin and deeper perp liquidity can make options cheaper to hedge and more capital-efficient for market makers, unlocking adoption.

One interesting finding: outside BTC and ETH, altcoin options have virtually no liquidity. Selling vanilla options exposes MMs to potentially unbounded risk, compounded by high volatility and limited hedging liquidity.

This is where I think binary options like GammaSwap V2 have an edge.

Binaries are effectively bounded call spreads. MMs know their maximum loss upfront, making them easier to underwrite, even on long-tail assets. Buyers also benefit from no path dependence.

My thesis: Binaries will capture 0DTE expirations and long-tail assets, while vanilla options will dominate larger, longer-dated trades on major assets.

Binaries will capture 0DTE expirations and long tail assets while vanilla options will continue to succeed on bigger size, long dated large cap trades.

text:
If I could tell someone in their early 20s one thing, I would say work hard, build a career, and chase success, but don’t make the mistake of thinking that is what life is all about.

I spent years working 12 hours a day, 7 days a week. It gave me an edge, helped me get to where I am today, and shaped the person I have become. But early on the way, I realized that being good at making a living and being good at living are two very different things.

I have always been sincere about my work. I have never looked for shortcuts and have always tried to do the best I could at every job. This probably comes from how I was brought up (strict CIS parenting, with little room for joy, emotions, or the idea that doing something poorly was ever acceptable).

But there are more important things in life than professional success.

Don’t get me wrong. I still work 12 hours a day on weekdays, put in half a day on Saturdays, and work on Sundays when something important comes up. But I’ve never measured someone’s success by their career achievements or how much money they have.

From a young age, I realized that real happiness comes from other things: love, family, interests, and freedom of thought, movement, and choice.

And just by being together with my wife, I realized that no amount of money in the world will make me happier or more successful. Maybe not in the eyes of others, but certainly in my own.

I have met plenty of “successful” people when it comes to their careers. But I think most of them, if not all, have lost the bigger game in the long run. They might be great at what they do professionally, but have very little else to offer as people.

And honestly, I have fallen into this trap myself, at least partially. I can barely talk about anything other than work. When I go on vacation, I rarely switch off and find myself thinking about work instead of enjoying the break. Outside of my job, I am a pretty boring person.

That said, you have to work hard. Be honest and give your best in everything you do, whether it is your job, your relationships, or sports. Take responsibility for your life. Your decisions, your actions, and your willingness to put in the effort shape the person you become. Don’t look for shortcuts or try to play everyone around you to get on top.

Professional success and the feeling of accomplishment that comes with it are very important for most men.

But don’t become so busy making a living that you forget to make a life.

Peter Ellis just joined X to lead Product and asked for feedback.

I read xAI's open-source ranking code (Oct 24 version) this week. Three things from a 23K-follower creator:

1. One "Not interested" click costs -52; a like adds 0.66. It takes ~80 likes to undo one misclick. Please separate "not this author" from "not this topic".
2. Replies never reach non-followers. A thoughtful reply only gets seen by people who already follow you.
3. In one feed refresh, an author's second post is worth ~62% of the first, so posting several times a day works against itself.

有人问我，这是不是意味着“把真股搬上链”这件事做不成了？

不妨先换位。假想你是相关公司。接到通知说：有人要把你们股票做成链上代币去交易；30 天不书面反对≈默认同意，还很难反悔。

你会先问：股东名册对不对得上？分红和投票怎么交到链上持有人？周末价跟主板拧着走，周一谁解释？年报要不要写？对我们有什么实打实好处？

多数问题当下答得还不漂亮。反对只要一封信；沉默可能把公司锁进一场自己没选过的实验。

所以这不是“讨厌加密”，是：还没问清楚，正常人会先踩刹车。

站在 OKX 角度：我们从没想过一步到位。

做真股上链，不是发个币。要和纽交所母公司 ICE 走合规框架，要让代币持有人真正有分红权、投票权，还要一家一家过发行人同意——难，而且会挨打。

第一轮通知发出去，一定有人说不。这不是意外，是路径本身。

金融基础设施是几十年堆出来的。想搬真股上链，就必须经过发行人质疑、监管磨合、市场教育。跳过去，做成的多半是跟涨凭证，不是股东权。

OKX 选的是难路：合规、真权利、和传统市场对齐。慢一点，但走的是能留下来的路。

我们仍觉得这是趋势

因为它真的在解决传统金融的诸多痛点：美股时段对亚洲不友好、跨境入口长、结算和公司行动摩擦大、资产很难在同一套可编程层里组合。

但当下问题也要客观看： 早期流动性薄，休市价容易歪，需要价格保护和更好的市场结构，「真股」和「合成资产」仍搞不清楚 同意机制本身，就是长期信任的一部分。

一句话：反对很正常；绕开反对去擦边，才不正常。谁能把发行人的担心变成可验证的产品能力，谁才配谈下一代金融基础设施。

黑石总裁 Jon Gray 在 2026 年第三季度的市场观点视频里谈 AI 基础设施 ⬇️

1. 典型泡沫是先砸钱建产能，满足预估的未来需求，还加大量杠杆

2. 这次恰恰相反，黑石旗下公司在模型上的花费涨了20倍

3. 需求到处暴涨，供给却落后，大部分被最有钱的大公司签走

4. 审批、社区反对、涡轮机和芯片短缺，让供给离需求越来越远

Jon Gray 说今天稀缺的就是AI基础设施，所以黑石押注这个瓶颈🏗️

🔺 判断是不是泡沫，关键不在钱花得多不多，而在钱是追着真实的需求跑，还是追着想象中的需求跑。涡轮机、电厂、审批这些慢变量，反而成了最硬的门槛。

Let me tell you that for any international public figure who has business and public connection with China, three Chinese political figures are untouchable.

1st, Mao Zedong. We Europeans are all told by many political narratives particularly left from cold war time, Mao is a "dictator that murdered millions of people" . Such narrative only looked Mao's mistakes in his decision-making in his later period (he exercised those bad decision however often due to his illusion that CPC members as whole do not treat people well anymore thus he mistakenly call people to rebel, which ended into total anarchy and loss in every dimension). However, heavily neglecting his enormous positive contributions to mankind especially to the Chinese. He is the real key person that prevent Chinese nation from falling into abyss with outstand private virtue. To most Chinese, respecting chairman Mao is not a choice but a faith passed through generations.

2nd, Xi.  The taboo of offending Xi is much from the political institutional reasons. The operating of Chinese society, unlike the west, requires the leadership dignity to maintain respected, as important signals for the functionality of the whole party and its ruling in China. Belittling and mocking Chinese leaders, signaling a challenge against this governing legitimacy thus receives painful penalty. Definitely many west-valued people dont understand it and even dispose it. But if anyone wants to have positive connections with China this is something worth very serious learning. 

3rd. Sun-yet Sen. Sun is another China-savor character whom even Mao Zedong needs to pay respects to. He stood up in China's most dangerous time to launch revolution, building the republic and offering the modern civilization to the Chinese. He was well-known as the founding father of modern China and dedicated his whole life into liberation of Chinese people. For Chinese, he is another faith symbol that shall not be insulted

text:
一个百万浏览的 Launch Video 的价值越来越低

很多 AI Startup 都想凭借一条 launch video 就能 go viral，不惜花重金做视频，找KOL 转发，把曝光做到几十万或者百万，放在置顶。

结果给官推就带来几百个关注，几十个注册用户。这是当前市场的普遍情况。

推特推流算法的现状，短期容易出现集聚效应，迅速出现数据繁荣，但长期缺乏长尾价值，超过 48 小时完全没有自然流量。

推流算法是一方面，另一方面是用户侧。一条百万播放的视频可以抢占受众 1-2 秒的注意力，但今天的市场，激活一个用户平均要出现在他面前十次。

因此想较于一个 Launch Video，更重要的是 Launch 后的持续输出，直观的产品录屏、截图、或产品带来的结果。

正确的做法是：

Founder 持续展示产品（用户更愿意看到真实录屏，而不是讲概念的 launch video）、作为内容角度的“发起方”，测试不同内容形式。

重点寻找 UGC 内容创作者，将产品真实融入工作流中，在不同内容形式下对受众持续激活。（小账号可能有更忠实的内容读者）

在早期用户中寻找 use case，挖掘内容形式并转化为 UGC 内容。甚至直接帮助 Early User 成为 Creator。

将 launch video 的成本花在这些地方，对于 AI startup 早期增长有奇效。

text:
Kylian Mbappé vient de présenter ses excuses à la Chine.

Son crime ? Avoir dit en riant que son mème préféré était celui où on avait collé son visage sur celui d'un "dictateur chinois". Mao Zedong.

En 24h : trois marques chinoises le lâchent, la télévision d'État coupe la Liga, le président de la Liga s'excuse au nom de tous les clubs. Et le capitaine de l'équipe de France publie un communiqué en trois langues pour demander pardon.

En 2026, un Français doit s'excuser d'avoir dit que Mao était un dictateur.

Alors profitons-en. Puisqu'on ne peut plus le dire en rigolant, disons-le sérieusement. Et parlons de ce que ça nous dit sur nous, ici, en Europe.

Commençons par un mot qu'on utilise mal : le projet globaliste. Ce n'est pas un complot dans une cave. C'est une idée, assumée publiquement : les grandes décisions de ta vie (ta monnaie, ton identité, ta parole, ta santé, ton logement, ta mobilité) seraient mieux gérées si elles remontaient de toi vers l'État, puis de l'État vers des instances supranationales que personne n'a élues. Au nom du bien commun. Au nom de l'urgence. Au nom de l'efficacité.

Ça a un nom plus simple : la centralisation. Et la centralisation est toujours vendue comme une décision technique, jamais comme une décision politique.

Regardez les signes.

La monnaie : l'euro numérique, émis directement par la BCE, pilote en 2027, lancement visé en 2029, avec un plafond de détention. Les textes promettent qu'il ne sera pas programmable. Mais on construit l'infrastructure. Et une promesse, ça se vote, ça se dévote.

L'identité : le portefeuille d'identité numérique européen, que chaque État doit proposer à ses citoyens.

La parole : le DSA, qui oblige les plateformes à modérer selon des critères définis à Bruxelles, sous peine d'amendes jusqu'à 6% du chiffre d'affaires mondial. Et le projet Chat Control, qui revient régulièrement sur la table pour scanner les messageries privées.

Le logement : en France, interdiction de louer les logements classés G depuis 2025, les F en 2028, les E en 2034. Tu restes propriétaire sur le papier, mais c'est la norme qui décide de ce que tu as le droit d'en faire.

La consommation : tout devient abonnement. Ta musique, tes films, tes logiciels, et maintenant même certaines fonctions de ta voiture. Tu ne possèdes plus, tu loues un droit d'usage révocable.

Et puis il y a cette phrase. En 2016, le Forum économique mondial publie une vidéo, "8 prédictions pour le monde en 2030". La première : "Vous ne posséderez rien et vous serez heureux. Tout ce que vous voudrez, vous le louerez, et ce sera livré par drone."

Le WEF explique depuis que c'était un scénario, pas un objectif. Admettons. Mais quand une élite imagine le futur et que, dans ce futur, c'est toi qui ne possèdes plus rien, ça en dit long sur la manière dont elle te regarde.

Maintenant, Mao. Puisqu'on n'a plus le droit d'en rire.

1949, Mao prend le pouvoir. Première étape : la réforme agraire. On prend la terre des propriétaires et on la donne aux paysans. Les propriétaires sont jugés en public, dans des assemblées d'accusation. Entre plusieurs centaines de milliers et deux millions d'exécutions.

Les paysans sont contents. Ils ont enfin une terre.

Trois ans plus tard, on la leur reprend. Coopératives, puis communes populaires en 1958. Plus de propriété privée. Plus de cuisine chez soi : cantines collectives obligatoires. Même les casseroles sont fondues dans des hauts-fourneaux de jardin pour produire un acier inutilisable.

C'est le Grand Bond en avant. Des objectifs délirants fixés au centre. Des cadres locaux qui gonflent les chiffres par peur d'être punis. Un État qui prélève le grain sur la base de ces faux chiffres, et qui continue d'en exporter pendant que les campagnes meurent de faim. On extermine les moineaux par décret : les criquets ravagent les récoltes.

En 1959, le maréchal Peng Dehuai ose dire à Mao que ça ne marche pas. Il est purgé.

Résultat : la plus grande famine de l'histoire humaine. Entre 30 et 45 millions de morts selon les historiens qui ont travaillé dans les archives, de Yang Jisheng à Frank Dikötter.

Ça ne s'arrête pas là. En 1957, les Cent Fleurs : le Parti invite les intellectuels à critiquer librement. Ceux qui parlent sont ensuite étiquetés "droitiers", plus d'un demi-million. En 1966, la Révolution culturelle : des adolescents en brassard rouge dénoncent leurs parents, humilient leurs professeurs, brûlent les livres, détruisent les temples. Des centaines de milliers de morts, peut-être près de deux millions. Et pendant tout ce temps, le système du hukou interdit de quitter ta commune, et les tickets de rationnement décident de ce que tu manges.

Ils ne possédaient rien. Et on leur expliquait qu'ils étaient heureux.

Voilà la leçon.

很多人都在说峰哥的《马驹桥》，又是底层人多惨啦？他们真的算底层人，又真的很惨么？

14亿人，难道每人都要坐在写字楼里，月薪8000  1W的才叫不惨么？

这个社会本来就是这样子的，中国这些四五十岁的人普遍开始有活干，是从08年往后的房地产/基建的大爆发开始的，尤其是4万亿之后，社会出现了大量体力工作，
现在房地产/基建 退潮，这些工作岗位没有了，这些人自然也就没活干了。

在那之前，比今天 北京马驹桥要惨的多得多，连零工都没得干，

2000几年的时候，我们那农村的30多岁的外出打工，还都是去江浙沪要饭，就是字面意义上的乞讨，不仅居无定所，每天走到哪要到哪就睡到哪，随便睡的，一年能剩一两千，我父母也出去要过饭，

他们想要饭么？肯定不想啊！还不是什么活都找不到。

慢慢的07 08年左右，尤其是 09年往后，大基建狂飙，年轻人才开始大规模的去 服装厂/电子厂，三四十岁以上的人才开始去工地，整个社会经济巨热，变得人人都有活干了。

12年我去北京，住的也是10块钱一天的挂壁房（农民房，一个房间住6~8个人，洗漱间是公共的，连暖气都没有）在北京海淀上地六七八街附近？
每天吃的也是10块/15块钱一顿的刀削面/炒面之类，我也没觉得我哪里苦啊！
甚至我现在每天吃的饭，可能就花15块钱吃一个炒刀削面。

我完全感受不到，他们到底惨在哪里？
这个社会，只要你在大城市里，只要你想干活，随便一天不是挣100~200，
你就是愿意出去在路边要饭，一个月最少都是好几千吧？
租房一个月500~600够了，北京五六环的位置农民房大把，吃饭一个月一千，还能剩下一两千呢。

真正惨的底层是什么？是自媒体都完全不关心的，你完全看不到的，绝对被社会忽略的群体，

这是我姥，苦了一辈子，80岁了，35°的天，还在土地里刨食，一年能挣1000么？

 HL 和 Lighter 都走 CloudFront. 换 Lightsail AZ C会比A快1ms..

quoted_text:
Ondo Perps 现金奖励改版
Maker、Taker 怎么参与？

@OndoPerps 新版首周现金奖池为 22 万 USDC
比旧版每周 17.5 万增加约 25.7%

旧版主要根据交易活动和持仓分配现金奖励
新版拆成三个池子，参与方式也变了：

① 交易量池：10 万 USDC

Maker、Taker 成交都计入，按交易量参与分配。

因此，继续用 Taker 做对冲，同样可以拿现金奖励。

② 流动性池：10 万 USDC

奖励在盘口附近提供流动性的限价挂单。

当前覆盖 20 个符合条件的永续市场，报价距离中间价 0.25% 以内，单边买单或卖单都可以参与。

其中，85% 的流动性奖池分给距离中间价 0.05% 以内的订单。

比如中间价 100U，买单挂在 99.96，距离为 0.04%，就在这个区域。

author: chrismaddern
quoted_text:
how X ranks your posts (breakdown of the new algo update)

the X algo predicts how each person will react to your post, and that then decides if and where it shows up in their feed

here's how much each reaction counts, compared with a like:

> someone copies the link: 30x
> someone you follow back replies: 30x
> a reply, a quote or a DM share: 7.6x
> a follow from the post: 6x
> a repost: 1.5x
> a like: 1x
> a bookmark: 0

the negative actions weigh far more, a report is -355x a like, a mute -89x, "not interested" -79x and a block -47x

if X predicts someone is likely to mute or report your post, it ranks lower in their feed

reports get a big weight because they are rare, a report is over 1,000x less likely than a like

these rules decide how far a post can reach:

> if you have 50,000 followers or fewer, X can boost a new original post up to about 16th place in someone's feed
> the boost only works in the post's first 2 hours, and stops once the post has 200 views in the Home feed
> X boosts one post each time a feed loads, and it prefers posts that got the most likes per view from their first viewers
> after 48 hours, X stops putting your post in people's feeds
> your replies and reposts only show up in the feeds of people who follow you
> original posts can also reach people who don't follow you, X scores them 25% lower for those people
> when several of your posts compete for one person's feed, the 2nd keeps 62.5% of its score and the 3rd keeps 43.75%
> replies, quotes, DM shares and copied links only count when people find your post in their feed, so engagement from a group chat link adds nothing
> if X labels your post low quality, it shows a notice on it and people can't like, reply, repost, bookmark or share it, misinformation labels can limit it too

what I'd do with it (my read of the weights):

> post when you can reply in the first 2 hours
> write posts people want to quote, reply to or send in a DM
> reply back to accounts that follow you
> post originals when you want to reach new people

救命，为什么老外也知道了。。🤣

中国第一部全流程 AI 制作的院线长片票房扑街，居然被 @Polymarket  发到了 X 上，开始接受全球网友围观了。
这部电影叫《三星堆：未来往事》，10 月 23 日正式上映，制作团队近百人，花了两年时间，制作成本超过 1000 万元。
结果上映四天，累计票房只有约 123 万元，上座率一度跌到 0.2%，平均一场电影只有 0.3 个观众。

不过，我觉得这事其实挺值得思考的。
这几年 AI 视频生成的能力确实进步得非常快，制作一部动画电影的技术门槛正在不断下降。
但问题是，观众为什么要为一部电影买单？
AI 能把制作成本降低十倍、一百倍，却没办法自动让一个无聊的故事变得有趣。

过去电影制作昂贵，技术、资金和发行渠道本身就是门槛。
未来当制作成本越来越低，真正稀缺的东西可能会重新回到创作者身上：审美、表达、叙事能力，以及对人类情感的理解。

我依然非常看好 AI 影视的发展，但这次票房至少说明了一件事：
观众不会因为一部电影是 AI 做的，就愿意花钱走进电影院。

电影好看才是硬道理。

text:
刚看到韩国《每日经济新闻》的一条消息，阿里、腾讯、字节这些中国云巨头，正跑去跟三星和SK海力士谈判，想签长达10年、直到2035年的内存长期供应协议。

说实话，我看到这个的第一反应是，之前不是大家都在传，长鑫和长存到了2028年、2029年产能大爆发，DRAM和NAND可能就要过剩泛滥了吗？既然以后不缺货，中国巨头为什么现在还要急吼吼地去签10年的长约，这看着是不是有点自相矛盾？

但仔细盘了一下，我觉得这笔账人家算得极其精明，一点都不奇怪。

首先，这是被逼出来的安全感。美国那几个巨头（谷歌、Meta）早就挥舞着现金把未来几年的产能给锁了。阿里腾讯字节这种体量的玩家，算力需求是个无底洞。在别人都把坑占了的背景下，你要是不签长约，到时候市场上就算有货，也未必轮得到你。他们买的不是内存，是绝对的供应优先级。

其次，大家对“长期协议”有误解。长约不是现在就把十年的钱全交了，它锁定的通常是基础采购量和供应底线。说白了，行情紧的时候，你保证得给我供货；等过几年真过剩了、价格打下来了，我超出基础量的部分照样可以按便宜的市价去买。这等于用极小的代价，给自己买了一份稳赚不赔的保险。

最后，这也给咱们自己的国产存储争取了宝贵的缓冲期。长鑫和长存确实猛，但良率爬坡、真正顶起国内巨大需求量还需要时间。这十年长约，其实是一张过渡期的安全网，让巨头们在国产存储彻底成熟之前，不至于被断了粮。

所以我的看法是，这就叫时间差上的完美对冲。买10年长约，是为了防备接下来最缺货的两三年；而你们担心的2029年过剩，那是更远期的图景。用一份长约把眼前的命脉护住，同时为以后的国产替代争取时间，这才是大厂在修罗场里活下来的真实玩法。

text:
About a decade ago, Databricks got an acquisition offer at roughly six times its valuation at the time. CEO Ali Ghodsi tells the story of the conversation with Ben Horowitz that made him turn it down:

Ben: "You just don't get this good of a market opportunity with this good of an entrepreneur. That's the rarest of rare things."

"We see great entrepreneurs, but their market opportunity is limited, and then we see companies that have a great market opportunity, but the entrepreneur is not big enough to fulfill that... But this was a case where we had both."

Ali: "The acquisition offer was on the table... I had made the mistake of telling my co-founders, and they were like, 'Take your hands off the keyboard. Nobody work anymore. We're done here. Let's count my money.'"

"And I was like, 'Maybe they're right. Maybe we should just sell.' And I remember having that conversation with Ben."

"He said, 'If you sell for this number, it's really great for me. I'll pay the investors back many times over... But if you're like me, you're gonna look back the rest of your life thinking, I missed that one shot. I should have taken it all the way. And now I'll never know how far I could have taken it. So do you wanna live with that, or do you wanna just have the money?'"

"And I was like, 'Okay, thanks.' Hung up the phone. 'We're never doing this. This is not happening.'"

@alighodsi @bhorowitz

亚马逊Q3前瞻:AWS这次增速得多高市场才能满意？个人基准判断三季度营收约2035亿美元，营业利润约270亿美元，AWS增速在40%左右。关于亚马逊财报核心的几点：
1、AWS增速卖方参考大致处在高30%的增速区间，但已经有机构看得更高。如果AWS增长40%，说明业务继续加速，成绩很好。部分资金在财报前已经按照更高的增长率做了准备，公布后可能还要再多看一步：四季度能否再快一点，明年的收入预测能否继续上调？

2、更关键的还是是普通企业开始花多少钱？
这也是看微软和谷歌财报要看的核心点，我会特别关注非前沿大模型客户。原因在于，少数模型公司的算力采购，可以在短时间内把订单数字推得很高。如果企业软件、传统行业和互联网应用也开始稳定增加消费，AWS未来增长的客户基础就会更广。这方面已经有一些实证。

3、自由现金流为负也是大概率的，当然市场更关心明年资本开支是什么情况，以及预期营收增速如何？

不认为资本开支一上调，就应该直接转向悲观。只要新产能能够较快投入使用，客户持续付费，较高投入可以有合理回报。所以市场需要更具体的证据：比如，新增收入是否跟得上投入速度；新一批服务器投入服务后，利用率和利润表现怎样。

4、零售和广告则是业务基石，它们决定集团有多少利润支撑投入

详细内容看okx星球全文
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
谷歌Q3前瞻如果云业务增长翻倍，但自由现金流大概率仍为负，市场怎么看？
市场对这份财报的预期已经很高。总营收共识约1279亿美元（+25%），云收入最新一致预期约291.6亿美元（+92%），搜索约+15%，YouTube广告约+11%。聊聊谷歌Q3财报最受关注的几点：
1、云业务接近翻倍，但还看营收质量 增长大概率落在95%-100%区间。但二季度起确认的TPU系统外销（交付到客户自有数据中心）会抬高数字，真正看点是剔除后原有云服务增速、传统企业消费是否加速，以及利润率（预期33%-35%，受第三方算力与Wiz整合影响略有压力）。

2、企业订单占比扩散很重要（这点与昨天聊微软财报前瞻里是一致的） Ryanair、法国巴黎银行等五年合作案例显示，非模型实验室客户开始用经营预算为AI买单。接近80%云客户已用AI产品、近90%财富100强用Gemini Enterprise，但接下来要看使用深度与持续付费。

3、资本开支与自由现金流是最大焦点 2026年Capex指引1950-2050亿美元，上半年已花约806亿，下半年压力大。2027年投行预期普遍3000亿美元以上。FCF大概率为负（含约52亿美元Android旧案罚款支付等），需拆出一次性项目再判断持续现金创造能力。

好的支出是提前到货+高利用率+客户提前付款；
坏的是成本上涨或回款持续后移。

EPS与利润率要穿透一次因素，去年有投资收益和欧盟罚款扰动，今年若有股权投资收益或报告利润率改善，要先看主营业务贡献。

总营收超预期（1285-1305亿美元），云95%-100%、搜索15%-17%，业务趋势偏乐观。但市场已计入强劲云增长，真正决定股价的是增长质量（剔除系统销售后的服务消费）、企业持续付费意愿，以及2027年Capex是否失控、现金流展望能否改善。

整体来看：
1）若明年资本开支没有明显超出市场假设，现金流展望也有所改善，这份财报的支撑就比较充分。
2）反过来，如果增长主要靠集中交付，云利润率和回款弱于预期，管理层又继续大幅增加支出，我会下调对资本回报的预期。

详细看OKX星球全文

如果你觉得有任何地方可以增加安全环节、避免被滥用、协助更负责任的使用，也可以评论或私信 @Peer_zh 看能否优化改进入产品中。

另一些朋友和我一样觉得 Peer 非常酷 ——— 我是 24 年左右在 @GCCofCommons 主持的 @gitcoin Asia Round 中注意到 @zkp2p 的，当时就觉得是同批中最酷的一个。

如果比特币是  Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System；

两年过去他们从 ZKEmail 换到 ZK TLS 换到现在的 TEE，尝试了多种背后的解决方案。
两年过去他们也在美国本土年流水大概 2200 万美元左右。每笔成交中位数大约就是我一直在测试的 50 美元左右。

text:
我想谈谈未来的AI的就业影响和关乎每个人的未来的事情。没有人，可以独善其身。我就不用某些公司改良派的风格去阐述了，就聊点普罗大众会经历的事情。

很多人可能看完这篇原帖，里面的内容是看不太明白的，也不太理解这件事意味着什么，对你我有什么意义。就这样说吧，如果这次OAI的三个科学难题成果全部正式，人类即将面临工业革命以来最彻底的智力生产力重组。2027的预言，很有可能是对了，不是危言耸听，也不是空穴来风。

知识工作的价值将被重估。 设想一下，如果最难的数学、理论计算机都能被 AI 攻克，那法律分析、药物研发、工程设计这些依赖推理的工作，被改变只是时间问题。职业规划，彻底没用了。

而且科研体系要重建规则。 功劳算谁的？论文还怎么审？经费该投给谁？这都是很大的悬而未决的问题。而且我记得OpenAI 自己也承认他们在试验发布方式。这套规则几百年没大变过，现在必须重写了。

就物质和经济层面而言，药器企研发成本将会遭遇几波断崖式下跌与效率暴增。具体哪些领域不知道，但是一定会有这个趋势。因为在药企，以往研发一款新药需要耗时十年、耗资数十亿美元，在半导体行业，设计一块新芯片需要成百上千顶级工程师熬夜数月。你可以想一下，如果 AI 具备了这种独立攻克极限数学难题的强推理能力，它就可以在几天甚至几小时内完成这些工作。药物、材料、工程设计的研发周期将被缩短到不可思议的程度，全社会的物质财富生产速率将迎来指数级的大爆发。

几个月内，资本市场的财富大转移也是可能的。传统的软件、外包、基础法律和常规工程设计公司的估值可能会在几天内缩水大半。而掌握了这一核心推理能力的极少数 AI 巨头，其经济体量和吸金能力将膨胀到富可敌国的地步，资本会以疯狂的涌向这些科技垄断新贵。这就是垄断。我不好说那个时候模型是否会完全发放给所有人。

过去几十年，社会最精英的阶层都挤在医生、律师、投行分析师、资深架构师这些依赖高强度脑力与推理的行业，享受着高额的薪水与崇高的社会地位。
想想几年前吧，麦肯锡多火啊，高盛的初级分析师多火啊，未来，你们去看看吧。当 AI 证明它能搞定人类智力最顶尖的数学证明时，就意味着这些依赖规则、案例和强推理的白领工作，其劳动力价值将面临极大的被稀释风险。

人类即将面临行业门槛的全面降维。
一个人不再需要苦学十年法律才能做案情分析，不需要苦学八年医学才能做诊断。他可能能会有，完全不同的未来。但是究竟是好的还是坏的，我不敢断言。

如果这套能够改写计算机科学和密码学底层的能力死死锁在一家公司的内部模型里，外界看不到，这已经超越单纯的商业竞争。
因为这家公司将拥有对全社会数字大厦的绝对解释权，甚至能无声无息地破解目前世界上所有的传统加密体系。 防止这种力量被滥用的问题，要不要在物质层面强行收归国有或进行极限监管的问题，会变成各国政府最头疼、也最惊心动魄的政治博弈。

做题意义的消亡，教育规则的重写，将无法估量，无法想象……
author: Phoenixyin13
quoted_text:
不想传播焦虑，但这次我无话可说。

今年科学界最大的新闻，没有之一。OpenAI 的内部 AI 模型自己做出了三个科学难题的成果。我用我自己的理解说一下。
第一，Kakeya 猜想。这个问题研究波聚焦时会怎样。原来的猜想我记得是说最极端的聚焦只会持续很短时间。人类以前只在低维度证明过，OpenAI 说它的模型证明了所有维度的情况，因此顺带解决了 Kakeya 猜想和 Stein 限制猜想。纯逆天。

第二，指数时间假说 ETH 被推翻。这个太难以置信了。ETH 好像是说有一类逻辑难题不可能被比暴力穷举快很多地解决。而之前学界普遍相信它成立，几百篇论文都以它为前提，现在 AI 却证明它是错的。
这个太他喵逆天了，因为我之前是研究过一段时间理论计算机的。这几十年ETH几乎被当成公理在用。很多论文的结论都写成假设 ETH 成立，那么某某问题不可能在多少时间内解决。现在地基没了，这些不可能，全都要打问号。
最让我感觉匪夷所思的是 AI 证明的方式。据 Lean 证明的说明文档，它给出的是一个确定性算法，应该是对固定宽度的 k-CNF 公式，它能在亚指数时间、多项式空间内精确数出所有满足的赋值。但是，懂行的人应该都知道“数出有多少个解”通常比“判断有没有解”难得多，它连更难的那个都做到了，所以 ETH 只是顺带被推翻。

第三，杨-米尔斯、量子色动力学。AI 应该是给出了一套严格的数学证明，证明描述强核力的理论在数学上确实成立，其中包括纯杨-米尔斯理论的存在性，这是千禧年七大难题之一的一部分。我不太了解，但是只是知道一些浅层的理论，就不评论了。

最让我恐惧和惊骇的是第二个。今天晚上我看了又看，感觉这是地震级别。如果最终确认无误，这会是 AI 第一次独立推翻一个被广泛相信的核心猜想。说它是一个时代的分界点，也毫不夸张。
如果这三个都核查通过，这代表 AI 第一次在多个顶尖领域独立解决了几十年没人能解决的难题，影响史无前例。

quoted_text:
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

Introducing FrontierCode 2.0: our new coding benchmark that measures a model’s ability to go beyond the spec.

Most coding evals measure a model’s ability to write code that meets a spec. With FrontierCode 1.0, we asked a new question: would you actually merge the PR?

FrontierCode 2.0 is comprised of more diverse tasks, featuring larger scopes and higher mergeability standards. We are now asking: not only would you merge this PR, but should you?

One key feature of FrontierCode 2.0 is underspecified prompts. Rather than including every engineering decision, prompts are deliberately ambiguous, giving the models room to demonstrate their judgment.

The result is a benchmark that is far from saturated, with the top model scoring just 45%.

text:
A scout drove out to a junior college in Missouri to watch him throw, and he walked eight batters in a row.

That is the story everybody tells. Somebody brought it up again this month and he corrected them.

It was nine.

They drafted him anyway. Fourth round, 2018.

Aaron Ashby is from Kansas City, Missouri, out of Park Hill High School. His uncle Andy pitched fourteen seasons in the big leagues and made two All-Star teams.

The Texas Rangers had taken him the year before that, in the 25th round, 764th overall. He turned it down and went back to the junior college.

His first big league appearance was two thirds of an inning and four earned runs.

Two seasons later he went 2 and 10 as a starter. Milwaukee signed him to a five year extension anyway, and then his shoulder went.

Arthroscopic surgery. He lost all of 2023. He says he has never gotten the slider he had in college back, not once, not all the way.

Then 2024 at Triple-A Nashville, a 8.04 ERA across 25 games. That is the number teams look at when they decide somebody is finished.

In August of that year, still in Nashville, he started messing with a knuckle-curve. He was in Milwaukee about a week later.

Last season he put up a 2.16 out of the bullpen. This season he went 13 and 3.

And then October started and he just stopped giving up runs.

Fifteen and two thirds scoreless innings to open this postseason. Five hits. Three walks. Seventeen strikeouts. He has pitched in eight of the Milwaukee Brewers ten playoff games and every single one at home.

He is one out away from the record. Andrew Miller went sixteen scoreless to start the 2016 postseason and nobody has matched it. Ashby passed Goose Gossage and Andy Hawkins to get here.

Pat Murphy watched him get a five out save in Game 2 Saturday and called it Goose Gossage-like.

He is also the first pitcher in the history of the postseason to record at least five outs in six straight appearances without allowing a run in any of them.

The pitch doing it is the curveball he was not supposed to have. Miguel Sano hit the fifth curveball he ever threw in the big leagues over the wall, back in August 2021.

He has thrown 1,045 of them since. Not one has left the yard.

They asked him how he stays that calm with the tying run on second in the ninth.

"It's a lot of breathing."

"Just kind of praying for peace, I guess."

Be straight about where this sits. Milwaukee is up 2-0 but the next three are in Tampa Bay, the Rays won 94 games, and nobody finishes a postseason at 0.00.

But a kid walked nine straight hitters with a scout in the stands, and a week from now he might own the record for the best October any bullpen arm has ever had.

text:
gm gm here we go again.

This morning somebody abused a bug in ApeStr to swap 21 apes for 21 ApeStr-owned apes.

This was a known exploit (see the SQUIGSTR exploit from ~1 year ago) but incentive to run it was never there.

The bug lies in buyTargetNFT: it forces a strategy contract to send arbitrary calldata to any target. Afterwards it checks only three things: its BAYC balance rose by exactly 1, it owns expectedId, and "cost" equals its ETH balance drop.

This was patched in later NFTStrategy releases, but affects the original 6 (PunkSTR not affected).

The attacker bought 2 BAYC to use as bait. Using a helper contract, they prep the strategy contract by selling an ape to it for 5 wei and immediately buying it back for 6 wei. That primes the contract's ethToTwap with 6 wei.

They then call buyTargetNFT and pass the calldata to transfer an ape from ApeSTR to the helper using safeTransferFrom. This in turn hands execution over to the helper (remember, safeTransferFrom is NOT safe), which transfer TWO apes back to ApeSTR to satisfy the balance check (1 out, 2 in leaves ApeSTR at +1). It also calls processTokenTwap, which converts the 6 wei, setting the cost of one of the newly deposited apes to 7 wei (6 * 120%). The helper contract buys it back in the same tx.

example flow: 
- Attacker has BAYC #1 and #2. ApeSTR has BAYC #3. 
- Attacker "sells" BAYC #1 to ApeSTR for 6 wei and sends BAYC #2 to it for free, but steals BAYC #3 in the process.
- ApeSTR relists BAYC #1 for 7 wei, which the attacker buys.
- Attacker now has BAYC #1 and BAYC #3, and ApeSTR has BAYC #2 (but doesn't even know it).

The attacker ran this for all 21 BAYC in the ApeSTR contract, resulting in them being able to claim packs for all of those BAYC. Total net proceeds: $14k.

This previously affected SQUIGSTR because of their shared contract - any art blocks NFT sent in would satisfy the balance check, allowing the attacker to drain the contract of squiggles in exchange for basically valueless art blocks NFTs.

It was known to be possible on ApeSTR as well, so I guess it was just a matter of time before we saw it happen.

The unfortunate consequence is that now, ApeSTR has 21 apes that it is completely unaware of, so they cannot be bought from the contract. And 210 attacker-owned mudwater packs were dumped into bids.
