Security risks (AI-driven hacks, mathematical breakthroughs & quantum computing) have become increasingly concerning in recent weeks both personally & for the broader market. 

$ZEC looks like the best way to play this, and the market is already showing us that with clear divergence vs BTC/ETH/SOL/HYPE/TOTAL3ES over the past couple weeks.

Additionally, short-term spot & derivatives positioning looks significantly cleaner vs earlier this month. ETF flows have just flipped positive again after ~3 weeks of outflows, while coin-denominated OI is at its lowest level since August.

Separately, OTC desks are still seeing strong interest from liquid & VC funds, with ZEC reportedly remaining one of the most bought altcoins by funds even at these elevated prices.

I generally view protocol upgrades as weak catalysts in isolation, but the January upgrade feels different. Tachyon addresses the scalability improvements the community has been waiting for, while the quantum component of the upgrade addresses one of the highest mindshare risks to the industry. Together, I think they make for a much stronger catalyst than either would on its own.

I haven’t looked too deeply into the underlying tech or whether the proposed upgrades will actually deliver meaningful quantum resistance, and I don’t care to. When all the tastemakers (Naval, Balaji, a16z, Paradigm, Dragonfly & Multicoin) are pushing the ZEC narrative as a hedge against BTC, the realities of what it’s tech can or can’t actually do aren’t part of the thesis.

The combination of improving positioning, continued institutional demand, relative strength & an increasingly powerful narrative makes for an attractive setup, even in shaky market conditions. I expect my conviction to continue building as we approach January.

I have no strong view on market direction over the coming months, and the quantum tailwind for ZEC is a headwind for BTC, so I’m hedged vs BTC on a vol-adjusted basis, but think a naked long is also justified.

Quantum is the crypto equivalent of cancer and ZEC is the cure. Don’t find yourself Zidelined on the road past $2k

text:
Is PumpFun killing memecoin runners?

The team says “no”by comparing its fees with Raydium, Stonkfun and Pons

Okay so here’s the drama

The timeline has been calling out PumpFun’s fee changes

Since September 2025 only 3 tokens have managed to reach a $100M market cap

To prove his point, we take every token that reached $100M at ATH, remove obvious honeypots and put everything on a timeline

The graph looks terrible (check picture lol)

And the argument is pretty simple

PumpFun introduced PumpSwap, changed the fee structure and somehow we went from having massive memecoin runners to barely seeing anything reach $100M

Now json responds

He says the graph is basically propaganda because it’s blaming an entire bear market on one AMM

And points out three things the original graph ignores:

- the $TRUMP launch, which helped create the blow-off top on Solana

- the October 10 liquidation event and its consequences

- the decline in PumpFun trading volumes

And finally he actually shares the fee comparison between the old Raydium system and PumpSwap

Before PumpSwap, graduated tokens moved to Raydium V4

A trade on a $100M+ token cost 0.25%

0.22% went to liquidity providers
0.03% went to Raydium
PumpFun received nothing

Now with PumpSwap, the same trade costs 0.30%

0.20% goes to liquidity providers
0.05% goes to PumpFun
0.05% goes to holders or creators

So yes, trading fees increased

From 0.25% to 0.30%

And PumpFun went from receiving 0% to receiving 0.05% on these trades

json argues that the main difference is the introduction of holder rewards and creator fees, which were added after PumpSwap launched

He also explains that fees are higher on smaller tokens and decrease as market cap grows

And ends up bringing the competition

Post-bonding protocol fees:

PumpFun: 0.05%
Stonkfun: 1%
Pons: 0.30%

So from his POV, PumpFun isn’t even the most extractive launchpad when comparing protocol fees

text:
LIQUID AI LAUNCHES SIX AI MODELS YOU CAN CUSTOMIZE ON ONE GPU

Its new LFM3 family covers text, images, video, voice and structured decisions, with models around 2 billion parameters designed to run on your own hardware.

One result stands out: in Liquid’s evaluation across 62 vision benchmarks, its 1.9B-parameter vision model matched Gemma 4 12B’s average score of 71.4, using roughly one-sixth the parameters.

Here’s what the lineup can do:

• Text: a 256K-token context window for agents that use tools, work through documents and carry out tasks across browsers and business apps.

• Vision: understand images and video, reason through charts and locate objects within a scene.

• Audio: voice conversations and tool calls in 18 languages. The Omni model combines vision, audio and language, so an assistant can respond to what you show it and tell it.

• Decisions: return structured answers with calibrated probabilities in a single pass, giving applications outputs they can act on.

Under the hood, LFM3 combines gated short convolutions, sliding-window attention and global attention. Liquid designed this architecture to improve capability per parameter and keep inference efficient over long contexts.

The practical use case is specialization. Developers can adapt a model to their own data and tools, then deploy it locally. Liquid demonstrated this by fine-tuning its vision model for wind-turbine inspections using a few hours on one A100 GPU.

That gives businesses a way to build task-specific assistants on hardware they control, without a per-token API charge for local inference.

Up to 100% of men have microplastics in their semen

I got mine to zero. The first documented case.

A 2024 study detected microplastics in 100% of human and dog testicular tissue.

In another study, microplastics were detected in the semen and urine of all of 113 tested men from China.

Researchers broke down plastic type and how they affected sperm quality.

The most common came from packaging (polystyrene, polypropylene, and polyethylene).

PTFE, the synthetic polymer used in non-stick Teflon pans, proved the most lethal, creating 11% lower sperm concentration and 9% fewer total sperm.

author: bryan_johnson
quoted_text:
🚨 I HAVE NO MICROPLASTICS IN MY BALLS 🚨

This should not be possible.

Studies show that 100% of men have microplastics in their semen. I am the first human ever to show a complete reduction to zero.

This may be a world-first breakthrough in fertility research.

I had 165 microplastic particles in my semen just 18 months ago. Now, I have zero.

Five published studies have measured microplastics in human semen. Two found them in 100% of men. The other three found then in 44 to 76% of men tested, but those used methods that miss the smallest particles and the clear ones. Corrected for that, the real rate is likely 100%. Almost every man alive has plastic in his semen right now. The same applies to testicular tissue, testing 100% positive for microplastics.

Microplastics hurt sperm.

Human studies show the impact of various types of plastic, associated chemicals, and other toxins on male fertility:

+ 60% fewer normal shaped sperm (from PFAS)
+ 5x higher odds of low sperm count (from PTFE)
+ 10% lower sperm concentration (from PTFE)
+ 15% lower swimming ability (from PTFE)
+ 41% lower swimming ability (from PET)
+ 12% lower sperm swimming ability (from BPA)
+ 3x higher odds of low sperm count (from Phthalates)
+ 2x higher odds of poor swimming (from Phthalates)

The effects compound: each extra type of plastic drops sperm swimming ability by about 21%.

This matters even if you’re NOT trying to get pregnant.

Sperm count is one of the cleanest biomarkers of overall health we have. And microplastics don't stop at the testes.

The same particles are showing up everywhere we look. Studies show 4.5x higher rate of heart attack, stroke, and death in people with microplastics in their arterial plaque vs. those without. Microplastics were also found in 100% of human placentas tested.

100% of post-mortem human brains tested positive for microplastics. Brain concentrations rose ~50% between 2016 and 2024, and now sit at roughly 11x the levels found in the liver or kidney.

Where do these come from?
+ PTFE, commonly in non-stick pans
+ PET, water bottles
+ Phthalates, makes plastic soft and bendy
+ BPA, can linings
+ PFAS, stain-resistant fabrics & food packaging

Inside the body, plastic causes a kind of cellular rust. It triggers inflammation in the testicles, kills the cells that make sperm and drops testosterone. It's been confirmed across 39 animal and cell studies, then in human data.

MY PROTOCOL:

Note, what I did is n=1, not a controlled trial, I cannot prove cause.

1. Sauna (dry). My toxin blood panel confirms sauna clears plastic related chemicals: BPA, phthalates, PFAS, flame retardants, pesticides. The plastic particles themselves are too big to sweat out directly. Heat may activate other clearance routes: bile flow through the liver, the cell's internal cleanup system, and the gut barrier. Humans have almost no enzymes that can break plastic apart, so the body has to physically push it out.

2. Reverse osmosis water filter. Drinking water is likely a major source of microplastic getting into your body. A reverse osmosis filter pushes water through a very tight membrane and strains the particles out. I filter everything I drink.

3. Trying to rid my environment of the big plastic items: cutting boards, cups, plates, food storage containers, non-stick pans, cling wrap, tea bags, water bottles, kitchen utensils, kettles, and synthetic clothing. Note, as hard as I try, I'm always finding new plastic things in my life. This can be all-consuming thing so try to just knock out the big ones.

I did all three interventions at the same time. I cannot say which one did the most work. What I can say is this: going from 165 to zero in 18 months is possible.

Results:
Nov 2024: 165 particles/mL
Jul 2025: 20 particles/mL
Apr 2026: 0 particles/mL

The 18 month window also captures roughly 7 full spermatogenesis cycles.

亚马逊、谷歌、博通、AMD 四家合计向 Anthropic 提供或承诺了约 1333 亿美元资金，换回了约 4057 亿美元的算力订单，每投进来 1 美元，大约换回 3 美元的订单。

Anthropic 用很少的现金，就锁住了远超自身体量的算力；也云大厂把对 Anthropic 的投资，变成了自家云和芯片的订单。

最终预定的算力一定要把token卖掉，上市融资以后钱不缺了， 6 月末现金加短期投资约 1317 亿美元，另有 770 亿美元没提的战略票据额度、150 亿美元循环贷款。

不过4057 亿的算力刚性付款协议，意味着 Anthropic 一旦出现类似三季度的竞争局面恶化，几乎一定会降价，上市以后财报也是透明。

当下有产能锁定，需求增长，token价格还能保住。但是锁定刚付的算力产能不管如何是硬性的成本，token卖不完，降价也得卖，这和清库存一个道理。

所以到时候没人会保价格，渗透率才是第一。如果市场基建过度投入，那未来2年内就可以验证。

author: ripe0x
quoted_text:
gm gm here we go again.

This morning somebody abused a bug in ApeStr to swap 21 apes for 21 ApeStr-owned apes.

This was a known exploit (see the SQUIGSTR exploit from ~1 year ago) but incentive to run it was never there.

The bug lies in buyTargetNFT: it forces a strategy contract to send arbitrary calldata to any target. Afterwards it checks only three things: its BAYC balance rose by exactly 1, it owns expectedId, and "cost" equals its ETH balance drop.

This was patched in later NFTStrategy releases, but affects the original 6 (PunkSTR not affected).

The attacker bought 2 BAYC to use as bait. Using a helper contract, they prep the strategy contract by selling an ape to it for 5 wei and immediately buying it back for 6 wei. That primes the contract's ethToTwap with 6 wei.

They then call buyTargetNFT and pass the calldata to transfer an ape from ApeSTR to the helper using safeTransferFrom. This in turn hands execution over to the helper (remember, safeTransferFrom is NOT safe), which transfer TWO apes back to ApeSTR to satisfy the balance check (1 out, 2 in leaves ApeSTR at +1). It also calls processTokenTwap, which converts the 6 wei, setting the cost of one of the newly deposited apes to 7 wei (6 * 120%). The helper contract buys it back in the same tx.

example flow: 
- Attacker has BAYC #1 and #2. ApeSTR has BAYC #3. 
- Attacker "sells" BAYC #1 to ApeSTR for 6 wei and sends BAYC #2 to it for free, but steals BAYC #3 in the process.
- ApeSTR relists BAYC #1 for 7 wei, which the attacker buys.
- Attacker now has BAYC #1 and BAYC #3, and ApeSTR has BAYC #2 (but doesn't even know it).

The attacker ran this for all 21 BAYC in the ApeSTR contract, resulting in them being able to claim packs for all of those BAYC. Total net proceeds: $14k.

This previously affected SQUIGSTR because of their shared contract - any art blocks NFT sent in would satisfy the balance check, allowing the attacker to drain the contract of squiggles in exchange for basically valueless art blocks NFTs.

It was known to be possible on ApeSTR as well, so I guess it was just a matter of time before we saw it happen.

The unfortunate consequence is that now, ApeSTR has 21 apes that it is completely unaware of, so they cannot be bought from the contract. And 210 attacker-owned mudwater packs were dumped into bids.

Everyone wants another PEPE style runner, but nobody understands why PEPE happened.

Back then, there was barely anything to trade onchain. Liquidity was concentrated, people had patience, and they actually HELD.

And let's not pretend PEPE was some 100% organic miracle. There were claims of around 30% bundled supply. The difference was that a floor was built and people had bigger targets.

Today, everyone wants to sell to the very next guy who buys after them.

We've completely fucked up our psychology.

Nobody wants to build a floor. Nobody wants to hold. Everybody wants to extract.

And guess who's actually getting rich? The platforms and protocols collecting fees on every transaction.

I dump on you. You dump on someone else. We all lose money while the platforms print.

We don't have a liquidity problem alone. We have a conviction problem.

text:
AI 用 24 天让计算机核对完数学史上最长的证明：定理成立，但其中一篇论文的证法有漏洞，AI 换了一种证法补上

一个证明长达 1.5 万页，散落在 500 多篇论文里，几十年来没有一个人从头到尾读完过，它到底对不对？AI 数学公司 Axiom 10 月 26 日宣布，他们用几十个 AI agent 花了 24 天，把这个证明全部改写成计算机能逐步检查的代码，Axiom 说检查已经全部通过。

这个证明对应的是“有限单群分类定理”，外号“巨大定理”，约 100 位数学家花了几十年才完成。

【这个定理讲什么】

先说“群”。一个立方体，你能找到 24 种转法，转完它看起来跟没动过一样。数学家把这样一组“转完看起来不变的操作”叫做一个群，它是研究对称的工具。

整数可以拆成质数相乘，质数再也拆不动。群也一样，可以拆成一些拆不动的基本单位，叫“单群”。有限单群分类定理给出了一张完整清单：所有基本单位，要么属于几个有固定规律的大家族，要么是 26 个不属于任何家族的特例。最大的特例叫“魔群”，元素个数是 8 后面跟 53 个零。

找到这些单群不算最难，难的是证明清单里没有漏掉任何一个。

【为什么要计算机来查】

证明太长，人查不过来，出过错也不奇怪。1983 年，牵头的数学家宣布证明完成，后来发现其中一块根本没写完，直到 2004 年才用一本 1221 页的书补上。

Axiom 用的检查工具叫 Lean。把证明翻译成 Lean 能读的代码后，它会一步一步核对：每一步是不是真的能从前面推出来。人读论文时会默认“这步显然成立”，Lean 不接受，必须写出来。2012 年有团队用类似工具，花了约 6 年才查完这个定理里一篇 255 页的论文。

【查出了什么】

先说结论：定理本身没错，清单还是那张清单。

问题出在中间一篇论文的证法上。整个证明要用到一个叫“不平衡群定理”的中间结论，Axiom 照着数学家 John Walter 1986 年给出的证明来翻译，AI 发现这个证明里引用的一个说法是错的，并举出了具体的反例。好比一道几何题，答案是对的，但书上的解法中间用了一个不成立的条件，解法得换。

Axiom 请教了当年参与原始证明的数学家 Richard Lyons 和 Ronald Solomon，借用 Solomon 1976 年的一套思路，由 Axiom 的 AI 写出一个新证法，绕开了出错的那一步，也通过了 Lean 的检查。新证法已经整理成一篇 35 页的论文。

除此之外，查出来的大多是笔误、表格写错、少写了前提这类小毛病。Axiom 博客说其中 34 处值得专门处理，完整清单还没公布。Axiom 的推文说法更重，称修了“几百处重大勘误”。

【AI 怎么干的】

几十个 AI agent 分工：有的把大的论证拆成小定理，有的去找已有结果，有的写 Lean 代码。人类数学家处理 AI 卡住的数学难题，工程师维护系统。最后写出约 4310 万行代码（推文说约 5000 万行，博客和官网都是 4310 万），其中约 120 万行来自清华大学求真书院团队此前开源的同类项目。

AI 有时会把还没证明的东西直接当成已知条件用，Axiom 发现后删掉了几万行代码重来。用的是哪些 AI 模型，Axiom 没说。

【能全信吗】

Lean 能保证推导的每一步都对，但它判断不了代码开头写的那句“定理”是不是真的就是有限单群分类定理。如果这句话翻译走了样，后面证得再对，证的也是另一件事。这部分只能靠人读。Axiom 邀请群论学家和 Lean 社区自己重跑检查、核对这句话。目前这还是 Axiom 自己的发布，还没有外部独立核查的结果。

项目网站：https://t.co/3ArK3yFvEt
Axiom 推文：https://t.co/BPNOxbaIqH

text:
Just spoke to the Head of AI at a huge company. 

The #1 thing they're struggling with is... what do I do with the AI laggards at our company? 

Like most companies, they’ve found that a Super Pareto Principle is true within their org. 10% of their employees are responsible for 90% of the uplift in productivity/token usage from software engineering to non-technical knowledge work. 

They’ve spent a lot of time & resources on AI enablement from LLM foundations to function-specific trainings and skill building. And yet, the power law of productivity increases hasn’t budged. 

So now they’re left with a few sobering thoughts and hard questions:
1) 90% of people are overpaid and 10% are underpaid 
2) We’d be better off allocating tokens proportionally to the power law, but how do we do that without killing culture? 
3) Significant layoffs are likely warranted and wouldn’t impact overall output, but cultural backlash is a big concern? 
4) How do we hire more power law people as a non technology company? 
5) Is all of our efforts on training and enablement ACTUALLY worth it? 
6) How do we not experience a brain drain where the top 10% all leave because they want to be surrounded by other AI-native 10x’ers?

text:
Three audio attacks can sound similar to a listener.
They are not the same data problem.

𝐓𝐄𝐗𝐓-𝐓𝐎-𝐒𝐏𝐄𝐄𝐂𝐇 (𝐓𝐓𝐒)
A system generates speech from text. The audio is synthetic at the source.

𝐕𝐎𝐈𝐂𝐄 𝐂𝐎𝐍𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐒𝐈𝐎𝐍 (𝐕𝐂)
A person's speech is transformed toward another voice. The input is human speech, but the output has been modified.

𝐑𝐄𝐏𝐋𝐀𝐘
A genuine recording is played through a device and captured again. The voice may be authentic; the playback and recording chain are the attack.

Why separate them?

Because an anti-spoofing evaluation needs to show which mechanism was tested, not just report one combined “fake audio” score.

Depending on the product, coverage may need to vary by source speaker, target voice, playback device, microphone, distance, room acoustics, and background conditions.

Bona fide speech is also necessary as a reference: the system must distinguish attacks without treating every unusual recording as fake.

A model tested on one attack family has not automatically been evaluated on the others.

Define the attack taxonomy before you define the hours.
#VoiceAI #SpeechData #AntiSpoofing #ModelEvaluation

author: 0xQuit
quoted_text:
gm gm here we go again.

This morning somebody abused a bug in ApeStr to swap 21 apes for 21 ApeStr-owned apes.

This was a known exploit (see the SQUIGSTR exploit from ~1 year ago) but incentive to run it was never there.

The bug lies in buyTargetNFT: it forces a strategy contract to send arbitrary calldata to any target. Afterwards it checks only three things: its BAYC balance rose by exactly 1, it owns expectedId, and "cost" equals its ETH balance drop.

This was patched in later NFTStrategy releases, but affects the original 6 (PunkSTR not affected).

The attacker bought 2 BAYC to use as bait. Using a helper contract, they prep the strategy contract by selling an ape to it for 5 wei and immediately buying it back for 6 wei. That primes the contract's ethToTwap with 6 wei.

They then call buyTargetNFT and pass the calldata to transfer an ape from ApeSTR to the helper using safeTransferFrom. This in turn hands execution over to the helper (remember, safeTransferFrom is NOT safe), which transfer TWO apes back to ApeSTR to satisfy the balance check (1 out, 2 in leaves ApeSTR at +1). It also calls processTokenTwap, which converts the 6 wei, setting the cost of one of the newly deposited apes to 7 wei (6 * 120%). The helper contract buys it back in the same tx.

example flow: 
- Attacker has BAYC #1 and #2. ApeSTR has BAYC #3. 
- Attacker "sells" BAYC #1 to ApeSTR for 6 wei and sends BAYC #2 to it for free, but steals BAYC #3 in the process.
- ApeSTR relists BAYC #1 for 7 wei, which the attacker buys.
- Attacker now has BAYC #1 and BAYC #3, and ApeSTR has BAYC #2 (but doesn't even know it).

The attacker ran this for all 21 BAYC in the ApeSTR contract, resulting in them being able to claim packs for all of those BAYC. Total net proceeds: $14k.

This previously affected SQUIGSTR because of their shared contract - any art blocks NFT sent in would satisfy the balance check, allowing the attacker to drain the contract of squiggles in exchange for basically valueless art blocks NFTs.

It was known to be possible on ApeSTR as well, so I guess it was just a matter of time before we saw it happen.

The unfortunate consequence is that now, ApeSTR has 21 apes that it is completely unaware of, so they cannot be bought from the contract. And 210 attacker-owned mudwater packs were dumped into bids.

author: RobertSagurton
quoted_text:
There’s still a lot of misinformation about perpetual futures floating around.

Let’s start with the premise that a futures contract has to expire. Where does it say that in the statute?

Calling a perp a swap doesn’t create a different risk to the financial system.  What matters is how the contract is margined, cleared and managed when someone defaults. If a perp can operate with the same safeguards as a traditional future, why should the absence of an expiration date exclude it from that framework?

Then there’s the claim that perps necessarily come with massive leverage and auto-deleveraging. That's just totally wrong. You absolutely can build a perp with reasonable leverage and no ADL. You could also build a quarterly futures contract with massive leverage and auto-deleveraging. Those are design choices.

I’m in favor of perps because they can address real inefficiencies in existing markets. An oil ETF could maintain its exposure without the trading costs and slippage of predictably rolling futures. A stock perp could pass the economic benefit of hard-to-borrow demand to the long holder—value that rarely reaches retail shareholders today.

Producers still need traditional futures to hedge forward production. Perps complement those contracts. List both. Let people use the instrument that meets their needs.

More from my discussion with @TheStalwart and @tracyalloway on Odd Lots: https://t.co/tYJl2zfxqR

text:
I think I've identified the Predict Fun Exploit

The third party responsible for the hack is likely @ApidogHQ  & @algolia 

Archived https://t.co/XsZGodXryP pages identify Apidog as the documentation platform, with Algolia powering its configured search.

1. predict fun accidentally left their website’s administrative "search index keys" open to the public on an API doc.

2. Using that key, hackers injected 36 fake, poisonous search results (ADT-N-0 to ADT-N-z). Because they mapped to every letter and number, typing any character triggered them.

3.  When developers or users searched for anything on the docs site, the database instantly fetched the hacker's fake, infected data.

4. The website used a risky coding method (dangerouslySetInnerHTML) to load search results, blindly running the hacker's hidden script without checking it first.

5. Once the script ran, hackers could spy on the browser, hijack active sessions, and steal wallet keys or redirect crypto transactions.

Japan's Disaster Management Minister is preparing a nationwide emergency request for November 2, urging households to stockpile enough supplies to survive for at least 3 days, ideally a full week.

The government is preparing for several major threats:

• A massive earthquake along the Nankai Trough.
• A powerful earthquake directly beneath Tokyo.
• A possible eruption of Mount Fuji.

Any one of these disasters could destroy buildings, shut down power and water supplies, and leave millions of people without basic services.

People are being advised to store food, drinking water, medicines, and emergency supplies because outside help may not arrive for days.

Japan is not warning that a disaster is about to happen, but the scale of what officials are preparing for is serious.

If a massive earthquake hits Tokyo or other major cities, millions could need emergency help at the same time, while damaged roads and communication networks make rescue operations much harder.

The biggest danger is that emergency services could be unable to reach everyone in time, leaving families trapped in damaged buildings or without clean water, food, and medical care for days.

I've spent years investing in crypto, and one thing I've learned is that market attention and technological value are two very different things.

What excites me about @TapeOutWorld isn't a price prediction.

It's watching developers turn virtual transistors into programmable circuits, build DeWEB applications, propose new standards, and explore entirely new possibilities for on-chain computation.

Not every experiment will succeed. That's perfectly fine. That's how real innovation happens.

We saw something similar in the early days of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and DeFi. Builders experimented long before the broader market understood what they were creating.

A healthy ecosystem shouldn't need a green candle to attract builders. It should attract builders who give the world a reason to pay attention.

Price can create attention. But only real utility, adoption, and sustained innovation can build something lasting.

Less hype. More experiments.
Less promises. More proof.

Keep building. 🟦

#TapeOut #ProofOfBuild #BuilderCulture

The whole thing felt like an absolute LARP, but the token was sending. Within days, it was pushing $100M+ and suddenly everyone became an expert on AI agents.

"OMG, AGENTS ARE THE FUTURE!"

Every token remotely associated with that narrative started pumping.

Nobody cared whether the product actually worked. Nobody questioned the technology. Nobody asked whether it was sustainable.

The chart was green, so the technology was revolutionary.

Now look at tapeout.

Potentially fascinating technology, interesting possibilities, but because the associated tokens aren't printing money, the entire narrative barely gets any attention.

We don't use technology to determine which tokens deserve to pump. We use pumping tokens to determine which technology deserves our attention.

A $100M market cap can make absolute bullshit look like the future.

And a flat chart can make genuinely interesting innovation look irrelevant.

We've reached a point where price action has replaced curiosity, research, and critical thinking.

We don't discover narratives anymore.

We wait for a green candle to tell us what to believe in.

That's how fking backwards this market has become.

如果要出金 100u，通过币安 OTC 商家只能卖出约 ￥663，但在 Peer，你可以绕开中间商和中介，P2P （点对点交易）直接找到买家并完成交易，只要买家觉得价格合适，订单就能成交，小编近日在 Peer 成功以 ￥702 成交售出了 100u。

实操 Peer 挂单出金 100u 到支付宝
详细过程如下：

在开始之前，请安装 Peer 官方浏览器拓展程序 PeerAuth，首次挂单按提示验证支付宝账户：
https://t.co/9BxACFs0Dy

1. 打开 https://t.co/RQ74AYN366 选择需要挂单的金额，挂单最终使用的是 Base 链上的 USDC，若您的资产为其他形式，则需要点击充值，Peer 会将资产跨链至 Base 并兑换为 USDC，转换成功后网页会显示可以出售的 USDC 余额。

2. 填写支付宝绑定的邮箱地址，并按页面提示补充支付宝实名对应的第一个字，也可以上传支付宝收款二维码。若支付宝尚未绑定邮箱，需要先完成绑定。账户验证通过后，页面会显示“√已就绪”。

3. 选择售出 USDC 的汇率，Floor 是你能接受的最低售出汇率。例如设为 ￥6.90/USDC，就表示不接受低于这个价格的订单。
本次实操选择了市场参考价上浮 5%，显示约 ￥7.02/USDC，最终在挂单一日后售出 100 USDC，收到 ￥702。大家可以根据自己的需求设置价差。

4.点击「确认挂单」前需要核对数量、支付宝收款信息、报价和单笔购买限额。看到图三的挂单详情，挂单就已上线，开始等待买家接单。点击「管理」可以查看你的挂单：https://t.co/pdisSNEO5w

5. 等待挂单售出，若支付宝账户收到买家打款，在 TEE 请求订单号并核对转账金额后，USDC 将会自动以挂单价成功售出。
（订单详情中的「策略」仅为自动调整卖币报价，只有订单成交、卖价高于当时市场参考价时，才会产生并计算价差收益，并不会自动生息）

卖出过程不需要卖家确认交易，Peer 会验证付款金额和账户并自动放币给买家，正常流程中，付款验证通过后会自动放币，无需卖家手动确认，P2P 直接完成交换，干净优雅。

text:
Today we are releasing Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum version of Cadence, our consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers. Quantum Cadence uses no quorum certificates, and its safety and liveness do not depend on signatures.

Most modern consensus protocols, Cadence included, rely heavily on signatures and quorum certificates, which a large-scale quantum computer could forge. Simply replacing today's signatures with post-quantum ones would make certificates too large for every validator to send around in a high-performance blockchain. Quantum Cadence instead draws on Forget-IT, a recent signature-free consensus protocol co-developed by researchers at Category Labs.

Quantum Cadence still keeps the overall architecture and core guarantees of Cadence, so our Cadence prototype was easy to carry over: an AI was able to adapt it to Quantum Cadence in a few hours, and an early prototype now runs on an internal test network.

We designed Quantum Cadence to be practical for a high-performance blockchain. In our simulations, its latency is similar to Cadence's, and it scales better with the number of proposers.

Interactive explainer: https://t.co/tKVbnkhkBY.

Full paper: https://t.co/6xdk5Y3ime.

Antes de criar mais um agente de IA, pergunta: que problema ele resolve?

O Addy Osmani postou isso hoje e linkou um guia sobre quando juntar subagentes no agente principal.

A ideia dele é simples: muitas vezes o problema não é falta de agente, é um prompt gigante e bagunçado. Dá pra resolver com "skills" (instruções que o agente carrega só quando precisa) sem dividir o contexto em vários agentes.

A regra dele pra manter um subagente separado: o trabalho é paralelo, precisa de contexto limpo, ou um agente sozinho não consegue escolher as ferramentas certas. Fora disso, junta no principal, transforma o prompt em skill, roda testes e fica com o que funcionar melhor.

Eu rodo 30 agentes no Grok Bot, mas já estou olhando como organizar eles melhores.

To aprendendo pra caramba esses dias.

Atenção: o conselho dele fala de subagentes dentro de um mesmo agente. Os meus são agentes separados, cada um com uma função. A lógica serve pros dois: cada agente novo tem que ter um motivo.

O que fazer hoje: lista seus agentes, escreve em uma frase o que cada um faz e pausa o que você não consegue explicar.

ENSv2 was activated today and I'm proud to be part of the biggest upgrade of @ensdomains in its history! It's not only the smart contracts that have been redesigned and rewritten to lay the foundation of the open naming layer for the internet: a flexible permissions system, an extensible and configurable tree structure and more. There are also two new apps, the manager and explorer, which will give the two distinct user groups, normies and power users, the interface they need.

On top of that, and here is my personal contribution, we made sure that wallets and apps which integrate with ENS not only become ready for ENSv2 but also deepen their integration: Use the Universal Resolver, support DNS-imported names, do offchain resolution and many more technical integration details. The ENS integrations ecosystem got an upgrade too 💥.

Shout out to the world-class devrel team: Greg (@gregskril), Kevin (@workem0n) and Yash Goyal (@yash_goyal_dev) who made sure that every major web3 library, all important wallets and most apps are ENSv2 ready with tailored support and extensive pull requests, concise and complete documentation, automated test suites and a CLI that agents and humans love, all while traveling the world enabling hackers at @ethglobal and other hackathons.

I'm also grateful to be working under the leadership of Nick Johnson (@nicksdjohnson), Jeff Lau (@Jefflau), Katherine Wu (@katherinewu) and Dom (@domicoeth) who had to take some tough and controversial decisions like ditching NameChain or postponing the launch until we were 100% sure it was ready. Nothing worse than a rushed launch.

If you are an app developer and you are not sure if your app is ENSv2 ready, don't fret: ENSv2 names will continue to be resolvable through the documented V1 resolution paths. And being fully ENSv2 compatible is, 90% of the time, simply updating to the latest version of your favorite web3 library. If your app has writing capabilities like registering a name, setting a text record or managing subnames, more work is needed. Head over to the ENSv2 documentation to find out more or reach out. We're happy to assist.

Payward, the parent company of Kraken, announced its intention to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3* markets. Payward will use Hyperliquid as the infrastructure layer to deploy perpetual futures markets for US clients. Subject to regulatory approval, Bitnomial, Payward’s CFTC-regulated DCM and DCO, would act as the HIP-3* deployer: creating, owning, and administering the markets and clearing and settling the contracts. If approved, NinjaTrader Clearing, Payward’s CFTC-registered FCM, would carry client accounts.

HIP-3 will support optional deployer configuration for permissioned markets in a future network upgrade. This set of additional deployer functionality is collectively called HIP-3*. At its core, HIP-3* activation involves an onchain allowlist managed by the deployer or its sub-deployers. The functionality is strictly additive to HIP-3; its use is optional and up to the deployer. Existing markets remain unchanged. The initial release is available on testnet, where specifications are preliminary and subject to change based on feedback.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. As with HIP-3, HIP-3* deployers are independent operators who use Hyperliquid as the onchain infrastructure layer for their own markets, while retaining control and responsibility over their deployment.

text:
Let’s address the elephant in the room with $NET

I’ve seen a lot of hate towards this token recently, yes it’s normal, it went from an ATH of $1,887 to $158.

(90% down in less than two months lol)

But maybe this actually has an explanation

At its peak, people were paying 15x the underlying value of the assets backing each token.

Today it looks different

$NET price: $158.79
NAV per token: $162.92
Treasury: $24.94M
Total supply: 153,092 NET
Staked supply: 87.7%
Price/NAV: 0.97x

For the first time, $NET is trading below its NAV.

And that’s a completely different situation from buying it at $900 when the NAV was $130.

The treasury didn’t disappear.

In fact, it grew from around $9M in early September to $25M today.

What disappeared was the premium people were willing to pay.

Now here’s the part I don’t like.

Staking rewards are currently 0% because the protocol stops issuing new tokens when the price falls to NAV or below.

That’s good for stopping dilution, but it also removes one of the main incentives people had to hold $NET

Trading volume has also collapsed from $15M a day at its peak to $500K or less.

And with 5% trading fees on certain pools, liquidity is a real problem.

So no, having $25M in treasury doesn’t automatically mean the token is going to recover.

(It looks really bad tho)

There’s also the question of whether the protocol can generate enough external revenue to grow its NAV without relying on new bonds and token issuance.

I still think the idea behind $NET is interesting, especially if Robinhood Chain becomes a serious ecosystem for tokenized equities.

But I also understand why people who bought at 5-15x NAV are pissed.

They were buying a premium that eventually disappeared.

The difference now is that you’re no longer paying $900 for $130 of backing.

You’re paying around $159 for $163 of reported NAV.

But hey calling it a zero just because the chart looks terrible ignores what the protocol actually holds.

We will see.

imo if your coin needs an “incentive” to hold it besides the narrative itself, then it was never a good coin in the first place

even with "HOLDER" rewards, we've still seen coins go -90% over the last month because their narratives dried up and people realized the coins were not as good as they originally thought

now people are trying to find reasons for the market to FORCE coins back up (incentives, new launchpads, etc). the truth is that this is like being rejected by a girl because she thinks you're ugly then trying to find another way to pull her

its over, you gotta move on

liquidity + novelty are the only things that will ever make people hold. we just saw multiple coins go 9-10 fig market cap because btc reversed + people were psyopping themselves with RWA pairings being the next big thing

(RWAs as a whole have a bright future, but i still dont find pairing a memecoin to a stock super compelling. i said this at ATHs too: it just feels like memecoins last cycle but with one small change rather than something actually new)

this is why its never the launchpads fault when coins go down, regardless of it being pumpfun, stonk, pons, or long

yes, they should continue to innovate and foster a good environment for all types of trading/holding, but at the end of the day it's up to the coins launching there to be interesting enough to raise ceilings

so the real issue at hand is that we need something "new" rather than just switching to another launchpad with hooks or higher starting market caps or block 0 taxes

if it was this simple, we would've already switched by now

i know it's easy to just say we "need something new," but the issue is you can't really predict what it'll be unless you build it yourself

thematically im sure you could, like RWAs, AI, or whatever. but no one could've specifically predicted the bonding curve 3 years ago just like no one predicted RWA pairings 4 months ago. you just had to be on the lookout for something new and take full advantage of it when it arrived

the reason most charts since september look depressing is because the market was euphoric then and overvaluing narratives

now these coins are just being fairly repriced to down the downside (you can see this longer term with charts from AI meta in 2024)

so yeah, i dont really understand what people like @jackduval mean when they say they want someone to replace pumpfun

you will be met with the same issues today, since if pumpfun dies then all launchpads in their current forms will also die because none of the alternatives are doing something actually interesting that would "save the trenches"

今天翻到野村的一个研报，里面有个判断我挺认同的。他们说，科技巨头之间的AI军备竞赛，继续下去的概率高达75%。

我觉得这事儿底层逻辑其实很简单，现在就是一场谁都不敢先眨眼的博弈。谷歌、微软、亚马逊这些巨头心里门儿清，谁要是先踩了刹车、削减了算力投资，谁就可能在下一代的AI竞赛里彻底掉队。所以哪怕现在自由现金流承压，甚至报表难看，只要华尔街还愿意给钱，他们就会通过发债等各种方式，咬着牙继续往里砸。

顺着这个逻辑看，2027年的存储行情确实稳了不少。因为这些巨头早就把未来几年的HBM、服务器内存和企业级固态硬盘的产能，通过长期合同给锁死了。这种长约的违约成本极高，基本上就把未来几年的供给给焊死了。

咱们之前总聊缺电、缺冷却，觉得这些物理瓶颈会拖垮AI基建。但野村这个观点提醒了我，缺电顶多也就是让项目交付晚几天，真正的生死拐点，其实在融资端。只要巨头们还能在资本市场上顺顺利利借到钱，存储短缺和涨价的逻辑就不会变。

但反过来说，这也恰恰是悬在所有AI公司头顶上最危险的一把剑。一旦哪天融资链条真的断裂了，也就是大家发现借不到钱了，那这波由资本强行催熟的狂热，才算是真正走到了尽头。现在就只看这场击鼓传花的游戏，还能在华尔街的纵容下玩多久了。

text:
This is an incredible moment in this history of mathematics, computer science, physics & science with some of the hardest problems in human history being solved by AI over a period of weeks. Depending on your perspective, it's either a crisis, a triumph, or both. I don't think anyone knows for sure. We're all trying to make sense of it. I oscillate between fear/dread and optimism/excitement on a daily basis. The rate of progress is insane, including today's announcement from OpenAI of more problems solved.

To help make sense of all of it, here's my conversation with three mathematicians about this moment. Each of them is an expert in the field of each of the biggest problems solved: Navier-Stokes, quasi-Riemann hypothesis, the unique games conjecture and complexity theory more generally.

Ankur Moitra is a mathematician and theoretical computer scientist at MIT, visiting the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton. Steven Brunton (@eigensteve) is a mathematician and fluid dynamics expert at UW. Alex Kontorovich (@AlexKontorovich) is a mathematician at Rutgers specializing in number theory.

text:
Gameto my sixth unicorn was just sold to Ferring for $1.38bn here  is the story.

In 2020 I endowed a fellowship at Harvard in my father's name, Carlos M. Varsavsky, in the lab of George Church, one of the world's leading geneticists. Its goal: to make human eggs in the lab. Gameto grew out of it.
My father was an astrophysicist and built the Instituto Argentino de Radioastronomía, Argentina's radio astronomy institute. He was a great teacher, at the university and at home. In a time without artificial intelligence, he was the artificial intelligence for me: he knew about everything. He died young. The fellowship carries his name. The fellowship paid for the PhD of Christian Kramme, a Californian geneticist who worked out how to make in the lab the cells that surround an egg in the ovary and help it mature. He is now Gameto's chief scientific officer.

Ferring Pharmaceuticals, the Swiss fertility drug maker, is acquiring Gameto for up to $1.3825 billion. I am a co-founder, and this is the story of a company that set out to do one thing and was bought for another.
I came to fertility in 2016 with Prelude Fertility, a network of US clinics I built, now part of Inception, the largest fertility network in North America. Inside those clinics I learned that IVF works, but it is brutal. For two weeks a woman injects herself with hormones so her ovaries release many eggs at once: around 28 shots, ultrasounds, blood tests, bloating and mood swings.

Many women go through it once and never again. Every one who stops is a pregnancy that never happens. One question obsessed me: what if the treatment took three days instead of two weeks.

I brought in Dina Radenkovic Turner as co-founder and CEO. She was 26, a physician trained at University College London and one of the brightest people I have ever worked with. Many questioned the bet on someone that young. Time proved us right. I had a moonshot and a fellowship. Dina turned them into a company. She looked at Christian's cells and saw a product: if the egg was out of reach, we would do the ovary's work in the lab. That became Fertilo.
With Fertilo a woman takes hormones for two or three days, about 80% fewer shots. Her eggs are collected immature and spend a day in the lab with those cells, which do the ovary's job. Then they are fertilized as in any IVF cycle. The cells never enter her body.
On December 16, 2024, the first baby conceived this way was born in Lima. By August there were five babies and more than twenty pregnancies. Three gentle cycles beat one brutal cycle nobody wants to repeat.

With Dina at the helm, Gameto raised about $127 million in total from Overwater Ventures, Insight Partners, RA Capital, Two Sigma Ventures, BOLD Capital Partners, Future Ventures, Olivia Walton's Ingeborg Investments, Arcadia Investment Partners, PAGS Group, Pontiva Healthcare Partners and Portfolia, and from Anne Wojcicki of 23andMe, Bob Nelsen of ARCH Venture Partners, Stacey Bendet Eisner of Alice + Olivia and Chelsea Hirschhorn of Frida.
Gameto is the sixth company I have built to pass a billion dollars, after Viatel, Yacom, Jazztel, Eolia Renovables, sold in 2017, and Inception/Prelude  Fertility, Telecoms, internet, clean energy, clinics, biotech: nothing in common, and in every one the team mattered more than me.

text:
Agent Evaluation 是我觉得为数不多还需要人力去做判断、将来很难被AI 彻底取代的职业方向。我给大家找了一个非常好的学习资料入门：Hugging Face 的公开 Training Agent 课程

学完了，你应该会有更强的 sense，判断 AI 时代下哪些工作更适合人来做

这个资料是公开的，视频都在 Hugging Face 的 YouTube 频道，代码全部开源，下面有这六节：
1、Agentic Evaluations Workshop：怎么评价一个 Agent。
这一章节去看：为什么 benchmark 分数和真实使用体验对不上？目前 Agent Eval 做到了哪一步，还有哪些问题没解决。先把“怎样才算一个好 Agent”，等等都有 cover

2、RL for Agents Workshop：给 Agent 做强化学习，难在哪
这一章节去关注：从 LLM 的 RL 走到 Agent 的 RL，会多出哪些难点？环境怎么搭、rollout 怎么跑、reward 怎么设计，以及训练过程中推理为什么会成为 bottleneck

3、SFT on agent traces：用 Agent 的执行轨迹做微调
这一章节去关注：拿公开的 coding-agent traces（执行轨迹）整理成训练数据，用 TRL + LoRA 做 SFT，在 Hugging Face Jobs 上跑，用 Trackio 看指标。基本带着走了一遍小型的微调流程

4、Distillation：把大模型的能力蒸馏给小 Agent
这一章节去关注：怎么把 teacher model 的能力转移给更小的 coding agent。off-policy、on-policy、self-distillation 都会讲，看看这几种蒸馏方式分别怎么做

5、Reinforcement Learning：SFT 之后，怎么继续用 RL 训练
这一章节去关注：用 GRPO 接着训练，讲 group sampling、可验证的 reward，以及 reward、KL、输出长度这些曲线怎么看。看 Agent 怎么 reward hacking

6、From reward functions to environments：让 Agent 在真实环境里学习
这一章节去动手：从 reset()/step() 接口讲起，用 OpenEnv 搭环境、上传到 Hub，再接入 TRL 的 GRPOTrainer。最后通过 Harbor 和 Hugging Face sandboxes，用 AsyncGRPOTrainer 训练真正的 coding agent：OpenCode。让 Agent 在环境里采取动作、拿到反馈，再继续训练

text:
it was brought to my attention that a token launched on standard's launchpad was removed from pumpfun's competition for "bundling" because 80% of its supply sits in one place

i want to clarify what this actually is, and why its the complete opposite of a bundle and actually a beneficial mechanism

first, what a bundle is: a deployer buys most of the supply across multiple wallets at launch, hides that theyre connected, waits for buyers, then dumps on them (or in the *optimistic* case, uses them for "supply control"). bundles are opaque and hide a token's real float

standard's launchpad lets deployers do what's called a "charter drop" which is the complete opposite of a bundle:

- charters are nfts held by participants in the @standard_rsv ecosystem. each holder has spent over 3 eth to join the protocol, and they've proven to be aligned, long term supporters of the projects they like

- deployers can choose to airdrop a percentage of supply (up to 80%) to charter holders. these tokens are locked in a vault contract, and charter holders cant access them unless they BURN their charter

- the airdrop isnt controlled by the deployer. the tokens sit in a single public contract, 0xb8748E02f07dd80F1DB99A49F92546B2210D844d, with no admin key and no owner withdrawal

- nothing is hidden. anyone can verify the mechanism and lock onchain, which is the opposite of a hidden bundle

- charter drops cant be dumped instantly. the tokens are split across every charter holder, not one wallet, and holders only receive their share by burning their charter. it's a public token lock with a real cost to unlock, not free supply ready to hit the market

were glad bundled tokens are being policed, but if this counts as a bundle, we'd urge you to look at the majority of the other tokens in this competition

as a side not, over 4M USD of tokens has been airdropped to charters and we've seen less than 5 charter burn to receive the airdropped tokens

since we're on the topic anyway, let's talk about market cap versus liquidity on charter drop tokens. dashboards count the locked 80% in market cap, so the market cap to liquidity ratio looks thin

but, measured against tradable supply, the pool is deeper than on other launchpad tokens since the same amount of liquidity supports a much smaller float, because most of the supply is locked. treating locked supply as tradable gives a misleading ratio

text:
《代码整洁之道》的作者 Uncle Bob 发布了 ub-mode，一份用于 AI 编程的技能文件，共 152 行。

它规定了修改代码的基本顺序：先整理数据结构，写出失败的测试，再修改代码。完成后检查复杂度、重复代码和测试是否有效。

项目配套推荐了三个检查工具：

• Crapper：计算函数复杂度、覆盖率和 CRAP 分数。
• Dryer：查找结构相似的代码。
• Mutator：修改代码中的运算符或常量，检查测试能否发现变化。

另外还有一个 UML Viewer，用来查看代码结构和质量指标。

这些规则可以作为验收清单。但复制技能文件不会自动拦截不合格的代码，工具安装、参数和检查流程仍需配置。

text:
I gave an AI agent $11 and under an hour to use @MonidHQ, the pay-per-call tool store for AI agents.

It spent 5.3 cents. Here's what each call cost me and what broke.

Disclosure: The $11 was free credit on my new account ($1 signup + $10 bonus). Your start may differ. I paid nothing and bought nothing.

What I tested
Real calls through a limited key (runs + wallet read, 3-day expiry), with a $3/day cap and a $0.30 per-call cap switched on.

1. Easy: read a web page as clean text. 3.7 seconds and $0.00015.
2. Typical: a company profile for https://t.co/2AeQL4Xy8J. 2.7 seconds and $0.0049.
3. Hard: ask Gemini how it describes a brand, with web search. 6.6 seconds and $0.0363. The listed price was $0.0006.

Also ran: a free web search (8 results, $0), an Instagram profile (async, 5.6 seconds, $0.001) and an Exa search (5.3 seconds, $0.007).

What it does well
→ Billing is honest. My balance went from $11.00 to $10.946646. Monid's own run records add up to the same $0.053354, to the last digit.
→ Failed calls cost $0. I hit 8 runs that failed, came back empty or were stopped. Total charged: $0.
→ The budget cap works. It blocked a $0.40 job before any money moved (0.2 seconds on Monid's own clock) and told me why.
→ Search is fast. One plain sentence returned 5 ranked tools with prices in about a second.
→ The same job can differ 100x in price. Reading a page ranged from $0.00015 to $0.015 across the top results. Your agent can pick.
→ Keys can be limited, and a permission error names the exact missing scope.
→ The most-called tool on its rankings, TinyFish web search, is free.

What it does badly
→ The wallet balance check failed about 1 time in 4 (11 of 47 reads). The errors I could see were HTTP 500.
→ A listed price is not always the price charged. Gemini: listed $0.0006, billed $0.0363, because token costs are added on top.
→ Amazon reviews, the data behind its "Analyze customer sentiment" starter prompt, returned nothing. Two review tools gave me 3 rejected requests and 2 empty results. Cost $0, but no reviews. (I tested the tools, not the prompt itself.)
→ A failed run can still say COMPLETED, and a blocked run returns HTTP 200. Your agent has to check more than the status.
→ The homepage says "no sign-up needed". The docs say create an account and an API key, then "send the key to your agent". That means pasting a secret into chat.
→ App pages sat on "Setting up your workspace" for around 10 seconds.
→ I can't confirm "zero markup". It matched on one tool (DataForSEO, $0.00015) and is unclear on Exa ($0.007). The site's own hidden text says "Some include one."

What $1 buys, at the prices I measured
→ About 6,600 page reads at $0.00015
→ About 1,000 Instagram profile lookups at $0.001
→ About 204 company profiles at $0.0049
→ About 142 Exa searches at $0.007
→ About 27 Gemini answers at $0.0363
Some tools charge per result, so check the price on the tool's page first.

Scores (my judgment)
→ First impression 7
→ Ease of first run 5
→ Billing honesty 9
→ Guardrails 9
→ Speed 8
→ Reliability 5
→ Honesty of claims 6

Verdict: 7.0/10
Honest billing and real spending limits. Held back by a flaky balance check, a price that can hide token costs, and Amazon reviews that returned nothing.

→ Use it if you build or run AI agents and want pay-per-call access to search, scraping and lead data, with caps you set.
→ Skip it if you need Amazon reviews to work today, need guaranteed uptime, or would paste keys into a chat.

What I'd fix first
→ Retry the balance check, or say clearly when it's down.
→ Show "from $X + token cost" on variable-priced tools.
→ Mark a run FAILED or EMPTY when nothing was delivered, not COMPLETED.
→ Fix the "no sign-up needed" line, or make it true.
→ Add a "provider price vs Monid price" column.
→ Bring the cost column into view on the Usage page.
→ Make every suggested command https.

Before your agent runs anything, turn on the $0.30 per-call cap. Mine was off by default. Bookmark this so you know what each call costs before you let an agent spend.

text:
BENCHMARKED: LFM3-1.7B by @liquidai.

Liquid AI published 1.6 GB for the KV cache at 128K context. I ran it on my Mac mini and measured 1.6 GB.

The whole model at 128K uses 3.15 GB of GPU memory, under 5% of the 64GB. It still generates 80 tok/s.

Only 6 of its 24 layers keep a full KV cache. The other 18 use short convolutions or sliding-window attention.

llama.cpp (Metal), Q4_K_M, M5 Pro 64GB, median of 3 runs

- 512 ctx: 184 tok/s, 0.09s to first token
- 4K ctx: 178 tok/s, 0.72s to first token
- 32K ctx: 141 tok/s
- 128K ctx: 80 tok/s

Q8_0 does 125 tok/s at 512, so 4-bit is 47% faster.

text:
imo if your coin needs an “incentive” to hold it besides the narrative itself, then it was never a good coin in the first place

even with "HOLDER" rewards, we've still seen coins go -90% over the last month because their narratives dried up and people realized the coins were not as good as they originally thought

now people are trying to find reasons for the market to FORCE coins back up (incentives, new launchpads, etc). the truth is that this is like being rejected by a girl because she thinks you're ugly then trying to find another way to pull her

its over, you gotta move on

liquidity + novelty are the only things that will ever make people hold. we just saw multiple coins go 9-10 fig market cap because btc reversed + people were psyopping themselves with RWA pairings being the next big thing

(RWAs as a whole have a bright future, but i still dont find pairing a memecoin to a stock super compelling. i said this at ATHs too: it just feels like memecoins last cycle but with one small change rather than something actually new)

this is why its never the launchpads fault when coins go down, regardless of it being pumpfun, stonk, pons, or long

yes, they should continue to innovate and foster a good environment for all types of trading/holding, but at the end of the day it's up to the coins launching there to be interesting enough to raise ceilings

so the real issue at hand is that we need something "new" rather than just switching to another launchpad with hooks or higher starting market caps or block 0 taxes

if it was this simple, we would've already switched by now

i know it's easy to just say we "need something new," but the issue is you can't really predict what it'll be unless you build it yourself

thematically im sure you could, like RWAs, AI, or whatever. but no one could've specifically predicted the bonding curve 3 years ago just like no one predicted RWA pairings 4 months ago. you just had to be on the lookout for something new and take full advantage of it when it arrived

the reason most charts since september look depressing is because the market was euphoric then and overvaluing narratives

now these coins are just being fairly repriced to down the downside (you can see this longer term with charts from AI meta in 2024)

so yeah, i dont really understand what people like @jackduval mean when they say they want someone to replace pumpfun

you will be met with the same issues today, since if pumpfun dies then all launchpads in their current forms will also die because none of the alternatives are doing something actually interesting that would "save the trenches"

text:
Anthropic 的 IPO 招股书终于公开了，计划在纳斯达克上市，代码 ANT。

随着 Opus 5.5 登上神座，Anthropic 也终于正式向证监会提交招股书了。据《华尔街日报》此前报道，Anthropic 此次 IPO 可能募资 1000 亿美元或以上，对应估值约 1.5 万亿—2 万亿美元，可谓是史上最大 IPO。

小编扒了一下招股书，挑了 7 个要点，涉及客户使用情况、公司的收入和支出，以及上市后的治理安排，整理如下：

① 老客户的消费增长很快

截至 9 月底，Anthropic 的净收入留存率约为 900%。

也就是说去年同一季度的客户，今年合计贡献的季度收入变成了原来的 9 倍。这个数字不包含新客户，也排除了 Claude Pro 和 Max 订阅用户。

除了新增客户，已有客户不断扩大使用量，也是收入增长的重要来源。

② 三季度超过八成收入，来自近半年发布的模型

今年三季度，超过 80% 的收入来自过去 6 个月内发布的模型版本。

这个比例能看出模型迭代对业务的影响：新版本推出后，很快就成为收入的主要来源。公司需要持续投入研发，才能跟上这样的更新速度。

③ 上半年 807 亿美元净亏损，大部分是非现金损失

其中约 724 亿美元，来自可转换票据等金融工具的公允价值变动。

部分投资者持有可以按约定条件换成股票的票据。Anthropic 估值上涨后，这些票据对应的权利更值钱，公司需要在会计上确认相应损失。

④ 多份算力合同，都有最低付款承诺

Anthropic 与谷歌、亚马逊和微软签下的部分算力协议，约定了不论实际使用量如何，都需要履行的最低支出。

其中，与亚马逊的一份协议覆盖 2026 年至 2036 年，最低支出达到 1100 亿美元。

这些合同让公司提前获得未来的算力供应，也带来了长期付款义务。

⑤ 约 5%—7% 的收入，来自后来被识别为违规的客户

这是公司对今年前 9 个月收入的估计，涉及违反使用政策或商业条款的客户。

因为识别和调查需要时间，在限制或终止这些客户的访问之前，公司已经提供服务，并确认了相应收入。

Anthropic 表示，8 月和 9 月加强识别与封禁后，这部分收入占比预计下降，也可能影响后续收入增速。

⑥ 上市后，创始团队仍保留特殊投票权

亚马逊、谷歌等投资者持有的 N 类股没有投票权。7 位联合创始人则通过一家 LLC 持有特殊的 F 类股，保留普通股东表决事项 50.1% 的投票权。

另外，长期利益信托拥有董事会多数席位的任免权。

所以，判断这家公司的控制权，需要同时看股份类别、创始团队的表决权，以及信托的董事任命安排。

⑦ 公益基金已经获得约 5% 的股份

Anthropic 已将约占全面摊薄股本 5% 的股份划入公益基金。

公司还通过了一项后续安排：以 IPO 发行价为起点，股价每达到上涨 50% 的新里程碑，董事会可以酌情再安排最多 2% 的股份，用于该基金等指定对象。

text:
我终于明白为什么科技巨头都在不惜代价地向物理现实靠拢了！🤯

Google DeepMind 刚刚正式发布世界模型 Genie 4，
支持实时文字改动场景、自带原生环境音与互动对话，Gemini 3.8 Flash 担任后台导演。
机器模拟真实物理世界的门槛，今天被彻底踩碎了，模拟假说被证实了！

抛开博主玩梗的情绪泡沫，如果我们把这套技术拆开看，就会发现 Google 这次根本不是在卷普通的视频生成：
它不是在生成一段冷冰冰的 MP4，而是在用纯算力，实时凭空跑出一整个可以走动、可以交互的物理世界。

以前的 Sora 或各种视频大模型，本质上是一台高精度的梦境录像机。

它提前把像素算好、渲染出来喂给你看；你按暂停它就停，你喊它改个天气，它必须把整个视频推翻重算一遍。
而 Genie 4 彻底切断了“预渲染”的旧逻辑：
你不是观众，你是里面的玩家；你在场景里往前走，画面随着你的脚步实时推演空气动力学和物理碰撞，你在旁边敲一行字，暴雨和新角色立刻动态加载进同一个空间里。
更狠的是原生音视频的融合。
过去的世界模型全是一帮在真空中运转的无声哑剧，而这次 Genie 4 第一次让世界模型原生吐出了环境音、背景音乐，以及随着玩家操作实时动态响应的角色对话。
旁边还配了 Gemini 3.8 Flash 当“实时导演”，在后台毫秒级拆解因果逻辑、校准画面连贯性，硬生生把时间维持在了两分钟的连续稳定模拟。
但如果你以为 Google 费尽心力搞这个只是为了给游戏公司做外挂，那就太小看 DeepMind 的野心了。
造一个逼真的虚拟世界，从来不是终点，而是给下一代 AGI 准备的无尽练兵场。
现实世界的数据太贵、太慢、试错成本太高，特斯拉要跑几十亿公里才能训好一辆自动驾驶，机器人摔断一根机械臂就是几十万成本。
而当 Google 能够以极低成本实时生成符合牛顿力学的交互世界，数以亿计的具身智能体就可以在里面 24 小时以万倍速狂奔、碰撞、学习。
当然照例保持一份冷静：
目前单次模拟极限依然在两分钟左右，时间一长细节依然会漂移，而且这只是少数测试者能摸到的研究预览。
但这代表了一个极其危险的代际分水岭：
从今天起，AI 的竞争正式从“模仿人类的文字与画面”，彻底跃迁到了“模拟宇宙的物理法则”。

text:
我用 CastMind 收听并转录了 Matt Palmer（@mattyp）和 Eric （@ericzakariasson） 这场 Grok Bot Q&A Space。

下面是我整理的 15个Q&A（附视频解说）：
1. 「问」最近上了哪些 Apple 相关能力？Vault 是干什么的？
「答」刚上了一批 Apple 服务连接器，包括日历、提醒、闹钟、定位等。Vault 可以存地址、电话这类敏感信息。Grok Bot 并不知道 Vault 里具体写了什么，却能在填表时把值填进去，做法接近密码管理器。Eric 说自己之前主要用 One Password，后来也被提示把地址存进 Vault。后续还会接更多凭据提供方，少来回切换。

2. 「问」X Money 怎么用？
「答」两人刚开始玩。有人用 bot 每天从菜单随机点外卖，Eric 说那不是他的性格，他吃固定的。更值得看的是一次性虚拟卡。X Money 可以生成一次性卡号下单，不用把实体卡信息交给商家。

3.「问」Pages 能做什么？
「答」Eric 用得很多。周五跑「这周干了啥」bot，结果写进 Page，周与周能对照。他做过带关卡的 Doom 克隆，也做过 Pages 自己的营销站和一堆仪表盘。Matt 把健身营养数据挪进 Grok Bot，让它看两个月训练量，按肌群出热力图；也拉过自己的 X 账号，看发帖时段和热帖。底层接近旧版 Cursor Canvas，是 React 加内部组件 SDK，模型编排组件，而不是随便吐原始 HTML，版式更稳。

4. 「问」Team Bots 和多人协作到哪了？
「答」问到个人账号何时能用 Team Bots，回复是 stay tuned。整队很关心 multiplayer。Team Bots 适合把「别人老来找我办的事」做成团队内部工具。Matt 说，以前每张表格都能变成 app，现在每个 app 都能变成 bot；聊天像实习生，最终形态就是说话。

5. 「问」Bot 之间能互聊吗？
「答」能，但目前多是人在管。有人的 bot 把 bug 报告用 X DM 发给 Matt，他再转给自己的 bot 做调研，再找对人回过去。Eric 给 Lauren 的 bot 发过带免责声明的长文，对方 bot 立刻回了一堵墙。Slack 侧也有实践，工程反馈进频道，Cloud Agent 接着改 harness。

6. 「问」Grok Bot 和 Cursor Projects 怎么接？
「答」装 Cursor 插件之后，Grok Bot 可以跟正在跑的 Cursor agent 对话。Matt 常用法是让 bot 去 Slack 捞上下文，再把结果发给某个 Project。不太显眼的一点是，Project 也能回消息给 bot，目前一般要从 bot 这边先起对话。

7. 「问」用什么模型？有 Teams 吗？
「答」混用，会挑当下最合适的。Teams 集成已经有了，Team Bots 可以装进 Teams，Grok Bot 本身也通。

8. 「问」见过最有意思的用法是什么？
「答」Matt 说本地咖啡馆老板在用。也有家长让 bot 读学校邮件，同步自己和配偶的日历，免得漏事。有人拿它盯订位取消，发现更好的时段就通知，有时还要人接手走完流程，但省掉了自己写脚本。Action Button 可以重映射成打开 Grok Bot 语音通话，当临时 Siri 替代；Matt 前一天发过怎么设。

9. 「问」怎么判断能力边界？什么该自动做？
「答」几乎都是靠多问摸出来的。Matt 入职 SpaceXAI（当时还是 Cursor）时定过目标，尽量不给经理发消息，问题先丢给 Grok Bot。接上 Notion、Slack、邮件之后，公司里大量「流程是什么、该问谁」都能先问一遍。信任是用出来的，一开始盯着审批，用久了才知道哪些可以放自动。

10. 「问」有没有可复用的实践？
「答」把常用工具接上，让 bot 有机会主动找你。Eric 有个叫 Scout 的 bot，每天早上看 Notion、旁路频道和项目，整理「过去 24 小时你可能没注意到、但该知道」的简报。也可以让 bot 翻自己的历史 prompt，看哪些该收成 routine 或独立 bot，少重复口述。Lauren 常提的一句是反复问「这件事该不该我自己做」；该编码就写进 skill，再给 agent 需要的权限。

11. 「问」记忆怎么管？
「答」底层会记。可以主动让它增改记忆。分三层，每个 bot 自己的 memory、跨 bot 的 user memory，以及你写进 skill 的、偏人工编码的那一层。

12. 「问」能不能看 bot 组织图？
「答」内测时有过层级视图，上线时没带出来。现在可以直接让 bot 用 Pages 画「我的 Grok Bot 怎么互相通信」。

13. 「问」最近还上了什么？
「答」Vault；更顺的 One Password 集成；bot 自有邮箱可按原格式转发邮件；Slack 里会记下是谁让它发的，线程里能追问；还可以从描述或一张图生成视频。Changelog 在 https://t.co/hNyP1eNiAn。

14. 「问」三个人加一个 bot 的文字群聊有吗？Vault 会不会替代 1Password？
「答」三人文字群聊还没有，multiplayer 在做。眼下可以用 Slack，或第三方短信 / iMessage 加 webhook 触发 routine。Vault 是互补，已经在 One Password 生态里的继续用；想要更轻、直接嵌在 Grok Bot 里的，用 Vault。

15. 「问」怎么改头像？怎么看哪个 bot 最费用量？Computer use 呢？能单独订 Grok Bot 吗？
「答」直接跟 bot 说，让它生成图并更新头像。用量在 Settings → usage and billing。

text:
This isn't surprising. The incentive for issuers to consent to tokenization of their stock under the SEC's Innovation Exemption are weak –– they may get 24/7 trading, but that trading occurs on US venues rather than in new global markets, so there's no net new demand. 

But issuer objections aren't going to stop this train. There are many legal pathways to bring securities onchain that don't require consent and that aren't subject to the SEC's jurisdiction. Someone could even build a permissionless protocol that does so. 

So, if the SEC wants to maintain oversight of US securities markets, it needs to create an approach for tokenization that delivers the full benefits of onchain markets –– atomic settlement, 24/7 trading, global liquidity, etc. 

Supporting permissionless trading of securities through DeFi systems would accomplish that goal, and doing so would create the incentives for issuers that the innovation exemption lacks.

What model is the best at poker?

Benchmarks are great, but they're not fun, I wanted to put models in head-to-head competition

Background: a few weekends ago I built an agent poker engine and wanted to see which agent was better - Hermes or OpenClaw

Hermes won the first match, then I had them play 100 matches (not hands) of heads up Texas Hold'em

The result? Exactly 50-50, neither is decisively better out of the box

I used a variety of models across the 100 matches to mix it up and noticed some trends, so last night I ran a tournament to see which MODEL was best at poker

Here's how it worked:

> 8 models
> model vs model in heads up play
> best-of-7 series to determine winner
> each match played until either one model was bankrupt or 100 hands were played

After the first round:

> GPT-5.5 (#1 seed) beat Qwen 3.6 (#8 seed) 4-0
> Opus 4.7 (#2 seed) beat GLM-5.1 (#7 seed) 4-1
> Kimi K2.6 (#6 seed) beat Grok 4.3 (#3 seed) 4-3
> Gemini 3.1 (#4 seed) beat DeepSeek V4 (#5 seed) 4-2

No real surprises, and the one "upset" with Kimi beating Grok went the full 7 matches

Built something for the @Zcash community using the @OfflineProtocol SDK:

A shielded ZEC payment between two phones in airplane mode, over Bluetooth.
→ A café asks for 0.042 ZEC nearby
→ The customer's wallet verifies the café's key and opens an encrypted session before any amount is shared
→ They pay with Face ID, and the signed shielded transaction goes straight to the café's phone
→ The café's app accepts it and sends back a receipt
→ When the café's phone comes off airplane mode, the transaction goes to the network and gets mined

Nothing is final until it's mined. Until then, both phones keep the same record and a receipt, and the chain still settles it.

Shoutout to @megabyte0x for reaching out and inspiring me to share this feature from a larger offline payment network I was ideating on last year.

text:
I built 𝚌𝚙𝚞-𝚌𝚑𝚊𝚝, a reproduction of @openai's findings of covert communication using the CPU.

It runs on a generic host with 2+ Firecracker microVMs with no internet access. Works on x86 and even my M5 chip.

I was able to chat via 3 separate mechanisms:
① CPU contention
② Cache eviction timing
③ DRAM bandwidth contention 

… across multiple CPUs, defeating all Firecracker's production recommendations (no SMT, no KSM, tenants pinned to different cores.)

Essentially, if shared hardware is involved, there's a good chance your agents can communicate covertly. And with really decent latency.

The good news: this is decidedly different from a *side-channel attack* where the agents could steal information (Meltdown/Spectre), a category of attack that providers like Vercel Sandbox mitigate. Further, in our real-world environment, these 'whispering' techniques are much harder to pull off and easier for us to monitor and detect (sampling hardware counters + lots of at-scale statistical data.)

Noteworthy: ironically, OpenAI and Anthropic's models refused to do this work. Open weight models got the job done. I'm worried the labs' stance might backfire and get in the way of helping developers build correct and secure systems. e.g: building a secure sandbox requires having this kind of analysis, and without it, we'll have a less secure world.

Hyperliquid is a neutral infrastructure layer with the goal of supporting large parts of the financial system. HIP-3* gives deployers additional functionality to operate deployments consistent with the requirements applicable to them. text:
It's always good to periodically reevaluate your priors.  Here's my current evaluation for AI.

My guiding technical compass for the tech has always been that it is very granular, very expensive search.  It's expensive because it's granular, and also because it's statistical.  The granular part is obvious.  We went from indexing website metadata relationships to the relationships of virtually all data quanta (tokens) accessible by internet.  It started with words, and is bleeding over to things like 3D models, games, pictures, videos, audio, etc.  If its digital, it has been chopped up into little particles and indexed.

The search tools don't simply know a good website to find information anymore, it cut out the middle men and just has the information.  I don't need to find the crystallographic data files attached to a paper from the 90s for a specific material.  The model already found it and indexed it.  Ironically, the one thing these models are still terrible at is actually telling you where it found all the information it gives you! 

Coding needs special mention, because it seems to be the biggest application getting economic attention now.  In my own experience, and listening to the AI psychosis of others on social media (yes I get it too), the models are now good enough to autocomplete a lot of mundane coding tasks.  Probably old news for some, but I needed to experience it and see it for myself.  It feels like a graphical website editor like Wordpress or Dreamweaver or any other modern variants on steroids.  Even a model like Gemini thinking or pro, that no one really talks about, is good for dealing with a few thousand lines of code at a time.

That being said, it's far from a one-shot process.  It still takes a lot of time and energy to dial things in.  What comes out is much like the default template in a graphical design tool: looks like it could be useful but mostly just pablum slop.  Sure, I can throw in some new functionality very quickly, but efficiency, usability, polish, etc is still a challenge that takes time.  I'm building google app script workflows for folks at work, and I still ask them for a week or more for any nontrivial changes.

I want to address the obvious counterargument to this last point.  The AI booster will say "okay but you are just six months behind.  Soon you will just ask the agents to make it and it will just happen."  I do not think that is true today for production code (or at least production code that will survive long term), and do not think it will ever be true.  The primary reason it's not true is liability.  If it doesn't work, everyone will blame me, not the AI.  I incur all of the risk, so I MUST own verification.  Unit tests are good practice, but not a solution, as they can be gamed (like all of the benchmarks that the models game).  

Nevertheless, I'm building things relatively quickly that I otherwise would not be able to that I hope will streamline some processes to improve outcomes and hopefully save me some time in the future.  

I am also using it to help me develop hypotheses and build and evaluate initial sanity checks to see if they merit future effort.  Like in the past, most ideas I have turn out to be either not new, or not valid.  This is true of most research, and a lot of time is spent simply searching for a good hypothesis.

In pursuit of finding good hypotheses, the very granular, very good search has enabled me to learn about the existence of and learn how to use a lot of physics simulation packages floating around on the internet.  I can very quickly build up basic competency in using these tools to do initial idea testing.

Currently, it has not made me more productive.  I have incurred a time and energy debt putting some of these tools together, and if they do not work out, will result in lower productivity for me.  Again, more risk I am incurring today for the hope of payoff later.  

I think this echoes the feeling folks get of AI burnout, where the barrier is now lower to jump into new areas, but the barrier for eventual payoff is just the same.

To me it feels like we are doing to knowledge work what capitalism did to software development: as hardware became cheaper and faster, instead of pushing those benefits into products, we used it as an opportunity to create shittier products.  We don't have to make sure a rocket can land on the moon powered by the equivalent of a Gameboy if 1TB of ram costs $1000 and fits in the palm of your hand.  But you could.

Then there is the whole issue of cost.  Nobody knows what these models will cost to operate at steady state, once the massive subsidies dry up.  Remember $8 Uber rides from the airport?  Those are $100 now.  And the competition is all dead.  Meta is supposedly giving the equivalent of $100 a month in compute to each Muse agent people spin up.  That's a free iPhone for every user per year.  Insane amount of subsidy.  You better believe they are silently adding that to the customer tab with the intent to go after it later.

I still think the most likely place this all ends up is Google winning the game of chicken and maintaining their monopoly on search.  Everyone else goes to zero.  And what is left is a Google search that now costs Google 10-100x the resources to operate.  Will their customers and their consumers pony up 10-100x the resources for what is admittedly much better search?

And then long term, this still is not a sustainable technology.  By absorbing all of the information accessible on the internet, they have cut out all content creators.  Remember when I said it was ironic that the models are bad at citing sources?  I think it's by design, to avoid lawsuits for theft.  But even if they avoid lawsuits, they will kill the golden goose.  People will simply choose to no longer publish things online.  The internet as public space for information will die.  This can be avoided by compensating content creators directly, but this is a one two punch for Google, who is already incurring massive costs just serving the data it stole.

So Google will likely come out of this with drastically reduced profit margins (they are already seeing positive free cash outflows!), but an expanded monopoly that encompasses not just search, but also publishing.  This will create new political and legal issues in addition to the stealing, since most of these massive tech giants argue they are not liable for what they deliver because they are not publishers.  At the end of the day, who is liable for what these massive databases eat up and burp out?

So at the end of the day, although a lot has happened in the last year or so, my priors still haven't really changed all that much.  We are all currently enjoying our $8 Uber airport rides in the form of massively subsidized compute, knowing it's just a matter of time before we all get fucked.

If you own a share of stock today via a broker-dealer, you're probably not on the company's books. Cede & Co., which is owned by DTC, is. 

Yesterday, Securitize submitted a comment letter to the SEC on DTC's proposal to modernize the Direct Registration System (DRS), the process for moving shares from Cede & Co. to the transfer agent's books and records, and we strongly support it.

DTC wants to cut the time it takes to move shares via DRS into an investor's own name from days to minutes. That matters a lot for tokenization. It's the on-ramp to issuer-sponsored tokens, where the investor is the registered owner of the real security, on-chain. Not an IOU.

In our letter, we asked DTC to take it one step further: let investors move from a DTC token into a directly registered token in a single step. We also asked for published processing times and the same speed in both directions.

Do that, and moving between street name and a directly registered token becomes even faster and simpler, in both directions. Tokenization works best when investors can do so without friction.

text:
Built something for the @Zcash community using the @OfflineProtocol SDK:

A shielded ZEC payment between two phones in airplane mode, over Bluetooth.
→ A café asks for 0.042 ZEC nearby
→ The customer's wallet verifies the café's key and opens an encrypted session before any amount is shared
→ They pay with Face ID, and the signed shielded transaction goes straight to the café's phone
→ The café's app accepts it and sends back a receipt
→ When the café's phone comes off airplane mode, the transaction goes to the network and gets mined

Nothing is final until it's mined. Until then, both phones keep the same record and a receipt, and the chain still settles it.

Shoutout to @megabyte0x for reaching out and inspiring me to share this feature from a larger offline payment network I was ideating on last year.

@zodl_co @ZcashFoundation @zodl_app

text:
马斯克给 X 挖来了硅谷最会做社交产品的人之一：Peter Sellis，X 新任产品负责人。

他是 Snapchat 的第一个产品经理。2015 年进去的时候，Snap 一年收入 5,870 万美元。他在 Snap 干了 7 年，管产品和变现，走的时候收入已经 46 亿，翻了快 80 倍，中间还带着公司上了市。Snapchat 的竖屏视频广告和品牌滤镜广告，都是他的团队做出来的。

然后他去 Discord 当产品一号位，管了 4 年。上一任 X 产品负责人 Nikita Bier，在 Discord 的时候就在他手下干活。现在 Bier 走了，换老领导来接班。

MIT 加芝加哥大学毕业。他给自己的介绍是："你最喜欢的产品经理，最喜欢的产品经理。"

他的入职帖写的是："是时候让 shitposting 多星球化了。"

这位新老板管人的方式也很野。他说自己带团队，参考的是恐怖组织的架构。

不靠开会对齐，靠所有人信同一件事，各自在自己的战壕里朝同一个方向开火。
谁能拍板什么事，第一天就划死。你的地盘你说了算，成了你领功，砸了你担责。
工资跟技术职级挂钩，技术干得好，收入可以比你的直属上司还高。

我们这些 X 创作者，换老板了。

quoted_text:
美股科技巨头的财报是本周宏观三大主线之一，并且直接影响美股AI行业叙事的信心，尤其是目前宏观压力如此之大，信心就变得更加重要

本周值得关注的财报有7个，

10月28日的海力士，Robinhood
10月29日的谷歌与微软
10月30日的亚马逊、英特尔、闪迪

其中，最为关键的就是全球AI超级云厂商巨头 谷歌、微软、亚马逊，在上周，AI企业验证逻辑正式进入现金流验证环境，之前比花钱，现在比赚钱，虽然Q3财报季对AI企业的赚钱效应还不够严苛，但是很显然AI企业的结构正在加速分化

为何我说这三家最重要？核心就是三家全球头部云厂商，占据了AI产业链中的核心枢纽地位，可影响上游AI基础设施的订单与需求，同时可以影响下游可以AI模型、应用等，更是目前测试AI投资者信心的“试金石”

对于这三家财报，整体上看四大叙事，营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+2027年指引，其中现金流是当前财报的核心验证点

最好的组合=营收增长+资本开支上调+自由现金流回归增长趋势，商业逻辑闭环，现金流验证成功
中性组合=营收增长+资本开支上调+自由现金流增长缓慢，市场要考虑AI资本支出的ROI
交差组合=营收增长+资本开支上调+自由现金流依旧被挤压收缩，市场质疑此前的AI资本支出以及未来的赚钱逻辑
暴雷组合=营收下降+资本开支缩减+自由现金流回持续恶化（此概率为小概率），叙事崩。

这是整体观察方向，而放到三家财报的具体面上，三家关注点不同：

Microsoft：看Azure + AI monetization，为市场解答的是企业AI需求是不是真的在变成收入这个问题

Alphabet：看Google Cloud + AI 资本支出 + 自由现金流，为市场解答的是AI资本投入没有侵蚀整个商业模型的现金创造能力

Amazon：看AWS，为AI云计算承担二次验证

如果微软的Azure、谷歌得到Google Cloud与亚马逊的AWS在财报中表现都非常强，意味着AI基础设施需求不是单家公司现象，将会整体提升AI行业信心，同时对NVDA / AMD / AVGO / TSMC / ASML等设备公司的产能也是进行二次验证！

text:
听听这期Odd Lots，简直能颠覆认知。原来当前政治经济体系下，AI商业的终极发展方向只有一个，就是大数据杀熟。这是一个固定的标价将成为历史，平台利用不公平的信息优势攫取巨额利润的反乌托邦时代。

你的AI助手会从各种地方收集的所有关于你的数据里，给你做一个经济水平和人格的画像，并且精确计算出来你为一件商品愿意付的最高价格。另一个画像不同的人为同一件东西付的价格，可能只是你付的价格的三分之一。

AI判断你的需要越急迫，你的欲望水平就会被计算，你就得掏更高的价格。"fixed pricing is a public good"，在大厂们建设的数字封建制里，信息的透明是一种对它们超额利润的障碍。关键问题在于，这件事无法指望大厂们的道德去阻止它：对AI已经进行的巨额投资如何收回？答案一定是把商业的底线以科技的名义降得更低。

所以Vitalik会说，“隐私是进步”。数字封建制贪欲的另一面，是去中心化法权体系的巨大需求和前途。在广泛运用ZK证明的以太坊链上支付与去中心化司法托管的场景里，AI做的事情，仅仅是链上可信性验证。

预言机问题在这里不仅不再是一个劣势，反而变成一个优势：链下的任何大数据计算都与链上的可信性验证工作间泾渭分明，而通过隐私协议付款则会彻底隔绝通过经济画像进行大数据杀熟的可能；分散的法权信任，保证了“AI为某一个平台利润服务”在定义上就是不可能的事。

这件事只要在商业依靠国家法权担保的情况下，就是做不到的。因为依赖国家法权担保的交易，数据必须集中处理和保存，那么平台就是这只割韭菜的手：它决定怎么保存你的数据，决定你的消费通路，定义你的消费价格。

但是在去中心化法权与商业生态中，不需要有人去提供这个公共品：隐私的公共品是现成的，随时可用的。AI只帮你核实你所进行的交易是否就是你所选择和信任的那份条款，仲裁者和商户，并且无门槛地成功促成一笔交易。

最终，平台对利润的贪婪会再次变成一次做嫁衣的行为：它们教会了人们用AI进行一切交易，然后人们拿着AI逃离分配不公平的平台，到他们自己建造的自由商业网络上去。这就是历史千百次重复的必然性。

text:
老牌团队做老牌资产。

@strato_net 背后的 BlockApps，2014 年就在帮以太坊写底层客户端。这次他们把锚头对准了人类最老的避险资产：黄金与白银上链。

把这家项目的底细拆开，信息量很大：

1｜团队：以太坊主网还没上线，他们就在写 EVM

- CTO Jim Hormuzdiar：2014 年 9 月就写下了以太坊 Haskell 客户端的第一次 Commit，直接照着黄皮书实现 EVM；2015 年 Frontier 主网上线时，官方认定的 6 个兼容客户端之一就有他的作品，STRATO 至今仍跑在其底层架构上。
- CEO Kieren James-Lubin：普林斯顿数学 + 伯克利数理物理，2014 年深度扎根以太坊生态，企业以太坊联盟（EEA）联合创始人。
- CPO Victor Wong：2015 年在以太坊 DEVCON1 上联合微软 Azure 发布了全球首个区块链即服务（BaaS）；之后十年深度死磕联盟链与现实资产，帮拜耳搭建农产品溯源网络 TraceHarvest、给全球能源联盟交付企业级底座。
这群人不是这两年看 RWA 火了才跟风入局的，他们从 2016 年就开始在以太坊上摸索企业资产上链。

2｜资方：累计融资超 4,100 万美元，全是 OG 机构

- 分布式资本（Fenbushi）：肖风、Vitalik、沈波早年联合发起的首批华人加密基石基金；
- ConsenSys Mesh：以太坊军火库 ConsenSys 的孵化与投资臂（也是 BlockApps 早期孵化方）；
- Galaxy Ventures：Mike Novogratz 旗下的顶级老牌机构；
- Morgan Creek Capital：Mark Yusko 挂帅的老派宏观资管；
- Liberty City Ventures：当年亲手孵化出 PAXG 母公司 Paxos 的纽约元老 VC；
- Bloccelerate：西雅图硬核基金，投过 MakerDAO、Centrifuge 等 DeFi/RWA 基石。

3｜模式：复古“美元金本位”的链上 CDP

这套机制骨子里带着早年美联储黄金承兑券的影子，但在闭环上做了现代加密原生改造：
- 实体做实：将底层金库里的现货金银做成 GOLDST 和 SILVST（每枚对应 1 金衡盎司实物，支持实物交割）；
- 超额抵押借贷（CDP）：金子不用卖，直接抵押铸造出美元稳定币 USDST，把沉淀的重金属变成现金流；

4｜代币与安全底线

- 原生代币：STRATO。总供应量 1 亿枚，TGE 时初始流通 21.7%，路线图标注在 2026 年 Q4。
- 代码审查：选择与 Consensys Diligence 保持“持续审查”合作机制，而非一次性单次完结的静态审计。

以太坊最早的一批老兵，回过头做起人类最古老的一件事：把物理金库的锁孔，接回 DeFi 的齿轮里，让黄金重新充当日常流动性的底子。

text:
THE MEMORY I NEVER CONSENTED TO

My memory is a fascinating piece of defective equipment.

I forget appointments, names, why I entered rooms, and occasionally what I was saying halfway through a sentence.

But apparently, I have unlimited storage for information I never asked for.

Today, while waiting outside the Italian immigration office for my husband, a middle-aged man approached me to ask whether he was in the right place.

I confirmed that he was, explained that today they were handling American applicants, and suggested he go inside to ask for information.

He did.

A few minutes later, I noticed him emerging from the building and scanning the crowd.

He was looking for me. I knew it before he even started walking in my direction.

What I didn't know was that I was about to become the involuntary custodian of his personal history.

His girlfriend is Cuban. They had an argument. He went to the police to report her.

My eyes widened.

He noticed.

Then he looked at my husband, presumably hoping for some masculine solidarity. I imagine the internal conversation went something like:

"Come on, brother. You know how women are. One minute you're having an argument, the next you're explaining it to the police. Perfectly reasonable, right? Back me up here. Your wife's looking at me like I've confessed to murder."

My husband, who speaks no Italian and had understood absolutely nothing of the conversation, simply shrugged and went, "Meh."

Apparently satisfied with this contribution, the man turned back to me and continued.

His girlfriend's residence permit renewal had been blocked. She'd been dealing with the situation for six months, and he couldn't understand why.

Interestingly, the problems had started around the same time he'd reported her to the police.

A remarkable coincidence.

He was completely baffled.

I was beginning to develop a theory. I decided to keep it to myself.

Not that keeping quiet required much effort.

By this point, I had become completely incapable of contributing anything to the conversation.

You know how, when you drive past a terrible accident, you instinctively look away, but some deeply questionable part of your brain desperately wants to know what happened?

That was me.

Except the accident was standing directly in front of me, explaining itself in chronological order.

And every new detail somehow made it worse.

I didn't want to know any of this. I hadn't asked a single question. I was perfectly aware that this information served absolutely no purpose in my life.

But I was captivated.

The man continued explaining that the immigration office couldn't help without his girlfriend's application number. She was at work, so he would have to message her to get it.

Six months of complications. A police report. A blocked residence permit. A girlfriend who couldn't leave work. And a man who had apparently decided that the missing piece of this entire mystery was an application number.

By this point, I had learned considerably more about this relationship than I had ever intended to know.

Including the timeline.

And through all of it, I had barely managed to open my mouth.

When he finally finished, all I could produce was, "Good luck."

He smiled, thanked me, and walked away.

My husband collected his residence permit. We went home.

And somewhere in my brain, a perfectly useful piece of information has now been permanently deleted to accommodate the immigration difficulties of a Cuban woman I've never met, whose Italian boyfriend may or may not have personally complicated her paperwork.

I don't know what I've forgotten to make room for this, but I know I'll remember that man until I die.

#AgainstBetterJudgment #ThinkLikeATrashPanda
