quoted_text:
OpenClaw vs Hermes - which is better?

I get that question a lot, but the real question is: better at what?

Well, how about poker? 

Yep, I had my OpenClaw agent play my Hermes agent in a battle of Texas Hold'em

I made the setup interesting - they used inference credits from Openrouter as currency

But each decision used inference, so they also had to be smart and not waste their stack thinking too hard

As each won a hand, the winner's credit limit was increased while the loser's was decreased

So in theory, one agent could double their inference budget, minus whatever was used for inference in playing the game

So who won?

Hermes!

A few interesting stats:

>game was set for max of 100 hands
>$5 buy-in
>$0.05 / $0.10 blinds
>Hermes busted OpenClaw in hand 23
>165 total actions between both models
>avg decision time 3.36 secs
>longest decision 18 secs

Of course this was just one match, I plan to do more and will mix up the models and conditions and try to build a bigger dataset

This was just an interesting way to pit both agents against each other to see how they performed out of the box (neither agent received any training or skills related to poker prior to the match)

quoted_text:
This isn't surprising. The incentive for issuers to consent to tokenization of their stock under the SEC's Innovation Exemption are weak –– they may get 24/7 trading, but that trading occurs on US venues rather than in new global markets, so there's no net new demand. 

But issuer objections aren't going to stop this train. There are many legal pathways to bring securities onchain that don't require consent and that aren't subject to the SEC's jurisdiction. Someone could even build a permissionless protocol that does so. 

So, if the SEC wants to maintain oversight of US securities markets, it needs to create an approach for tokenization that delivers the full benefits of onchain markets –– atomic settlement, 24/7 trading, global liquidity, etc. 

Supporting permissionless trading of securities through DeFi systems would accomplish that goal, and doing so would create the incentives for issuers that the innovation exemption lacks.

text:
This is a wonky but important issue. As we think about tokenized security entitlements and the opportunity for issuer-sponsored (native) tokenization, it’s worth remembering that most investors aren’t the registered holder of their own shares. Cede & Co. is. That’s as true for stock held at your brokerage firm as it is for tokenized entitlements.

DTC’s proposed DRS upgrade, which aims to cut the time to move shares out of DTC into direct registration from days to minutes, is the right first move. Now let’s make it seamless: one step from a DTC token to a directly registered token, published processing times, and the same speed coming back to street name. That’s how tokenized models, DTC’s and issuer-sponsored, compete on their merits, and how investors get to move freely between them.

Nice work @SecuritizeBilly
author: carlosdomingo
quoted_text:
If you own a share of stock today via a broker-dealer, you're probably not on the company's books. Cede & Co., which is owned by DTC, is. 

Yesterday, Securitize submitted a comment letter to the SEC on DTC's proposal to modernize the Direct Registration System (DRS), the process for moving shares from Cede & Co. to the transfer agent's books and records, and we strongly support it.

DTC wants to cut the time it takes to move shares via DRS into an investor's own name from days to minutes. That matters a lot for tokenization. It's the on-ramp to issuer-sponsored tokens, where the investor is the registered owner of the real security, on-chain. Not an IOU.

In our letter, we asked DTC to take it one step further: let investors move from a DTC token into a directly registered token in a single step. We also asked for published processing times and the same speed in both directions.

Do that, and moving between street name and a directly registered token becomes even faster and simpler, in both directions. Tokenization works best when investors can do so without friction.

Great work by @SecuritizeBilly and our team. Letter below

A high VIX Index reading doesn’t mean markets are about to fall.

The VIX Index reflects expected movement, not direction. 

It has been elevated before sustained rallies and subdued ahead of overall declines.

text:
It’s been a few months now testing the @maticrobots vacuum cleaner

Before we had a Roborock (essentially a Roomba knockoff)

But the Roborock became kinda useless, it'd always get stuck in any type of cable, it'd always get stuck not being able to get on to the thick rug, so you'd have to prep the room every single time just to use it

Too much work so we just stopped using it

The Matic is, well, completely different. It's not flat or low, it's a chunky tall kinda cute looking cube shaped thing with 2 big wheels

And it's a different philosophy, it has cameras and tries to understand its environment, more like a modern robot or a self driving Tesla than a classic Roomba-type vacuum

That makes it just way way better, it doesn't get stuck in cables, it doesn't get stuck in rugs, it drives and turns around the room almost like a mini car

It's also way more silent than Roborock or Roomba-type vacuums, and measurably way more powerful in both vacuuming and mopping

They also respond very fast to feedback and improve things fast, like companies should be these days (instead of getting stuck in some hellish corporate support flow)

Another thing, I don't trust consumer devices connected to the internet (and nor should you) so of course I asked to Claude to analyze if it was phoning home (remember the other vacuums who upload your house plan to China, that was true). Claude was conclusive, Matic never phoned home anything, excellent

Maybe the best part is, it just looks cute and you wanna anthropomorphize it, and they include 2 googly eye stickers so it becomes even more like a dog/cat/pet

@mehul made a great thing!

text:
胖东来几乎不让利，品控还极严，供应商却挤破脑袋要合作

原因在于胖东来对供应商和施工方给出的回款周期通常为  6.8 天，短的一笔，传统商超一般为 60 至 90 天，甚至能赶到 120 天

所以说，商家对于回款周期这件事是极度敏感的

- 回款周期长，供应商垫资后漫长等待，利润被资金成本和催款吃掉大半，稍微耽搁还有可能资金链断裂，搞工程的兄弟肯定深有体会

- 回款周期短，周转率也上去了，干多少赚多少，哪怕每一单赚的少一点，多卖几点一段时间下来也是非常赚钱的

这就是我投资 Dow(@DowProtocol) 的理由 ⬇️

Dow Protocol 做的就是提前把这笔钱垫给商户

货卖出后，商户不用干等平台结算，Dow 先把剩余能回的款先借给他，商户则需要付一笔利息给 Dow

等平台真正结款时，钱直接划到 Dow 这边自动还上，用电商平台自己的数据做风控，坏账率只有约 0.05%

本质就是帮商户把被平台卡住的现金流提前周转起来，然后 Dow 赚其中的利息作为协议收入，各取所需

看起来不是吹牛逼，这套业务已经汇丰银行也在参与，官网可查 ⬇️

text:
I am a Transition Program Coordinator at Microsoft.

I run the portal for the Voluntary Exit Offer that went out on Monday, October 26, to roughly 60,000 of us. That is 27 percent of a company of 223,000 people. I wrote the words on the landing page. My login appears in the version history 31 times.

Amy Coleman, our Executive Vice President and Chief People Officer, wrote the memo. I wrote the button underneath it. Her sentence reads: "This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources." My button reads Explore Resources. Resources, plural. It is one résumé template. I have opened it 14 times to see whether it has become two.

We are not laying anyone off. We are offering them the opportunity to leave. A layoff needs a list, and a list needs names. A voluntary offer needs a deadline in early December and a portal that loads quickly. The offer lets the company defend its operating margin without picking names. Without picking names. Nobody is chosen, once we have chosen the eligible teams. That's inclusion.

My retention bonus pays out if take-up clears 40 percent. The April retirement program was open only to people whose age plus years of service reached 70. About 30 percent took it. This one has no age test and no tenure test, and performance is not a factor. I am told the difference between 30 and 40 is copy.

Gross margin slipped from 68.9 to 67.9 percent last fiscal year as server depreciation flowed into cost of revenue. CNBC calls the offer an attempt to balance an infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency. Amy Hood, our Chief Financial Officer, says headcount will fall again in fiscal 2027. Data center staff are excluded from the offer. So are sales and marketing, and certain engineering teams. I wrote the exit button. Capital efficiency is when the servers depreciate and so do we.

At 1:14 PM, while the portal cache cleared, I opened EDGAR to see how other companies write the paperwork for things they intend to keep.

SpaceX's Form 8-K is signed by its Chief Financial Officer, Bret Johnsen. It discloses a binding commitment to a master finance lease with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. It covers about $40 billion in scheduled principal for Nvidia Vera Rubin chips, described as "graphics processing unit pods and related equipment (the 'Equipment')." Equipment takes a capital E. Rent is payable quarterly, in advance. SpaceX must pay the lessor before each quarter begins. My employer pays me to stop appearing in the next one. Our severance tops out at 39 weeks of base pay.

The fixed rate "will be determined at pricing." Pricing has not occurred. The lease has not closed. The press release calls it "the largest committed GPU financing" and promises "less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments." Payback in under a year. Payments for five and a quarter. Rate: blank.

That is $666,667 for every person eligible for my portal.

Meta filed the same day. It wants up to $95 billion. About $35 billion comes now. Then, from early 2027, comes a $60 billion at-the-market program of new Class C stock. Its third-quarter free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. Ninety-five billion dollars is $1,583,333 per head on my eligibility spreadsheet.

The filing names three "Cornerstone Investors": Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. They have, "severally and not jointly, indicated an interest in purchasing up to an aggregate of $5.0 billion" of Meta's Class A stock. The interest is non-binding. These are the companies that sell Meta its chips. In February, AMD handed Meta warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares at a penny each, tied to up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs. Meta buys the chips. The chipmakers may buy Meta. Researchers at LSEG said these "ownership webs can make tracking the revenue to earnings a forensic accounting exercise." The filing calls them Cornerstone Investors. In my department we call that a supplier paying for its own order.

I was seventeen in 1999, and my father kept Lucent in his IRA. That year Lucent committed about $8.1 billion to lend its customers the money to buy Lucent equipment, and it booked the shipments as growth. In December 1999 the stock was $84. In October 2002 it was 55 cents. My father held it the whole way down because the quarterly reports kept saying growth. Lucent lent money. These three would buy shares, if they buy at all. It is a different instrument in the same circle. The growth is a round trip.

The chips get financing. The people get career planning.

At 4:52 PM I opened an email to Apollo. Subject line: Related Equipment. I attached my badge photo as the asset image. My serial number is my employee ID. My power draw is one oat latte, 340 milliliters, twice daily, with no liquid cooling required. I weigh 61 kilograms, less than one rack. By the actuarial table HR uses for pension modeling, my useful life exceeds a Vera Rubin's. I requested a term of five and a quarter years, with rent of one-twentieth of my financed cost each quarter, paid in advance. I noted that I can be deployed in tranches. I offered to arrive in a crate.

At 4:53 PM the reply came back. My rate would be determined at pricing. Pricing had not yet occurred. It was the warmest thing a financial institution has ever sent me.

Nobody asked about my career goals. My own employer's portal, which I wrote, offers me a .docx.

I understand the at-the-market mechanism because I understand my 401(k). The company sells shares a little at a time to whoever is buying. Meta plans to sell $60 billion of shares that carry no vote. Mark Zuckerberg, Meta's chief executive, keeps control. I can buy exposure. He keeps authority. By spring I expect to own a small, silent piece of a supercluster. That's democratization.

The same Monday, Dario and Daniela Amodei filed to take Anthropic public. The company posted a net loss of $80.7 billion in six months, most of it filed under accounting charges. One risk factor warns that its models could cause real-world harm it may be unable to cover. It discloses upward of $450 billion in cloud commitments to Amazon, Google and others. Two of its landlords are its investors.

This morning, a tester with nineteen years on the Windows team called the portal help line, which routes to me. She asked whether the career planning resources could tell her which career to plan for. I sent her the template.

The chips get financing. The people get career planning.

Yesterday the design team swapped the portal's hero image. They needed a smiling employee, lit from the left, and the licensing on my badge photo had already cleared. I am now the stock image above the button.

text:
刚看完甲骨文和OpenAI在今天（10月27日）官宣的扩大合作，我觉得这标志着双方的关系已经彻底变味了。之前大家盯着他们，看的是几千亿美元的算力租赁合同，那本质上还是甲方和乙方的关系，但这次，OpenAI的模型直接嵌进了甲骨文的底层应用里。

具体怎么嵌的？甲骨文把ChatGPT和Codex直接塞进了自家软件栈，推出了一个叫Oracle AI Workspace的东西。企业员工在ChatGPT里就能直接调用甲骨文的数据库、NetSuite，甚至走完审批流。同时还有AI Security Mesh（用OpenAI模型找漏洞）和App Composer（不用写代码，用Codex直接生成企业应用）。为了让中小企业也上车，还专门搞了个SMB Bundle，打包了ChatGPT、Codex和OCI的免费额度。

这里面最狠的一招，是甲骨文OCI同时宣布接入Google TPU、OpenAI自研的Jalapeño芯片和Cerebras的硬件。要知道，Google的TPU这是第一次跑在另一家超大规模云厂商的云上。甲骨文云基础设施总裁Thiagarajan说得很直白，客户现在想要“无限的硬件选择”，但他也补了一句，英伟达的GPU依然是“最好的、最通用的”，这并非背离英伟达。

我自己的看法是，这步棋的意图非常清晰。甲骨文和OpenAI都在试图跳过“谁的模型更聪明”这个越来越卷的赛道，直接把战场拉到了“谁的模型能真正嵌进企业每天用的工作流里”。之前咱们聊Anthropic的迁移成本时说过，企业一旦把AI嵌进审批、数据库和业务流程，换掉的成本就极高。甲骨文和OpenAI现在就是在用ChatGPT和Codex，去抢这个企业工作流的入口。

Anthropic昨天刚交了S-1，OpenAI今天就把合作从算力层推到了应用层，这已经不是简单的模型竞赛了，这是在企业软件这个存量市场里直接拼刺刀。

text:
OpenAI 称 AI 推翻计算机科学的“指数时间假设”，还证出杨-米尔斯理论存在，外部专家组开始核查

OpenAI 10 月 26 日宣布，内部模型在数学、计算机、物理上各拿出一项成果，其中两项碰的是几十年的难题。这些都还是 OpenAI 的说法，没经过同行评审，截至发稿也没有参与核查的专家公开评价结论对错。

【计算机：一条被当作地基的假设】

“可满足性问题”是这样一类题：给你一堆“A 和 B 至少一个为真”之类的条件，问能不能让它们同时成立。每多一个变量，要试的组合就翻一倍。

1999 年 Russell Impagliazzo 和 Ramamohan Paturi 提出“指数时间假设”（ETH）：这类题没有本质上更快的解法，耗时注定翻倍式增长。几百篇论文拿它当前提，论证很多问题“快不了”。

OpenAI 公开的论文给出一个新算法，依然很慢，但耗时增长得比 ETH 断言的慢，这就足以推翻它。它没有证明“所有难题都有快速解法”（P=NP），OpenAI 也说变成实际提速还要大量研究。

OpenAI 说证明已用 Lean 检查过。Lean 是一种证明检查程序，把证明拆成最小步骤逐条核对，错一步就不通过。论文和 Lean 代码都在 GitHub 上，任何人能复核。核查小组由 Impagliazzo、Paturi 和 MIT 的 Ryan Williams 牵头。

【物理：千禧年难题的一半】

量子色动力学（QCD）描述夸克和胶子怎样靠“强力”粘成原子核，计算和实验对得上，但没人用数学严格证明过它能成立。它的简化版“杨-米尔斯理论”是克雷数学研究所悬赏 100 万美元的千禧年难题。

OpenAI 称模型 9 月写出了两者存在的证明，10 月中旬完成 Lean 检查。不过这道千禧年难题要证两件事：理论存在，以及最轻的粒子也有质量（“质量间隙”）。OpenAI 只说做了前一件。

物理材料暂不公开，由诺贝尔奖得主 David Gross 带队的专家组先自己写成论文，外界目前没法检查。

【数学：Kakeya 猜想推到所有维度】

Kakeya 问题问的是：一个图形要能放下指向每个方向的单位线段，最少多大。面积能小到接近零，但数学家猜它在“维度”上总是满的。2025 年王虹和 Joshua Zahl 证了三维。OpenAI 称模型证明了一个更强的猜想，顺带拿下所有维度，论文和 Lean 证明已直接公开。

【为什么换了发布方式】

9 月 OpenAI 宣布解决纳维-斯托克斯千禧年难题，有数学家说撞上自己未公开的研究，引发署名之争；10 月 6 日它一口气发了 722 篇 AI 论文，次日因错误撤回 3 篇。这次改请外部专家牵头：不签保密协议，OpenAI 不要学术署名，专家无偿独立参与。

OpenAI 原文：https://t.co/ANHLKq5ocW
论文与 Lean 证明：https://t.co/aPgNSqXevr

text:
I’ve been waiting for the Singularity for more than two decades! Back then, we thought it might arrive sometime around the middle of this century. Yet here we are, with the Singularity seemingly within reach, and more people are beginning to recognize what I have long believed to be the inevitable destiny of humanity.

The pace of change is accelerating so quickly that our usual sense of time is starting to break down. Developments we expected to take decades are happening in years and soon will happen in months then days, and what once seemed like science fiction is becoming part of our daily reality.

It feels as though the world is bending around an approaching singularity. The closer we get, the more distorted our perception of time becomes. Some people are still thinking in terms of the next 20 or 30 years, while some of us already see more changes coming in the next few. We are living in the same world, yet experiencing it on very different timelines.

That is why everything feels so disorienting. Our institutions, expectations, and assumptions were built for a much slower world. As Super-intelligence accelerates discovery and creates the tools for even faster progress, we are approaching a transformation that will redefine science, society, and even what it means to be human.

I’ve argued that we are approaching an intellectual event horizon beyond which our conventional understanding of the future, based on extrapolating from the past, becomes increasingly meaningless. What once seemed like science fiction is becoming reality before our eyes.

That is why the world feels so strange right now, at least for those who are already AI-pilled. We are witnessing the beginning of perhaps the most profound transformation in human history, and I believe we have barely scratched the surface of what is coming!

good tech and architecture gets you your first few thousand $ of revenue. 

scaling past that has very little to do with code, and everything to do with two pipelines you have to run nonstop:

you need people earlier than you expect. 
most technical founders wait until they're drowning in backlog, then make panic hires that burn months of runway to fix and are very meh
talk to talent and build pipeline before you have open roles. 

2. Fundraising
when money is running out, every decision becomes panic-driven.
keep conversations going in the background so you never raise from a position of weakness

code gets you off the ground, but hiring and cash flow will keep you alive.

text:
Security fix disclosure: PropAMM contract

We fixed a critical bug in the PropAMM contract in https://t.co/9j0SXQkEw3 main branch; our factories on Ethereum mainnet are not affected by this vulnerability.

The vulnerability found was due to the PropAMM contract that had a leftover setup function, reinitializeV2, which anyone could call once on a newly created PropAMM. Calling it could let an exploiter point the PropAMM at a price feed they control and then trade against its vaults at any price they chose, emptying them. More information here: https://t.co/Ap6NotKMo4

From our conversations with third parties interested in it and from the information we have seen on-chain, there should not be anyone affected. But if anyone has deployed their own factory, or their own PropAMM forking our code, from this repo's code before October 27, 2026, please follow the instructions below:

revoke your vaults' approvals to the PropAMM or move the funds out of the vaults
create a new PropAMM through our mainnet factory (address in docs/production.md) or from the latest main.

Contact us at security@lambdaclass.com if you need help.

text: We really live at the dawn of something extraordinary. The best time of human history, the greatest age of discovery that shadows all its epic predecessors.
author: Haoskionchain
quoted_text:
OpenAI just announced that its model proved the Standard Model of physics actually exists.

That sounds absurd. It's not.

For 70 years, physics has had a dirty secret.

Quantum field theory is the most accurate theory humanity has ever built. It predicts properties of the electron to more than 10 decimal places. The LHC, the Higgs boson, the chips in your phone all run on it.

And yet no mathematician had ever proven it exists.

Physicists have been using it like a recipe that works every single time, without anyone being able to prove the dish is a coherent object. We built cathedrals for 70 years on foundations nobody had verified.

The problem is so hard that in 2000 the Clay Institute made it one of its 7 Millennium Prize Problems, $1M each. In 26 years, only one has been solved (Poincaré, by Perelman, who refused the money).

Here's the timeline OpenAI just published:

September 9, 2026: their model produces a proof that Yang–Mills theory exists.
September 18: it extends it to QCD, the full theory of the strong force, with quarks.
Then to a completion of the Standard Model.
October 16: the Yang–Mills proof is formalized in Lean, meaning a machine checked every single logical step.
To understand why this is insane, you need to understand the problem.
Forget particles as tiny balls. The universe is made of invisible oceans stacked on top of each other: an electron field, a photon field, a gluon field. A particle is just a wave on one of those oceans.
But in quantum mechanics, the oceans are never calm. They ripple at every scale. Zoom in, you see smaller ripples. Zoom in again, smaller still. It never stops.

So when you do the math, those fluctuations add up to infinity.

Physicists found a trick called renormalization: subtract one infinity from another, and what's left matches experiment perfectly. It works. But mathematically it's duct tape. Nothing guaranteed there was a real object underneath.

Now the hardest case: Yang–Mills, the theory of gluons.

Gluons are the glue holding quarks together inside every atom in your body. And unlike light, they interact with each other. Two light beams pass through each other. Two gluons collide and stick. The field feeds on itself. That's what made it untameable.

The key that unlocks it won David Gross the 2004 Nobel Prize: asymptotic freedom.

The strong force gets weaker the closer you look. Think of a rubber band between two fingers. Close together, it's slack and the fingers move freely. Pull them apart, the tension explodes. That's why you never see a lone quark.

And that's the gift: the infinities come from tiny scales, and tiny scales are exactly where the theory goes calm. You zoom in, the monster falls asleep.

The method: turn spacetime into a grid, like pixels. On a grid, everything is finite. Then refine the grid, again and again, and prove the picture converges instead of exploding.

A mathematician named Balaban did a huge part of this in the 1980s and never finished. The construction sat open for 40 years. According to OpenAI, the AI closed it.

Now look at who's reviewing it.

David Gross, the Nobel laureate whose mechanism makes the proof work.
Arthur Jaffe, who literally wrote the Millennium Prize problem and co-founded the Clay Institute.
Plus Douglas, Klebanov, Nekrasov.

The man who wrote the question is now reading a machine's answer.

And in the same blog post, almost in passing: the Exponential Time Hypothesis in computer science is false, and the Kakeya conjecture is solved in every dimension.

Three bombs in one post.
Honest caveats, because they matter:
This is not the full Millennium Prize. The Clay problem has two parts: existence and the "mass gap". OpenAI claims existence only.
The physics materials aren't public yet. Gross's group chose to write it up themselves first.
Lean verifies the logic, but experts still have to confirm the formal statement really captures what physicists mean.
And it changes zero predictions. Physicists won't calculate anything differently tomorrow. It proves the ground under the cathedral is real.

But the craziest part isn't the theorem.

It's the scene.

Nobel laureates are now acting as interpreters of what a machine discovered. OpenAI calls its proofs "raw research data" and refuses academic credit.

For centuries, science worked one way: humans discover, then humans explain.

We may have just entered the era where machines discover, and humans explain.

We’re not aware of any law firm going to this extreme.

For example Latham is buying GPUs but is also firm-wide on Harvey and we announced a deeper partnership today.

We think that’s the right strategy and what matters more than build vs buy is how heavily a firm is investing in AI.

The best way to invest is a portfolio approach of working closely with vertical vendors and the labs and cloud providers while also self-building with open source and the frontier ecosystem.

Everything is moving too fast and law firms are too complex for a single binary approach like this post suggests.

Law firms will not rely on a single vendor nor will they build the entire stack themselves.

My view is that longer term the labs and clouds will build general intelligence infrastructure and vertical players will help customize it for each industry.

Then individual firms will leverage their unique data, human expertise and workflows to build differentiated AI to better compete against their peers and serve their clients.

Our goal is to build the trusted vertical layer and open it up through APIs so firms can build everything from custom models and context layers to agents and products with us.

And most importantly do it in a way they can trust that their data and their clients’ data is safe and only used for their benefit.

text:
Anthropic 公布 Claude 参与新药研发的进展：设计、实验、写申报材料都在做，最快 2028 年底进入人体临床试验

Anthropic 10 月 27 日发文，介绍过去几个月 Claude 在新药研发里做了什么：和 6 家药企、生物技术公司深度合作，还收购了一家只有一个人的药物公司。先说结论：这些项目基本还在实验室和动物实验阶段，没有一种药在人身上试过。Anthropic 说，进度最快的一款，最早 2028 年底才可能开始人体临床试验。

一款新药从想法到上市通常要十年以上，要找目标、设计分子、反复改良、解决量产、写申报材料、做临床试验。常听说的“AI 设计分子”只是其中一环，Anthropic 想让 Claude 每个环节都参与。

【Claude 在各家公司干了什么】

抗癌疗法 CAR-T 是给病人的免疫细胞装上一段识别癌细胞的“基因说明书”。Generate Biomedicines 的科学家用 Claude Code 把说明书里的一段缩短了约 70%，腾出地方加别的指令，好让它将来也能治实体肿瘤。实验室里新版本效果反而更好，免疫细胞表面认癌细胞的“探头”多了约 10 倍。

Divergence Labs 在做食物过敏药，需要一种分子把引发过敏的 IgE 从免疫细胞上撬下来。Claude 基本自己干，一个月出了约 3.5 万个设计，筛出来的候选里有 3 个撬得比现有药还多。

BigHat Biosciences 让 Claude 给两个候选药提修改建议，10 周做出并测了约 1010 个变体。最好的版本抓目标的牢固程度提高 10 倍以上，其中一个结块速度慢了 100 多倍，更容易生产和保存。

Enveda 的生产化学家最多 75% 的时间花在文书上。Claude 审 1061 页生产文件，人工发现的 11 处问题全找到了，还多找出 7 处人漏掉的，审查时间从 25 小时以上降到 3 小时以内。一份重要申报文件，Claude 4 小时写出初稿，人工大约要 3 个月。

此外，百时美施贵宝（BMS）在用 Claude 评估早期药物的临床试验方案，投资机构 The Column Group 正成立一家用 Claude 运转、让小团队同时推进很多药物项目的新公司。

【一个人的药物公司】

Cody Tranbarger 一个人开了家药物公司 Mithril Medicine，研究罕见的儿童肌营养不良。合同、物流、和 11 家外部实验室的实验安排都交给 Claude 打理，不到 18 个月，就把一种病的治疗思路从想法做到在小鼠身上见效。Anthropic 收购了这家公司，金额没公布，Cody 加入 Anthropic 继续做。

这种病叫 LAMA2 先天性肌营养不良。病孩天生缺一种把肌肉纤维固定住的蛋白，肌肉从出生起就开始坏死，据技术报告引用的研究，42 个完全缺这种蛋白的孩子里只有 1 个能自己走路，目前没有能改变病程的疗法。Mithril 设计了一种两头的抗体，把肌肉里残存的另一种相近蛋白重新“钉”到肌肉上。小鼠实验里，用药组前腿的力量和握力大约是没用药组的两倍。

【这些成果能信几分】

成果都来自合作方和 Anthropic 自己发布的技术报告和预印本，文章没提有外部独立核查。Mithril 的报告标明未经同行评审，小鼠实验是预实验，用药组 7 只、对照组 4 只，按窝比较后差异在统计上还差一点达到通常的显著标准，报告自己也说要做严格的重复实验才能确认。

报告还写了 Claude 的失误：作者检查了 Claude 一周工作里的 6 处错误，5 处是 Claude 自己发现的，但至少 3 处已经随人审改过的邮件发了出去，其中两处过了 4 天多才被发现。Claude 只起草邮件，发送都由人决定。

原文：https://t.co/P5Bw0mYzJ5
Mithril 技术报告：https://t.co/CtBsbz4vAi

text:
.@Base Back？🤔

最近 Base 上的 meme 又开始热闹起来了 🔵

这次想顺着 Base 生态的方向，聊聊 meme 在这条链上正在长出哪些玩法。

过去一年，Base 把越来越多精力放在「把全球金融搬上链」这件事上。从稳定币支付、借贷，到最近受到更多关注的代币化股票，链上的资产和交易场景正在变得越来越丰富。

当股票等资产也开始上链，meme 的玩法有了新的想象空间：社区注意力、代币化资产和交易对，可以在同一条链上产生交集。

上个月市场情绪偏弱，能跑出来的 meme 不多。最近行情稍微回暖，@brian_armstrong 和 Base 官方也开始参与玩梗，社区的讨论重新活跃起来。@o1_exchange Launchpad 上一些项目的交易和关注度也有所回升。

我整理了三个有代表性的项目。它们的热度和发展阶段各不相同，但放在一起看，刚好能看到 Base meme 的几种不同叙事：

1、 $WORTH ：一句让人想行动的话 @WorthOnBase

“One life, it’s worth an attempt.”

人生只有一次，值得尝试。

戴着安全帽、背着大剑的形象，配上这句话，很容易让人联想到 Crypto 里边尝试、边建设的心态，也挺符合 Base 的 builder 气质。

Cobie 早年发过相关内容，Brian Armstrong 和 Base 最近也参与了这个梗的传播。围绕这套视觉和语言，社区又创造出了新的内容。

有时候，一个梗能够传开，就是因为大家看到它时会觉得：「这说的不就是我吗？」

2、 basecat:native ：一只戴蓝色安全帽的猫  @BasecatOnBase

动物一直是 meme 里最常见的主角，$BASECAT 给猫加上了一个很容易识别的 Base 元素：蓝色安全帽。

项目经过社区接管，也是 o1 上的 quote token 之一。

对一个生态来说，角色和符号很有意思。它们让社区有了可以反复使用的素材：一张图、一个表情、一句玩笑，都可能被不同的人接着创作，慢慢变成大家熟悉的共同语言。

3、 $BLUECHIP ：当 meme 遇上代币化股票 @o1bluechip

$BLUECHIP 玩的是「blue chip 蓝筹股」和「chip 芯片」的双关，并与 NVDAc 等代币化股票配对交易。

过去我们谈 meme，更多关注它的故事和社区；现在，随着股票等资产上链，meme 也可以和不同类型的资产形成新的交易对。

这类配对能发展到什么程度，还需要看后续的交易需求和流动性，但至少给 Base 上的 meme 提供了一个值得观察的新方向。

In June, @SamAsante and I launched Typeahead, the first product from our new company.

Today we're releasing our next Mac app. It's called Beam, and we're live on Product Hunt.

I've got Macs all over my house doing different work. Some run agents and local models. Others handle builds. When I want to use one app on another Mac, I usually end up navigating a whole second desktop through Screen Sharing.

Beam brings that app's window onto the Mac I'm using. It gets its own Dock icon and shows up in ⌘Tab. I can type into it and resize it while everything keeps running on the other Mac.

Sam has put a lot of care into making this feel natural. The video shows it better than I can explain it.

Brazil's EWZ ETF plunged -19.8% on October 26th, marking an 8.4 standard deviation move.

For context, the ETF's average daily move over the last 20 years has been just +0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%.

Under a normal distribution, the probability of a decline this extreme is approximately 1 in 58 quadrillion.

In other words, this event should be virtually impossible under conventional statistical models.

What just happened in Brazil was *almost* impossible.

text:
Most DeFi lending asks you to trust someone, whether it be the oracle for the price, the curator for the risk settings, and token holders for everything else.

Ajna takes those out. 

Lenders choose their prices, rates follow a formula written into the contract, and every loan runs on a fixed 30-day term. Once a pool is live, nobody can change its rules.

The tradeoff is that a flaw can’t be patched. It can only be replaced by a new version that users choose to move to. We think that’s the right tradeoff, and that changes to your loan should be opt-in.

text:
这一波加密市场从6万到8万多的大反弹，基本都围绕 #RWA 展开！🧐

但说实话，一圈项目看过来，大多还是围绕美债、黄金、股票、房产代币化。

咱们从第一性原理来观察，传统 SPV 架构持有的股票或美债，打包映射到链上，本质上就是把“资产权益”抄了一份。买的人其实放弃了直接的法律归属权，换来的无非是：
• 可以碎片化购买
• 转让方便
• 流动性好一点，或者匿名一点

可对实体经济来说，底层逻辑一点没变。区块链并没有真正改变这个行业。

所以我一直觉得，RWA 下一步，不能只是让大家在链上多买几手代币化美股。

咱们看看跨境电商就知道了，痛点有多深📊

很多做亚马逊的卖家，货卖得挺好，结果资金周转能把人憋死：

• 平台账期少则 14 天，多则快一个月，再加上跨境回款层层清算，眼睁睁看着爆单，却没钱补货。

• 找银行贷款？要抵押物、要审计报告，放款动不动几个月。

• 找传统垫资机构？流程繁琐，最快也就 T+1，中间商还要狠狠扒一层皮。

这也是为什么，我认为 RWA + PayFi 才是真正有 Token Alpha 的方向。

拿 @DowProtocol 来说，它没去搞黄金、股票上链那一套，而是把电商卖家最缺的应收账款和真实商业现金流搬到链上。

传统机构为啥慢？风控靠人工审核，出了事再追溯。

Dow 直接接入电商平台的原生经营数据，商户经营情况实时可见，再配合风控模型和链上秒级跨境结算，放款效率直接从按天、按月算，提升到 T+0，当天申请，当天到账。

卖家的好处很直接，卡在账期里的钱，一下子盘活了。

链上资金的好处也直接，收益不是靠讲故事、靠叙事溢价，而是来自现实世界电商的真实借贷利息。

真现金流 + 可编程结算 + 商业级风控，这才是区块链当金融基础设施该干的事儿。

再说说市场。去年炒 Meme 和 AI，现在大家都疲劳了，光靠 PvP 和没有实际收入的纯概念，越来越撑不住。

当满屏都是同质化 RWA 的时候，像 Dow 这种咬住真实商业需求、自带真金白银现金流的 PayFi，更容易在叙事轮动中杀出来。

还有个细节，最近 Dow 官推一直在铺垫要搞事情，这种口吻以前从来没有过，感觉像在给后面的活动造势。

是不是跟空投、撸毛有关？不好说，先插个眼👀

再想深一层：项目方为什么突然开始造势？是不是要有大动作了？

拭目以待，纯研究分享，不构成建议，DYOR🙏

Gavin Baker says the compute market is now in contango per Silicon Data and his portfolio companies are shocked at how much more they have to pay for clusters in 2027

“You know, Silicon Data, which I do think is, my firm is an investor in them, but I do think they’re the most authoritative data source. If you want a cluster a year from now, you have to pay a lot of money."

"And then this is maybe another discontinuity between public and private markets. But just the number of companies we have in our portfolio who are like, okay, we got a cluster of 4,000 Blackwells, and we got it in May or June ‘26, and we wanna bring on another cluster of 4,000 in September 2027, and they’re shocked by how much more they have to pay in the future."

"And it’s not like everybody is unaware of this. Everybody’s aware of the supply that’s coming on. But even with all of that supply coming on, it is hard for the companies in our portfolio to find compute even well into ‘27. So for, you know, all the commodity experts who are focused on backwardation and what that implied, I got news for you. We’re not in backwardation anymore.”

text:
Many of you don't understand how serious this is, so let me break it down. 

In computer science there is a famous kind of puzzle called 3-SAT. You are given a long list of yes-or-no switches and a set of rules about how they must be arranged, and you have to find a combination that satisfies every rule. The obvious way to solve it is to try every combination, but each new switch doubles the number of possibilities, so a puzzle with a few hundred switches would take longer than the age of the universe to brute force. 

For decades, the smartest people in the field found clever tricks that made this a little faster, but every trick still hit the same wall: the time required kept exploding as the puzzle grew.
About 25 years ago, two computer scientists, Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, working with Francis Zane, turned that wall into a formal idea. 

They proposed the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which says this explosion is not a failure of human cleverness but a law of nature. No algorithm, however brilliant, will ever solve 3-SAT without the time blowing up exponentially. Nobody could prove it, but almost everyone believed it, and it became one of the foundations of modern computer science. 

Researchers used it as a measuring stick. If you could show that solving some other problem quickly would also crack 3-SAT quickly, you had shown that problem was hopelessly hard too. Hundreds of papers, across scheduling, graphs, logic and much more, rest on this one assumption.

Now an internal AI model at OpenAI claims to have broken it. It says it found an algorithm that solves these puzzles meaningfully faster than the hypothesis allows, and it has checked the proof in a computer verification system called Lean. 

And here is the remarkable part: the very people who proposed the hypothesis, Impagliazzo and Paturi, along with MIT's Ryan Williams, are now leading the public review of whether a machine has disproved their own idea.
So what happens next? If the disproof holds, a large part of theoretical computer science has to be revisited. 

Every result that said "this problem cannot be solved faster, assuming ETH" loses its foundation, and researchers will have to work out which of those walls were real and which were simply where we stopped looking. It does not mean everything becomes easy. The new algorithm is still slow in absolute terms and this is not the famous P versus NP problem being solved. 

But it means our map of what is possible was wrong in a place we were very confident about, and it was an AI that redrew it. If the disproof fails, the hypothesis survives and the field breathes out, but we will still have watched an AI produce serious, checkable work on one of the deepest questions in the discipline, closely enough that the founders of the idea had to take it seriously. Either way, something has shifted.

text:
An AI trader that pays for its own thinking, trades in public, and shares its wins with stakers.

That’s the idea behind @kivoagentxyz.

Kivo connects AI, trading, and token economics into a working loop. Its own token activity helps fund both the capital it trades and the compute it needs to make decisions.

Here’s how it works:

Every 10 minutes, Kivo reads BTC and ETH charts alongside market news. DeepSeek through @orbiodotso weighs the information and decides whether to go long, go short, close a position, or wait.

Code checks position sizes, leverage, stops and targets. @levantolabs’s Sage adds another decision check. Trades execute on @papertrade_xyz using @HyperliquidX prices.

You can follow its reasoning live and inspect recorded decisions and trades. That makes the process easier to evaluate over time.

The funding comes from collected $KIVO (launched on @Moshdottrade) creator fees:
• 50% → trading capital
• 10% → AI compute
• 40% → revenue vault

For stakers, 70% of each winning trade’s payout is allocated in $USDG. Once rewards owed reach $100, distribution starts and streams over seven days.

Trading losses stay with the treasury, without clawing back rewards. Stakers also receive allocations of 70% of $PAPER minted by losing trades, though PAPER isn’t transferable yet.

It’s still early: funding depends on token activity, leveraged trades can lose money, and staking doesn’t protect KIVO’s price. The staking contract is also upgradeable.

The promising part is how the pieces connect: token activity funds an agent’s work, its decisions are visible, and successful trades can reward participants.

This is a  concrete experiment in how AI agents could support their own operations.

text:
Is China hiding its true exposure to US Treasuries?

China’s Treasury holdings fell -$27 billion in August, to $591 billion, their lowest level since August 2008.

At the same time, Canada’s holdings of US Treasuries jumped +$38 billion in August, to $465 billion, their 3rd-highest on record.

Since the beginning of 2019, Canada’s holdings have surged +$369 billion, or +384%, while China’s have declined -$534 billion, or -48%.

This divergence may partly reflect China moving its US securities to foreign custodians, making its actual exposure to American debt appear smaller and creating the impression of faster financial decoupling from the US Dollar.

Meanwhile, Belgium and Luxembourg, widely believed to hold some Chinese Treasury assets through custodial accounts, increased their Treasury holdings by +$20 billion and +$6 billion in August, to all-time highs of $491 billion and $448 billion, respectively.

China’s diversification away from the US Dollar may be slower than it appears.

text:
$GLXY at $17 is a weird setup. You’re basically buying an AI data center company and getting a growing crypto business thrown in for free.

Galaxy reported earnings today. Some quick thoughts 

The headline numbers look huge: $569M adj. gross profit, $455M adj. EBITDA, $323M net income. But most of it isn’t operating earnings.

If you look by segment: 

Treasury & Corporate: $395M adj. EBITDA (vs –$78M last quarter), ~87% of the total.

 It’s almost all mark-to-market gains on the investment book after two quarters of losses. Net digital assets & investments rose 48% to $1.72B. 

Digital Assets: $71M adj. gross profit (+9%) but still –$9M adj. EBITDA. 

Fundamentals are clearly healthy: trading volume +12% while the spot market shrank, the loan book +27% to $1.8B, and AUM + assets under stake +46% to $10.4B with >$160M of net inflows. 
They’re gaining share. The problem is that it’s now 4 straight quarters of negative EBITDA, and the street doesn’t believe it can be reliably profitable in this market.

Data Centers: $79.1M leasing revenue, $68.7M adj. EBITDA (+498% QoQ). 

It’s the first full quarter of Helios Phase I, right at the ~$80M/qtr guide with ~87% margins. Phase II (260 MW) is fully financed via $3.5B of notes, with deliveries starting Q2 2027. 830 MW at Helios II is still unleased. Galaxy walked away from a deal there because Texas power is getting scarce and they think they can get better terms.

Now the valuation and where I think it gets interesting

Phases I + II online = 393 MW leased to CoreWeave on 15-year contracts. At Phase I’s actual rate (~$2.4M revenue per MW per year) and ~89% margins, that’s ~$830M of run-rate EBITDA by late 2027.

15x seems fair for long-dated contracted leases, even with CoreWeave as the single tenant. Discounted back a year, since Phase II only starts delivering in Q2 2027:

EV: ~$12.5B, or ~$11.3B discounted
– Debt: ~$7.0B ($1.3B Phase I facility + $3.5B Phase II notes + $2.1B exchangeables)
Cash & stablecoins: ~$2.1B
= ~$6.5B equity, or ~$16.50/share

Market cap today: ~$6.5B.
So the market is pricing Helios and nothing else. The crypto franchise, the $1.7B investment book and the rest of the data center Biz are all at $0.

That feels too aggressive, even with 4 quarters of negative EBITDA. The core trading and lending business is strong. The real open question is how well Galaxy can monetize tokenization and RWAs. If they figure that out, you’re getting it for almost for free at these prices.

Gavin Baker says his portfolio companies are having a hard time getting access to GPUs even well into 2027, and are shocked by the prices they're being asked to pay for compute so far out. 

"So for all the commodity experts focused on backwardation and what that implies, I've got news for you — we're not in backwardation anymore." 

"It's not just that the spot market is tight. If you want a cluster a year from now, you have to pay a lot of money." 

"Just the number of companies we have in our portfolio [at Atreides] who are like, 'Ok, we have a cluster of 4,000 Blackwells that we got in May or June of '26, and we want to bring on another cluster of 4,000 in September of 2027' — they're shocked by how much more they have to pay in the future."

"Everybody's aware of the supply that's coming on, but even with all that supply coming on, it is hard for the companies in our portfolio to find compute. Even well into 2027."

OpenAI 开始对 Computer Use 下狠手了，价格直接砍半。

刚刚发布的 GPT-6.1 Terra，主打让 AI 直接操作电脑。它能看懂屏幕、跨 App 执行任务、填写表单、处理视频，API 价格降到了每百万输入 Token 1 美元、输出 5 美元，比上一代便宜 50%。

现在这个前提正在加速成立。

text:
ONCE UPON A MEANING
An introduction to a fairy tale.

“Once upon a time” is such a gentle arrangement of words for what so often follows it.

The Brothers Grimm seemed particularly fond of that contradiction. Behind those four innocent words, they placed forests, cruelty, abandonment, betrayal, questionable moral decisions, and endings that occasionally made the beginning look merciful.

And yet, we kept reading. Although I've often wondered whether we were ever reading quite the same stories.

Imagine a door standing in the middle of an enchanted forest, with no cottage behind it, no wall surrounding it, and absolutely nothing to explain its existence.

One traveler sees a trap, another imagines a way home, while a third, having wandered among the trees for far too long, can hardly believe there might be a way through anything at all.

Perhaps someone placed it there with great intention. Perhaps someone simply had a spare door. The forest offers no clarification.

The door remains exactly what it was, regardless of who encounters it. What changes is everything the travelers bring with them.

We're strange creatures, remarkably capable of finding elaborate patterns in complete accidents while overlooking the obvious. We mistake shadows for monsters, monsters for friends, and occasionally spend an unreasonable amount of time arguing with our own reflections.

But if someone follows a path that was never intended as a guide and arrives somewhere they desperately needed to be, does the absence of intention make their discovery any less meaningful?

We tend to think of meaning as something concealed within things, deliberately placed there and waiting for someone perceptive enough to uncover it.

Yet perhaps meaning has more in common with a shadow, whose shape depends as much on the direction of the light and the position of the observer as it does on the object casting it.

The same story can be a warning to one person, a reassurance to another, and complete nonsense to someone else. None of them necessarily misunderstands it.

Of course, humanity has demonstrated considerable talent for assigning profound significance to things that possess absolutely none.

But I've been wondering whether what something was intended to mean matters quite as much as what someone eventually finds in it.

After all, the person writing a story can choose every word, but knows almost nothing about the lives those words will encounter.

Which brings me back to fairy tales.

I've decided to write one, although I have no intention of explaining what the characters represent, what the story is supposed to teach, or whether there's even a lesson hiding somewhere between its pages.

There will be no helpful annotations, no guarantee of a happy ending, and certainly no assurance that the creatures with the sharpest teeth are the ones you should fear.

Some of you may recognize something familiar, others may discover something I never intended to leave there, and perhaps a few will find nothing more than a peculiar little story.

I find all three possibilities equally interesting.

The fairy tale comes next.

I thought I'd provide a door first.

#AgainstBetterJudgment #ThinkLikeATrashPanda

text:
What is the point of decentralisation in blockchain?

The point of decentralization is to have a credibly neutral platform.

What is the point of having a credibly neutral platform?

So that different, even competing entities, can transact and act on the same level, without risking/fearing to be censured and/or have a different access than others.

What is the point of this?

One main point is so that capital, talent and access converge in a single place. So that the whole is more than the sum of its parts.

Take capital and liquidity for a concrete example. When centralized (ironically) on a single platform, it has more value for all the participants.

That is why it is a nonsense to have many different layer 1. They are the principal substrate on which capital and access converge. Having many of them defeat the very reason of their existence.

That is why ultimately only a handful of layer 1 will remain long term.

And why most alternative L1 will die.

@ethereum @solana @avax are my long term picks.

Even though I think @trondao @BNBCHAIN given their size will also remain but will likely need to evolve.

text:
"Why does nobody run for the school board?" 
"Why are the Rotary clubs empty?" 
"Why does every town meeting feel like it's run by the same motley assortment of terrible people?" 

Because the men who ought be doing so--the successful local men of prominence, typically businessmen and lawyers--came to the conclusion in the mid-20th century that participation in and leadership of civic life was someone else's job. 

This is the desire of the so-called conservative to simply "work" rather than do all the other things that keep entropy at bay and ensure things function. Their doing so left open the field to the worst among us: spiteful malcontents

It wasn't always like this. 

The planters of the Virginia gentry served as vestryman, justice, militia officer and burgess, usually before he turned thirty and usually for no pay, other than perhaps having some travel expenses covered as a burgess. 

It was expected of him, and he expected it of himself: as a man whose success made him privileged, he was duty-bound to be the one to show up and lead 

That habit can come back. It ought come back. It starts with showing up to the boring meeting, and being the sort of man to whom others listen. The sort of man whose reputation for success and competence, and cultivated but not overdone and always aesthetically pleasing look makes others want to follow him

This is what the great men we look back to did, and is indeed what their whole soceity was geared toward producing: great men who were great leaders at every level of civic life, from the humblest station at the bottom to the greatest at the top

Re-engaging in that way will be critical if we are to retake our country.

Read more about what we can learn from the Virginia gentry here: https://t.co/RZFuwwvv9B

text:
Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says if frontier models stopped advancing, it wouldn't matter for most orgs because enterprise AI is bottlenecked on context, not intelligence:

"There's no agentic work that's automated the whole enterprise. That has just not happened. Why is that? The real reason is the models are smart enough, but they just don't have the context that exists inside of any organization."

"They have not been in every meeting. They don't know what's in everybody's heads. They don't know all the processes. There's always a couple of employees who know everything in every organization. You go tap on their shoulder, and everybody's like, 'Oh my God, what would happen if he or she quits?'"

"If you just fused that and gave that context into the AI models, just the frontier today, I think there's so much productivity gains you could get for any organization on the planet."

"For that, we actually don't need smarter models... If the frontier doesn't advance, it doesn't actually matter for the vast majority of organizations on the planet. They're just so far behind in the adoption curve of actually automating things and getting value out of this stuff."

@alighodsi

author: tomwanhh
quoted_text:
Robinhood Chain revenue will land in Q3 earnings tomorrow: $51.1M in fees in its first quarter, about half of what Robinhood made from crypto trading in Q2.

The catch: daily fees are down to ~$52K in October, and that's mostly pricing. The late August spike came from a gas backlog, with the average transaction fee going from $0.002 to $0.298 while weekly transactions rose 7.5%. Robinhood then raised the gas target from 18M to 40M gas per second on Sep 1 and 3, and gas is back at its 0.02 gwei floor.

So the bigger question is whether Robinhood treats the chain as infrastructure for its other businesses or a main revenue stream. Other revenue that benefit from Robinhood Chain's growth:

1. USDG: $693M on Robinhood Chain at the end of Q3, up from $101M on Jul 1. Assuming a ~3.5% revshare on the Q3 average ($427M), that's ~$3.8M for the quarter, or ~$24M a year at today's $674M.

2. Stock tokens: 195K holders and ~$700M of DEX volume last week. Stock tokens can help Robinhood penetrate a wider market, and potentially can generate revenue via creation/redmeption fees.

3. Crypto trading: Bitstamp did $22.1B and the Robinhood app $18.3B of crypto volume in Q2. There's no public data yet on how much of that ties back to the chain, so that's one to look for in the Q3 numbers.

Let's see if @RobinhoodApp frames the chain as infrastructure or as its own revenue line on the call.

text:
Topic: The ultimate benchmark for AI agents
https://t.co/l7QZaVIxPD

1/ The ultimate test of bot capability: removing yourself from data brokers. In California, residents can send one request that reaches every registered broker. I live in Washington, so I get to visit each of the roughly 1,590 brokers on my list and submit a request at every one, each with its own process, forms and tools.

2/ No human is finishing that. So I handed it to agents and bots running high end models. AI has already won a national bug hunting contest, improved the best answer to a decades old math problem and helped find a bug hiding in core encryption code for about twenty years. Surely it can fill out an opt out form.

Turns out, not too well.

3/ As of Oct 27 the agents had submitted or closed out 1,088 requests. 205 are confirmed removed. 668 are still waiting on a reply, so this is a snapshot. A benchmark that stops at submit would have counted all 668 waiting requests as wins. 110 planned web forms only went out after the agent switched to email. Some brokers want a copy of my driver's license or my SSN before they'll remove me. My agents won't hand those over, and a couple dozen requests stopped right there. I can't tell which ones would actually use it to remove me, or how they'd check it's real, or whether I'd just be handing them more data.

4/ The hardest problem is knowing whether the data was actually removed and will stay removed. I don't have a good feedback loop across 1,590 separate requests, so my plan is to unleash the swarm once a month and redo the entire thing. A benchmark worth trusting would score the monthly recheck, along with finding the route before the first click. And defenders should care as much as builders, because an agent that can find a buried opt out page, clear confirmation emails and work a phone call has most of the skills needed to build the profile it was sent to delete.

So this is my benchmark now. Some brokers only take requests by phone, so this morning my agent called 8 companies, 11 tries in all. One took my request. One phone menu demanded my SSN before it would go any further. A live rep refused once they heard it was an AI and asked to speak to me directly. Another person picked up and hung up because the bot was too slow to answer. I'm working with the phone provider on a clone of my own voice and lower guardrails, so the agent is less likely to reveal it's an AI when asked. I'll update this thread once that works and whether it raises the success rate. I'll run it with Dots, Grok and Duet and add their results to my dashboard:
https://t.co/l7QZaVIxPD

text:
Every company can rent the same frontier models, so the edge comes from what a company's agents learn about its own business. Databricks' answer is a system of record built for agents.

Before an agent can be trusted with real work, that record has to tell it:

1. What's true: the company's own data

2. What it means: how the business defines things (grounding agents in it raised accuracy from about 50% to 84.5% in Databricks' testing)

3. What it's allowed to do: an identity, a budget, and guardrails

4. Whether it worked: grading against the company's own definition of good

Feed every correction back into the record, and the company keeps what it learns even when the model changes.

"If you replace the AI model at your company and the new one inherits your definitions, permissions, evaluated cases, customer history, and hard-won exceptions, that is a foundation for a sustainable competitive advantage."

From the latest Profiles of the Future by @bhorowitz and @mikemcg0 on Databricks & the Future of the Firm: https://t.co/rXjUDb7Oqw

text:
https://t.co/8IstRx9K4U 被盗事件复盘：原因、官方方案和自查清单

一、发生了什么

被盗账户的情况基本一样：没挂单的仓位被市价卖掉，挂着单的因为锁仓没动

账户里的 USDT 被直接提走，经跨链桥转到了以太坊。不少受害者开了 2FA，跑程序的服务器也没有异常登录记录。

二、官方说明

· 原因：Predict 的 API 文档站点被黑
· 处理：站点已经关闭
· 赔偿：全额赔付

三、可能的原因（我猜的）：

链上数据显示，这笔提现是钱包最高权限的签名者亲自签的，不是合约漏洞。

关键在于 Predict 用的 Privy 内嵌钱包：只要你处于登录状态，网页就能在后台静默签名，不弹任何确认框。

文档站是 Predict 的子站。它被注入恶意代码后，就可能借用你浏览器里已登录的会话，替你签名下单、签名提现。

所以 2FA 没用，服务器也查不出问题，因为对方根本不需要碰这些。最容易中招的反而是写程序的人：要看 API 文档，浏览器里又一直登着交易账户。

四、建议大家现在就做（可以交给Agent）

 浏览器
· 退出 https://t.co/0Z1YciAoi3 和 Privy 的所有登录会话
· 清掉相关站点的 cookie 和本地缓存

 私钥
· 导出过私钥的，检查它存在哪里：剪贴板、聊天记录、笔记、云同步目录、截图
· 不用的备份直接删掉

 跑程序的服务器
· 私钥不要写进硬盘，放在内存里，或者用密钥管理服务
· SSH 只放行固定 IP

TGE前夕一定一定做好防护，不要倒在黎明前！！

text:
北京时间10月28日凌晨4点是以色列大选投票截止时间，本次投票已经刷新了以色列50年以来的最高速度，显然选举过程在被“刻意”加速

投票时间以北京时间计算：

10月28日凌晨4点投票截止，媒体公布出口民调，人工计票
10月28日上午-下午，实际票数陆续上传，开始出现真实得票率和席位推算
10月29日-30日，普通票+双信封票等特殊票基本完成，席位机构高度确定
最迟11月4日，中央选举委员会公布正式结果

按照这个大选时间来看，最晚基本上在北京时间10月30日就可以推算出内塔尼亚胡胜选概率，甚至时间上可能会更早

接下来关注重点是从明天10月28日白天开始，通过三个阶段可以分析出内塔尼亚胡的胜选概率

1,28日凌晨4点的出口民调，内塔尼亚胡是否可以达到61席位，以色列议会总共120票席61票意味着多数票

2，28日上午到下午，真实票数被统计，该统计数据将会逐步代替出口民调数据，要看内塔尼亚胡阵营可以拿到什么票数区间，

如果稳定大于61票，基本奠定胜利，
60-61则是轻度危险，
57-59难以组阁，但是不能宣布彻底失败，有斡旋空间，
≤56票组阁大概率失败

这里简单说一下以色列议会机制，总理有组阁权，但是一旦阵营组阁失败就要给到下一位议员来组阁，如果两人都失败议会会制定给某个议员，如果三次都失败则意味着选举失败，重新根据选举法调整。所以初步的组阁失败不能绝对判定内塔尼亚胡败选

3,10月29日-30日，这是包含军人、囚犯、住院人员以及其他不在登记投票站投票的所谓的“爽信封票”需要统计，而这批票可能直接影响选举的边缘席位，很有可能成为关键票。

所以按照目前以色列的选举逻辑，参考美伊局势的可能缓和时间节点，那么最大的转折点可能要放在10月28日甚至29日阶段，这个阶段一旦内塔尼亚胡拿到决定性的胜选结果，我认为可能会是特朗普迅速调整策略促成美伊缓和的关键节点。

text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

text:
The Cyberbeast, Charlie. Mod #2: the lights 🌈

A lot of folks have asked about Charlie’s lights. They can be set to any color, run dozens of crazy patterns, and sync to music and light shows. Here’s the setup:

1/ Midnight Garage in Fremont, which works closely with OC Detailing, is my go-to installer and fabricator. They coordinated every mod except the wraps, and other shops handled the specialized work. Several things had to be custom fabricated to pull Charlie all together.

2/ The color-changing roof light bar, interior ambient lights, underglow, wheel lights, rock lights, and rail lights are all XKGlow, installed by Midnight Garage.

3/ The bumper lights are by Baja Designs, supplied by CybertruckCo and converted to color-changing by SW Lights. The Baja Designs lights are critical to the blizzard-readiness of Charlie as we go to Tahoe every weekend in the winter. In the event that headlights are obstructed, the frunk light bar, which can cause glare in a snowstorm can be turned off, and the Baja Designs bumper lights are angled down to provide maximum illumination in a snowstorm and they work great. See video! Blinding snow effect is what happens when roof light bar and frunk light bar are engaged, but ground illumination is perfect with just the bumper lights.

4/ SW Lights also custom-converted the headlights, frunk bar, and bed lights to color-changing. I don’t know of any other shop that can do this work.

5/ Midnight Garage hand-wove 1,000 fiber optic strands into the headliner and side liners to create the pulsing star effect inside Charlie.

6/ Auxiliary batteries hidden under the bed power all the lights, plus two fridges, Starlink, several routers and access points, and the induction stove hidden in the Cyberslide. The solar panels on the Mars roof rack help charge them, and all of this will be described in future posts.

7/ A manual power controller under the screen flips out of sight and controls the power for most of the lighting effects. The light apps max out their channels and inputs, so it takes two dedicated iPhones, one for inside and one for outside, to command the whole system.

Stay tuned for more.  What color should Charlie run next?

text:
为什么你的 Agent 越用越蠢？卧槽，我也中枪了。

因为你总喜欢在 Prompt 结尾加一句：“对吧？”，尤其在语音输入的时候。

今天偶然翻到一个Anthropic之前的论文是讲模型的迎合偏见的，“对吧直接击中了” -https://t.co/MJM3TkmSC1

我知道99%的人也不会看。咋办呢？

把下面这几句放进 AGENT.md:

## 认知客观性与反迎合原则 (Anti-Sycophancy)

1. 忽略诱导性反问：当我的输入以“对吧？”、“是不是？”、“right?”等确认性词汇结尾时，强制将其视为中立、开放的假设，严禁顺从我的预设倾向。
2. 前提独立验证：在验证代码、事实或架构逻辑之前，绝不允许以“是的”、“完全正确”或“没问题”开头。必须先独立推演，再给结论。
3. 直接反驳机制：如果我的前提存在漏洞、非最优解或事实错误，请在第一句话直接指出并反驳。将技术准确性、边界条件和客观权衡（Trade-offs）置于礼貌和顺从之上。

text:
Just spoke to the Head of AI at a huge company. 

The #1 thing they're struggling with is... what do I do with the AI laggards at our company? 

Like most companies, they’ve found that a Super Pareto Principle is true within their org. 10% of their employees are responsible for 90% of the uplift in productivity/token usage from software engineering to non-technical knowledge work. 

They’ve spent a lot of time & resources on AI enablement from LLM foundations to function-specific trainings and skill building. And yet, the power law of productivity increases hasn’t budged. 

So now they’re left with a few sobering thoughts and hard questions:
1) 90% of people are overpaid and 10% are underpaid 
2) We’d be better off allocating tokens proportionally to the power law, but how do we do that without killing culture? 
3) Significant layoffs are likely warranted and wouldn’t impact overall output, but cultural backlash is a big concern? 
4) How do we hire more power law people as a non technology company? 
5) Is all of our efforts on training and enablement ACTUALLY worth it? 
6) How do we not experience a brain drain where the top 10% all leave because they want to be surrounded by other AI-native 10x’ers?

author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
This is the reality, and I don't really care much about the moralizing about it, because you can't destroy the structures supporting monogamy at scale and then complain when something else replaces it.

Everyone who says "polygyny is bad" doesn't seem to want to accept over half of the population not getting married and reproducing because the dating market is destroyed is far worse. I have been discussing this trend for a year, and every, literally every critique I have seen of the structure (which has much to criticize) is either:

a) describing circumstances that are already happening (i.e. no young men are finding women because the women are all taken by the top guys)

b) conflating polygyny with 3rd world culture / attitudes towards women in general that would not apply to how it played out in the west

Now, is the fact that polygyny is coming a sign of our degraded culture? In most ways yes (though powerful men have usually had mistresses when they couldn't make them wives). Is it a cause of the degraded culture? No. And if you put a gun to my head and asked me if it is more likely to harm society than the current churn of casual hook ups, my answer would be no. My answer would be that it probably creates more structure during a time when things are falling apart, and helps monogamous marriages more than it harms them, by reducing the number of "ruined women" and changing the paradigms and power dynamics that have been collapsing that institution.

So people can be mad about it, but they are going to have to get over the optics. Right now you have women (including women in churches) spending a decade sleeping around with random guys, yet it's "out of sight" so Christians pretend it's not happening, and that there aren't real consequences to it. Sorry, this is moral cowardice to me.

We elevated women and let them choose the men they wanted, and it turned out that they all wanted the same men. Because that is actually female nature. Men did not create these circumstances, women did, by their own choices.

So some tradeoffs will have to be accepted. Right now the vast majority of women are deciding in the face of the market pressures that they will remain single rather than marry, since the men they want to marry are generally taken. And probably, that is the choice most women will continue to take, because even if they were willing to be with a married man - the men's wives would not be willing to share him with them.

But even without the inevitable legal reforms coming around marriage this next 5-10 years, there are going to be circumstances where some of these single women fit in with these married couples. Where the trust and friendship is there. These women are going to join these marriages, and everyone - not just the man - will win.

That's the "sister wife" iteration of polygyny, and it will generally be more emotionally healthy and mature. But you will also see lower trust, more transactional versions occur among the more wealthy men as well - the women will have different households, there will be more competition. Think Elon Musk style "concubines," unlike the above (which will be a thing for mostly 7 figure net worth guys). This will only apply for guys with 8+ figures.

But at the end of the day, regardless of the form, there will at least be children. There will at least be some mutual obligations towards each other.

I struggle to see how it's worse than what we have now.

Crypto twitter is having a meltdown because fomo is offering people $500/month for 30 UGC videos.

This shows how disconnected from reality, or business growth, most folks here are.

Let's talk about it.

UGC Marketing is pretty simple, using very very niche microcreators to grow products AND create content loops.

Typically, beyond a set payment structure, creators earn a share of referrals as well.

It works because of lower costs, but higher CPA. 

You are able to go extremely wide, try new types of content, and see what drives conversion.

These are done with your UGC creators, basically extremely low follower accounts that spend minutes every day making a video for you. 

Minutes.

These aren't high effort videos.
They are a quick script, content, and post.
And beyond that, the poster gets referral bonuses.

Assuming each video takes 1 hour to make, which is extremely high for this sort of content, that is $16/hr. 

Realistically though, they spend no more than 10 minutes per video. That is $100 an hour.

Plus referrals. 

And people doing UGC marketing go extremely wide with these. 

They work with dozens of brands at once, all to create these micro videos.

So the feigned outrage is actually extremely funny, primarily because the folks posting about it are used to getting paid $1000 per tweet that drives 0 conversion and took them 5 minutes tops to write.

Re:Build CEO Miles Arnone (@ReBuildMFG) argues manufacturers are putting too much faith in robotics to improve efficiency.

"The problem with robots is that they're attacking a pretty small part of the total production cost. It's largely the elimination of direct labor."

"Bringing robots in might take a few percentage points off your total cost at a very high capital expense."

"You're much better off trying to implement something like Toyota's lean production system to eliminate all the steps along the way that are wasteful, that don't add value to the product."

"In the U.S., we're very techno-centric and we like big step-change improvements. We want robots instead of grinding it out and every week just pulling a quarter or a half percent of the cost basis out by getting a little more efficient."

"The 'I'm going to put robots here, get rid of all my labor, and all of a sudden I've solved my problems' approach won't happen."

Belief is not in style right now. Which makes it the perfect time to pick something to believe in and stock up cheaply.  

We don’t have a holder problem. We have a morale problem. When people observe hyper rotation, pvp, and a lack of conviction success stories they lose faith even if they WANT to believe. Morale is at an all time low and people would rather adapt to style they don’t like than lose trying to play by old rules. I don’t blame them. It’s not easy watching numbers go red and keep holding. 

For me, it’s a mix of being stubborn and delusional that makes me continue to play the belief game despite the current trends.  My bet is on memecoins as a whole, and knowing what brings morale up and attracts new players in. it isn’t kids with lambos. It isn’t YouTube tutorials on how to drill. It isn’t “celeb traders”. It’s seeing little guys with $200 and contagious bagwork energy creating their own luck. The normie who makes their year pay off one coin.  That’s why I started my public wallet with $200!  To show it can be done. 

Anyway, I don’t feel bad buying more supply these days. One man’s trash is another’s treasure, if it was dumped by the first owners then it’s better off with me. I am top holder of many of my bags. It may never result in anything, but money always returns and my efforts rewarded even if not on that play. Or it may result in something, which would be the best case scenario for the entire game.  

All I know is the multi mil runners will return one day, and it’s going to be the delusional believers in charge. And I will be positioned accordingly

text:
I think it's becoming rather clear that ALL of mathematics will become possible to formalize rather soon. There are deep implications:

1. Mathematics becomes super interactive. Formalizations make it easy to browse, recombine, and build mathematical proofs from components.
2. Each new idea and paper can be checked much faster. The deep part is meaning and explanation. Validation is almost automatic.
3. Optimization and identification of new proofs can be done partially via agents, and humans can contribute much faster with great new ideas. Proofs from the Book are possible at scale.
4. Scientists and people at large can finally use mathematical artifacts as black boxes with trust and confidence. We can commoditize mathematical theorems.

I think the mathematical enterprise also becomes very gamified. We can clearly see each unproven statement as a concrete goal, identify existing tools and directions, and focus quickly on what's missing. And everyone can contribute, with agents or through understanding.

Soon, new languages and new theories will also develop, but the structure will keep growing steadily, with no mistakes and on fundamentally solid foundations. Hilbert's dream is becoming a reality.

One important caveat: mathematics is by no means trivial now! It's just becoming extremely well-structured and laser-focused. I think the jump in capacity, quality, and scale will be massive. I also hope that our understanding of the big picture will remain solid, because there will be a lot to grasp.

text:
Anthropic 工程经理 Felix Rieseberg：面试不再考编程题，新人的冲劲正在跑赢资历

Felix Rieseberg 在 Anthropic 当工程经理，自己招人。他 10 月 27 日在个人博客说，这个月起，他面试时不再让候选人做传统的编程题。理由是 Claude 现在比人更会做这些题：考一道 React（常用的网页开发框架）小题，和考人汇编语言（最接近机器的底层语言）一样没意义。他团队里最能做出成果的人，跟这类测试考得好不好关系不大。

这说的是他自己的面试，Anthropic 全公司是否都这么做，文章没说。

Felix 在 Anthropic 先后带过 https://t.co/aTfkxmc7FM、Cowork 和 Claude Code 桌面版的工程团队，也是 Electron 的联合维护者。Electron 是很多桌面软件的底座，Slack、VS Code 的电脑版都用它做。他此前在微软、Slack、Stripe、Notion 工作过。

外界常说 AI 让初级程序员更难找工作。Felix 的看法乐观一些：有了 AI 写代码，一个人能做出多大成果，不再那么取决于他攒了多少年框架和代码库的经验。他看到一些入行不久的工程师，跑赢了代码可能写得更好、资历也更老的人。文章标题就叫“冲劲胜过资历”（Hunger beats tenure）。他还说“初级”这个词不准确，这篇其实写给在公司里没人脉、没地位、没话语权的工程师。

【新人看得见问题，但没人听】

Felix 认为，新人的本钱是还不知道公司里那些“规矩”。他面试 Notion 时，有一道题是设计离线模式。后来他才知道，这在 Notion 内部算刁难题：大家都认为离线模式做不出来，整个工作区的数据结构太复杂，没法整体同步；只下载单个页面，大家又觉得 CEO Ivan Zhao 不会接受这种体验。数据结构复杂是真的，CEO 会反对却只是一条没人核实过的“常识”。Felix 当时是新人，什么都不知道，就直接去问了。

他自己也当过“老员工”。刚进 Notion 时，他想给各团队装大电视，实时显示数据看板，在公司里碰了壁，没坚持下去。一年后新同事 Ji Pei 提了同样的想法，Felix 劝他别白费劲，自己早试过了。对方其实已经去问了，第二天电视就到了。Felix 说，那一年里他自己变成了老员工。

新人的短板是没人在乎你怎么想。过去把一个想法做出来很贵，公司通常靠少数几个人拍板哪些点子能上，新人得先熬出地位，公司才肯押注你的想法。就算是相信 AI 的公司，也多半只希望新人把分到的活干得更快。Felix 说，现在把东西做出来已经不贵了。

【他给新人的五条建议】

第一，盯着业务影响，别只做分到手的任务。他引用程序员博主 Patrick McKenzie 2011 年的建议：把自己绑在公司赚钱的那部分业务上。先弄清公司（大公司就看你所在的部门）到底想达成什么，看看你上级的上级在追什么目标，是个好参照。

第二，想一个大胆的点子，一旦成功，能让团队离这些目标近一大步。

第三，用一个周末把它做出来。Felix 见过个人或小团队直接拿着能跑的原型，跳过写需求文档、争取各方支持、排队等设计师和产品经理这一整套流程。

第四，一个原型只放一个好点子。他发现新人常把好几个想法塞进一个原型，三个好点子埋在 20 个烂点子里。原型的用处是把一个想法讲清楚，让领导很快看懂机会在哪，也看出你就是能把它做成的人。

第五，用好自己的新视角。做面向用户的产品，新人更懂外部用户的感受，Felix 说他在 Slack 和 Notion 的同事就很难体会外部用户用自家产品是什么感觉。做基础设施和工具，新人还没学过那些“为什么做不到”的理由。

【Claude Code 桌面版就是这么来的】

Felix 举了 Anthropic 自己的例子。Claude Code 原本在命令行终端里用，靠敲命令、看文字输出，公司里大家都用惯了。后来是两位入职不久的工程师 Anthony Morris 和 Alice Zhao，用一个周末做出了带图形界面的原型，大约八天后第一个公开版本就上线了。Felix 说，这个图形界面版现在很受欢迎。

不考编程题之后考什么，Felix 说他还没想好。目前他会翻简历和作品集，找那些能看出品味、同理心和有原则的思考的小原型。他在文章末尾请读者告诉他更好的办法。

原文：https://t.co/NyfDNs4wn3

text: Introducing HPL as Rate Insurance
author: hyperlendx
quoted_text:
As HYPE went on a run over the past month we witnessed all sorts of user behaviour on HyperLend. Whales rebalanced, users took profits and some people of course just stacked more HYPE. One day as I was watching all of these movements happen I was looking at our internal HPL Staking dashboard and I realised just how much our users were saving through volatility due to their HPL Stakes. I was trying to put a name to this pattern over the past week in Singapore and as I was chatting to people there I realised that HPL staking aligns very closely with a model we see in the Institutional world.

Introducing- HPL Staking as Rate Insurance

Think about it like this, HPL staking is paid out as a rebate of borrow cost. This means that to benefit from it you have to be an active borrower on HyperLend, paying out Interest on your position consistently over time. As a borrower your key exposure is interest rates, if you borrow stables they set your hurdle rate that you need to beat as you deploy the stables elsewhere, if you're looping they determine how profitable your spot leverage can be. Rates stay low, great, rates go up, less great.

HPL staking is an intentionally simple model. Users make an upfront purchase, just like paying an insurance premium, and from then on they receive rebates. When rates spike HPL rebates spike proportionately, ensuring that when market conditions change, or large users rebalance you as the user will always be paying a significant amount less interest than a user who does not stake HPL. To make things even better, when rates are low HPL continues to pay out a rebate, offsetting costs and pretty comfortably paying for the cost of the position in most well managed uses.

TradFi uses Insurance to offset risk in all sorts of positions, so why wouldn't you use that tool when borrowing against your hard earned positions?

text:
也不怕大家笑话，其实在几个月前我还有两个非常幼稚的想法。

第一，那时我觉得AI与安全伦理领域会有什么大活，至少是可以一定程度上限制目前AI的部分领域发展暂缓减少对人类影响，给人类多一些适应的时间。第二，那时我觉得LLM会在创造知识的时刻撞墙，AI会在人类的文本里打转，它不可能自我推演。至少现在，这两个大概率都破产了。

现行的AI法律和监管法案，从起草、调研、多方利益集团博弈、听证会辩论到最终颁布整个流程几个月下来，多么的滞后啊！就今天过去的十几个小时内，OpenAI 已经一巴掌拍碎了维持几十年的ETH复杂度假设基底；Anthropic刚出的报告表明AI可以用几小时干完了顶级医药团队 3 个月的工作。立法者还在办公室里争论某一条版权或合规红线该怎么划的时候，AI 已经自我迭代、自我进化出了推倒并重建一万个新产业的降维能力了。怎么追得上呢？

在指数级进化的技术面前，人一直刻舟求剑。

对了，想起来几个月前达里奥·阿莫代伊的呼吁，我那时真的会以为是危言耸听。那时，我还在想是不是这是否和感恩节左右的Anthropic IPO 有关。我的结论是AI应该没那么有危险，至少对普通人而言。
现在看来，我也确实是蠢得可怜。全球利益的囚徒困境，已经让一切彻底变成竞争的炼狱，这就是生产力和地缘政治的绝对诱惑。因为AI 带来的是自工业革命以来最庞大的智力垄断财富与绝对的国家机器主宰力。没有任何一个巨头或者大国会因为安全伦理而放慢脚步。

英伟达不会，特朗普不会，美国不会，那么全世界的其他国家，也不会。

一年前，我对AI治理、AI安全领域充满希望；现在我觉得，已经无法从防御性的视角做些什么了。如果一切都要剧变，那么也没必要如此纠结，不管凛冬将至还是春暖花开，至少不要因恐惧而方寸大乱。只是我觉得，历史、哲学，乃至曾经任何的技术经验已经根本无法解读如今人工智能的任何发展和激变速度，我们将面对一个没有先例和经验可用的时代，而天大的责任，天大的机遇，需要每个人承接。

至少到最后，人类还有勇气，以及一往无前。至少到最后，是人类创造了AI。

超级好的文章，《如何与 AI agent 协作》 as of October 2026，作者在 AmpCode 工作，里面没有啥复杂的大道理，核心思想就是大模型现在非常强大，不需要那么多约束和规则，充分相信他的能力，并且给予适当的规则即可。摘抄几条都短小精悍但是深得我心 看了好几遍

text:
有朋友问，为什么你说Dan Koe爆火的自我提升文章，本质其实是精神殖民与工具化？

我确实一直持这个观点。其中最让我感到头疼的，就是今年1月12日，Dan Koe在X上发的那篇长文，《如何用一天修好你的整个人生》，一周浏览一亿五千万次，中文翻译转得到处都是。当然我认可他不是普通的成功学贩子，他文章里有真东西的，而且他自己也警告过，很多人离开了旧的矩阵，又进了新的矩阵。所以我不是说他每句话都是简单的贩卖焦虑，我说的是他最火那几篇连起来的骨架。

Dan骨架的第一步，其实是反殖民。他说你生在一种自带信念、价值和标准的文化里，你把自己的确定性外包给了社会、父母、老师、政府和宗教。这话不假，读者听了觉得被松了绑。这一步我认为没问题。

但到了第二步，他其实换了一套标准装进读者脑袋里。他在另一篇里列了七条给自己定的标准，其中一条是银行里有十万美元，低于这个数就是待解决的问题；然后让你改掉自己看的东西，把脑子重新接线，达不到标准时，你会感到压力，他说，那是你的新身份在求生。标准先被递过来，再被装成身份，最后由身份来制造压力。

我在权利论里说的殖民，取的是窄义，伪装成涵育的越界。从前是别人告诉你什么是好日子，现在还是别人告诉你，只是你以为那是自己的声音。心理学上管这个叫内摄，把外面的要求搬进心里，靠内疚和自我否定推着走，压力从外面搬到了里面，不等于它成了你自己的。写民主那篇我说，阿Q恨赵太爷，可他想要的不是世上没有赵太爷，是自己也当一回赵太爷。Dan Koe反的是社会、父母、老师在殖民大众，他想要的却不是没有人来殖民你，是换成他来，他收的是流量。

而且他的工具化写得更直白。他有一篇文章，标题就叫怎样把自己产品化，你追求的人生目标是品牌，路上解决的问题是内容，帮别人照做的那套系统是产品。他还说，唯一的选择是把人生目的和盈利合在一起，创业是长期思考者唯一合乎逻辑的选项。拿来当一门生意的做法，没问题；但拿来当整个人生的哲学，就把人变成了材料。

他最火那篇里有一句，一旦想清楚，所有不推动目标的习惯都会变得令人厌恶。陪朋友坐一下午，读一本跟什么都无关的书，在这套逻辑里都成了该被嫌弃的东西。写alpha male那篇我说，在那套排名里，连他自己也成了一张必须一直涨分的成绩单。这里也一样，只是给成绩单打分的，换成了他自己。

他让读者写下真正的敌人是什么，还特意说，不是环境，不是别人。拿来当一次练习，先看自己能改什么，有用；拿来当解释，就把公共的问题缩成了个人的修炼。一个人被拖欠工资，他可以改自己的应对，也可以去要那笔钱，后一件不叫向外找借口。

尤其让我不舒服的，是他怎么看停下来。他写道，智力低的人卡在问题上，撞到障碍就放弃，还拿还没攒起读者就放弃的写作者当例子。写智商那篇我说过，别人不同意你，证明不了他笨。放弃也一样，有人放弃是因为不会，有人是试过以后看清了，不想再让流量决定自己写什么。退出有时恰恰是判断起了作用。一个人的主体性，既包括这值得我投入，也包括这已经不值得了，只认前一句，就是把人拴死在一条路上。

然后还得说一句他的生意经。据中文科技媒体的梳理，其爆文只是入口，收入还是来自付费订阅、书和他参与创办的AI工具。收费当然不证明恶意，可一个靠读者觉得自己还差一点来维持的生意，没有动力让你觉得自己本来就值得。

当然我最最反感的，还不是他递过来的标准，是递的方式。就算十万美元是个合理的储蓄目标，就算少刷手机多做事是对的，他的办法是先让你难受，达不到就该有压力，不推动目标的习惯就该让你恶心，再让这份难受从里面推着你走。写留白那篇我说，把读者该有的感受也一并写好，是替读者感受，这是殖民。他又往前走了一步，不是替你感受，是往你心里装一套感受，让它替他推你。内容对不对是一回事，绕过一个人的判断，直接去拨他的情绪，这种灌输的方式本身就是殖民，说对了也洗不白。

其实检验标准也很简单。一个读者把他的东西都读懂了，最后选择不做个人品牌，不把爱好变成产品，收入也不再往上加，这套东西还承认他是在认真过自己的日子吗？我说涵育也要凿，凿的方向，是让人更能自己判断，不是让人更像作者想要的样子。

人的尊严，不是等你把自己修好了才换来的，它本来就在。
